What teams will pay in present value, not what the production is worth. Formerly mGuarantee.
entries.methodology: A two-stage regression (contract length first, then log guarantee given length) trained on the 2014-15-to-present FA signing corpus. Features: age, projected year-1 WAR (fWAR basis), position group, qualifying-offer status, class supply, the winter $/WAR level (carried forward ex-ante), nearest-comps anchors, and economic anchors (discounted projected WAR x $/WAR; prime years x quality). Predictions clamp to a 2.5x envelope around the comps median and blend toward comps in the megadeal regime. P10-P90 bands are empirical residual quantiles from the forward-chained backtest. It beat the nearest-comps baseline on guarantee, AAV and years across nine held-out winters (Gate 2, Model Accountability page). Phase 2 (2026-06) moved targets, comps anchors and the winter $/WAR series to the NPV basis; the current Gate 2 read (re-saved 2026-10-08 on the fWAR training label) is guarantee MAE 9.85 against comps 10.74 ($M, 1,199 signings). A LightGBM challenger with monotone economic constraints lost to this model on all three ship criteria at n = 1,199, so the two-stage OLS stays. The winter $/WAR carry was chosen by a forward-chained eval over 9 winters: carrying the last prior winter forward at 5% scored MAPE 0.104, a log-linear trend 0.105 and the trend with a CBT covariate 0.131, so the carry and the trend tie at this n. The served carry keeps the carry's form and escalates at the rate the series trends at (4.0% for the 2026-27 winter), not at 5%.

entries.definition: Predicted average annual value: projGuarantee / projLength, with its own P10-P90 band. Formerly displayed as mAAV.
entries.methodology: Both framings are projected: the per-year price (projAAV) and total value / length (projGuarantee / projLength). The projAAV band rides the guarantee band at the point-estimate term.

entries.definition: Predicted contract length in years (P10-P90 banded), from a log-years model with comps stacking and a prime-years-remaining term. Formerly displayed as mYears.
entries.methodology: Length is modeled before money (teams trade years against AAV). The stage predicts log(years) with curvature terms (WAR squared, age x WAR), prime years remaining (max(0, 30 - age)) and the nearest-comps median length as a feature. It beat the comps baseline 0.437 against 0.492 MAE across nine held-out winters (Gate 2, fa_mkt_v2, re-saved 2026-10-08).

entries.definition: The FA surfaces print a verdict (value = projected underpaid, market = about right, overpay = projected overpaid) backed by Deal+, the 100-scale index of rational value against price.
entries.methodology: Deal+ = 100 x rational value / predicted (or actual) guarantee. The verdict edges are empirically centered corpus terciles, not symmetric around 100: Deal+ is right-skewed under convex pricing. Since 2026-07-30 (owner decision) the edges are per position group, cut on the 1,300-signing forward-chained corpus at the actual price, so 'value' means cheap for the position group; re-cut 2026-10-08 (owner decision): SP overpay < 97 / value ≥ 214, RP 45 / 101, C 140 / 240, other position players 109 / 246. The RP edges sit lowest because relievers are paid more per projected WAR; about half of the old all-pitchers-look-like-overpays effect was that market property. A class that skews one way against these fixed edges is information.
entries.formula:
Deal+ = 100 x rational value / guarantee (predicted before signing, actual after)
verdict: overpay < lo, value >= hi, market between, with per-position-group tercile edges (lo/hi): SP 97/214, RP 45/101, C 140/240, POS 109/246
entries.example: A starter predicted at $60M with $130M of rational value reads Deal+ 217 (100 x 130/60): past the SP value edge of 214, verdict value. The same 217 on a catcher sits under the C edge of 240: market.

entries.definition: Rational value minus predicted market price.
entries.methodology: Two independently derived numbers: rational value (what the projected production is worth in NPV) and predicted market price (what teams will pay, from the market model). Contract Surplus ($) = rational − market; positive means the market is expected to underprice the player. The retrospective ledger applies the same lens backward: realized WAR (on the basis the ledger was built on, which the Archive names) x each season's estimated $/WAR minus prorated money paid, for every MLB free-agent deal since 2014-15.
entries.formula:
Contract Surplus ($) = rational value - predicted market price (both NPV, independently derived)
retrospective ledger: realized WAR (on the basis the ledger was built on, which the Archive names) x each season's estimated $/WAR - prorated money paid, summed over the deal
entries.example: Rational value $88M against a predicted guarantee of $70M reads +$18M. Backward, a 4-year $70M deal that returned 9 WAR at $11M/WAR ledgers 9 x 11 - 70 = +$29M.

entries.definition: The mean of the worst 10% of simulated WAR paths over the predicted term: a conditional value at risk, not the P10. A surplus point estimate hides what a deal looks like when it goes wrong; this is that number.
The probability a player reaches free agency at all. It is 100% when a contract simply expires, and lower for the option family, where membership stays probabilistic until the option resolves.
entries.methodology: Single-party options (club option, player option, opt-out) use the market model's band distribution (v2): a log-normal interpolated from the empirical residual bands (mu = log point estimate, sigma = P10-P90 span / (2 x 1.2816)), and P(enter) is the tail probability of the market against the strike. Strike and market number must be the same kind of quantity: club and player options strike one season's salary against projected AAV; an opt-out strikes the remaining guarantee against the projected multi-year guarantee. Mutual options keep a fixed empirical prior (both sides cannot want to exercise at once); conditional options carry a documented unknown prior. The v1 $-gap logistic (fa_class, config-documented) is the heuristic these paths replaced. Decision-level validation waits on historical option-decision data; the 2026-27 winter's logged events are the first live test. The source is carried per row in enterProbSrc.
entries.formula:
player-held (opt-out / player option): P(enter) = 1 - Phi((ln K - mu) / sigma); club option: P(enter) = Phi((ln K - mu) / sigma)
mu = ln(point estimate), sigma = (ln P90 - ln P10) / (2 x 1.2816); K = the strike (one season's salary for options, the remaining guarantee for opt-outs)
mutual option: fixed empirical prior; conditional: documented prior; no anchor -> no number
entries.example: A $20M club option on a player priced at $14M AAV (P10 $9M, P90 $22M): the club likely declines, P(enter) near 0.85. As a $20M player option he keeps the money: near 0.15.

entries.definition: A 0 to 1 score for how well a club and a free agent match, built from positional need, contention window, payroll room, park and the club's own signing behaviour. It is a model of where a player signs, scored on signing-team hit rate (top-1, top-3 and top-5 hits and MRR, forward-chained 2018-2026, n 1,173; fa_team_fit provisional), not a grade of club quality.
The dollar cost of forfeited draft picks (and intl pool money) when signing a qualifying-offer free agent.
entries.methodology: Signing a QO-attached free agent forfeits picks per the CBA compensation matrix (rule-versioned; CBT payors forfeit their 2nd- and 5th-highest picks plus $1M of international pool). Each forfeited slot is priced from the site's own draft research: realized expected first-six-season WAR at the slot through the surplus machinery. Rational value and pick values share the same 7% NPV currency, so the tax subtracts directly.
entries.formula:
QO tax = SUM(forfeited picks priced in $) + forfeited intl pool $ at face value
pick $ = realized expected first-6-season WAR at the representative slot, spread flat over 6 control years, priced through the service-time surplus machinery with a draft-to-debut lag (fallback: median consensus FV at the slot through the prospect surplus curve)
forfeiture matrix is rule-versioned CBA text, e.g. CBT payors forfeit their 2nd- and 5th-highest picks + $1M of intl pool
entries.example: A CBT-payor club signing a QO free agent gives up its 2nd- and 5th-highest picks plus $1M of international pool. With the two slots pricing near $12M and $3M of prospect surplus, the tax takes about $16M off the signing's rational value.

entries.definition: The NPV of a free agent's projected WAR path: each season priced convexly through the tier curve at the winter's ex-ante FA $/WAR level, escalated per season and discounted at the platform's configured 7% rate. What the production is worth, never what the market will pay.
entries.methodology: Since v2, the same convex season shape as PROSPX prospect surplus (the value framework's tier curve), at the same dollar level: the 2026-27 winter prices a win at $16.9M, and since 2026-09-25 prospect surplus and /projections/ price every season at that level too. On the curve, a 1-WAR season and the third win of a 3-WAR season are different products, and flat pricing graded the bottom of the class as bargains (class median Deal+ 220 under flat pricing). Computed with no reference to the market model; Contract Surplus is only meaningful because neither side reads the other. The winter $/WAR level is the NPV-basis signings-implied series (deferral-adjusted numerator): the last prior winter, carried forward at the rate the series itself trends at (4.0% a year for the 2026-27 winter, the same rate each later season escalates at).
entries.formula:
RV = SUM_t tiered_war_value(WAR_t) x level x (1 + infl)^t / (1 + r)^t
level = winter $/WAR (ex-ante, signings-implied) / the valuation set's flat $/WAR; r = the platform's configured discount rate
each season prices through the CONVEX tier curve, never WAR x a flat rate
entries.example: A projected 3.0-WAR season at a $12M/WAR winter prices above the flat 3.0 x 12 = $36M because the tier curve pays a premium for the third win; a 0.7-WAR season prices below its flat $8.4M. A discounted 3.0 / 2.6 / 2.2 path lands near $90M.

entries.definition: The 10th-90th percentile range around every FA market prediction: empirical residual quantiles from the forward-chained backtest. Parametric intervals failed the coverage gate (0.858 against the 0.75-0.85 target) and were rejected.

The 2022 CBA expires 2026-12-01, so every 2027 threshold, tax band and QO figure is the last known rule carried forward, not a bargained number. Every surface using one carries the carry-forward flag.

The per-winter price of a win implied by that winter's FA signings: guaranteed dollars over projected WAR, carried forward ex-ante so a prediction never sees its own winter. The PROSPX $/WAR (tiered) is FanGraphs' three-tier shape rescaled to this level.
entries.methodology: Two ex-ante steps. First, each winter's implied price: total NPV guarantee (deferral-adjusted when a schedule is on file) divided by total discounted projected contract WAR across that winter's MLB free-agent deals. WAR is projected point-in-time, so the ratio reads what buyers thought they were buying; thin winters are dropped. Second, the carry-forward: a class year's level uses PRIOR winters only (config market_model.dpw_forecast.method): flat5 carries the latest prior winter forward at a flat escalation, the trend variants fit a log-linear trend, and under four prior winters it is always flat5. The method choice is adjudicated by the forward-chained ledger in data/dpw_forecast_eval.json. This series sets the one level rational value, veteran surplus and prospect surplus price at; the PROSPX tiered $/WAR applies FanGraphs' tier shape around it. One copy is served (since 2026-09-25): it is written once a night before anything is priced (fa_market.write_dpw_series, also called by the Gate 2 persist), carries the level for the next class, and the class board, /projections/, prospect surplus, the $/WAR chart, the Archive and the Club Ledger all read it. The class board still re-derives the series from its own corpus as a check and publishes the largest gap.
entries.formula:
dpw(winter) = SUM NPV guarantees / SUM disc-WAR over that winter's deals; disc-WAR = SUM_t WAR_t / (1 + r)^t over each contract's term; thin winters dropped
winter_dpw(class year) = carry-forward from PRIOR winters only: flat5 = dpw(latest prior) x (1 + esc)^gap; trend = log-linear fit on prior winters; under 4 priors always flat5
entries.example: If the 2026 winter implied $11.5M per discounted projected WAR, the 2027 class prices off that number carried forward one year, about $12.1M under flat5. The 2027 winter's own signings never enter its level.

entries.definition: Badge on FA projections whose platform season is missing or injury-shortened: below 30% of a role-aware full season, scaled by how much of the season has elapsed. A projection resting on older seasons is the model's weakest case (the Burnes / Bieber rehab class).

The five 0-1 scores behind every FA team fit: need (displacement WAR gap at the position, discounted when a near-ETA PROSPX prospect blocks it; MLB incumbents block through the gap and are named in the blocked-by list), window (marginal playoff leverage at the club's baseline wins), afford (CBT-basis tax space against the predicted AAV, with a floor for habitual taxpayers), park (batted-side park factor, the smallest weight) and behavior (biggest-ever guarantee against this price, recent 3-winter outlay, $100M-deal participation).
entries.methodology: v2 weights: need 0.31 / window 0.19 / afford 0.22 / park 0.04 / behavior 0.24. Park was cut from 0.12 after the most suppressive park topped every pitcher's fit list. Afford reads Spotrac's CBT-basis tax space and floors at 0.4 for over-the-line clubs that keep signing nine-figure deals; behavior blends deal-scale history (0.5), recency-weighted three-winter outlay (0.3) and $100M-deal count (0.2). Blocked-by names two kinds of blocker: PX = a near-ETA PROSPX prospect (FV ≥ 50), MLB = a contracted incumbent projecting ≥ 2.5 WAR at the slot.
entries.formula:
fit = 0.31 x need + 0.19 x window + 0.22 x afford + 0.04 x park + 0.24 x behavior, each component 0-1
behavior = 0.5 x deal-scale history + 0.3 x recency-weighted 3-winter outlay + 0.2 x $100M-deal count; afford floors at 0.4 for over-the-line clubs that keep signing nine-figure deals
entries.example: A club with a 2-WAR hole at short (need 0.9), on the playoff bubble (window 0.8), tax room (afford 0.7), a neutral park (0.5) and a real spending record (behavior 0.8) scores 0.31x0.9 + 0.19x0.8 + 0.22x0.7 + 0.04x0.5 + 0.24x0.8 = 0.80.

entries.definition: Winter events (signings, option decisions, qualifying offers) are dated the day the pipeline first saw them, because the source publishes terms without dates. Stamps are append-only and never revised.

The FA module's two shipping gates: Gate 1, the projection engine against ten held-out seasons (beat the naive baseline; P10-P90 coverage in 0.75-0.85); Gate 2, the market model against nine forward-chained winters (beat nearest comps on guarantee, AAV and years). Both verdicts render on the Free Agency Model Accountability page, misses included.

The most similar historical contracts to a free agent's profile, by standardized feature distance over the 2014-15-to-present signing corpus. Always real deals; they anchor the market model and appear on every board row.

A Marcel-style weighted-rates projection (5/3/2 recency weights) with hitter ISO blended toward Savant xISO (2015+), mapped to WAR (fWAR basis: the corpus labels follow the training label, published fWAR since the 2026-10 epoch) through a fitted rate-to-WAR model and decayed along survivorship-corrected aging curves fit on the 2000-2026 corpus. Multi-year decay walks regressed-rate curves: raw observed deltas mix aging with luck regression, and chaining them double-counted the regression (the horizon-5 star tail collapsed to a 0.06 predicted/actual ratio). Power and finesse pitchers age on separate curves; hitter power/contact cohorts were measured and parked.
entries.methodology: Beyond Gate 1 (next season), multi-year decay is measured by a forward-chained horizon backtest (proj_eval.py, bases 2017-2021): the regressed-rate curves doubled the horizon-5 ≥3-WAR tail ratio (0.06 to 0.12) and cut star bias from -1.34 to -0.64 WAR while Gate 1 improved. Since Phase 1 (2026-06) horizons 1-5 on /projections/ are served by proj_lgbm_v1, LightGBM quantile models (P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 per horizon) stacked on the Marcel champion (its prediction is a feature, so the trees learn its residuals), with no zero floor on the bands. It shipped after beating the champion on dev bases, the Gate-1 seasons and a touched-once 2022-2024 holdout. Marcel + aging stays the fallback, the stacking feature and the shape for horizons 6+. The /fa/ page does not use the quantile heads. It prices every contract on the Marcel champion path, the input its market model passed Gate 2 on, so /fa/ and /projections/ can print different WAR for the same player and season. The /projections/ card names the FA path beside its own. Each surface serves the engine that won its own gate, and both pages print that gate's figures. A future class (the 2028 and 2029 winters) overlays the projection's champion mean for the seasons it reaches and, past the fifth, chains this page's own fifth season along the projection's champion aging curve with the same function /projections/ uses for a contract past its fifth season (P10 and P90 at 0.6 and 1.4 times the champion, the P10 not floored at zero), so the two pages extend a path on one curve and a later season differs between them in the same proportion as the fifth season does. A future class (the 2028 and 2029 winters) overlays the projection's champion mean for the seasons it reaches and, past the fifth, chains this page's own fifth season along the projection's champion aging curve with the same function /projections/ uses for a contract past its fifth season (P10 and P90 at 0.6 and 1.4 times the champion, the P10 not floored at zero), so the two pages extend a path on one curve and a later season differs between them in the same proportion as the fifth season does. Long-horizon star medians run ~0.2 WAR below the champion (zero-inflated labels), with equal star MAE.
entries.formula:
year-1 rate = Marcel(5/3/2 recency weights, exposure-weighted) regressed to the league mean, hitter ISO blended toward Savant xISO; WAR1 = fitted rate-to-WAR map(rate)
year-t: WAR1 decayed along the survivorship-corrected REGRESSED-rate aging curve for the player's cohort (power and finesse pitchers on separate curves)
/projections/ horizons 1-5: proj_lgbm_v1 quantile heads (P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 per horizon) stacked ON the Marcel prediction; horizons 6+ and the fallback ride the Marcel+aging shape; /fa/ pricing: the Marcel champion path at every horizon; a future class past the projection's fifth season: chain_aging_tail(its fifth season, the projection's champion aging curve); a future class past the projection's fifth season: chain_aging_tail(its fifth season, the projection's champion aging curve)
entries.example: A 29yo hitter with trailing wOBA .350 / .340 / .320 (most recent first) blends to (5x.350 + 3x.340 + 2x.320)/10 = .341 before the league pull moves it a few points toward .310. The rate maps to a year-1 WAR, and the aging curve lowers each later season.

entries.definition: ERA scaled so 100 = average; lower is better. 90 reads 10% better. Two quantities share the label: on MLB seasons it is MLB's published ERA- (park- and league-adjusted, read verbatim); on MiLB seasons it is level-relative, shrunk, and has no park adjustment.
entries.origin: Industry metric. The ERA- park- and league-adjusted index, implemented by FanGraphs (100 = average, lower is better). The MiLB version here is level-relative and not park-adjusted.
entries.methodology:
MiLB: ERA- vs level = 100 × ERA_adj / level ERA, where ERA_adj = (IP × ERA + 50 × level ERA) / (IP + 50) pulls a short sample toward the level mean (K = 50 IP) and the level ERA comes from the level norms. No park term. MLB: read verbatim from MLB's published eraMinus.

On a combined MiLB row of the PROSPX Leaderboards the level ERA is the mean of the levels played, weighted by innings.
entries.formula:
MiLB: ERA- = 100 × ((IP·ERA + 50·lgERA_level) / (IP + 50)) / lgERA_level
MLB: published eraMinus (park- and league-adjusted)

entries.definition: On-base average with each event weighted by its actual run value (a walk is worth less than a double, which OBP ignores). Scaled to look like OBP: ~.320 is league average, .400 elite.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Created by Tom Tango (The Book); implemented by FanGraphs. It weights each offensive event by its average run value.

entries.definition: Lifecycle markers on module names: α = newly launched, numbers may still move; β = established, in beta. The masthead chip and the nav superscript are the same marker.
The homepage MLB News feed and ticker: MLB and MiLB transactions, debuts, IL moves, eFV changes and FA events, dated, typed by colour and glyph.
In-season days a free agent spent on the injured list in each of the last three seasons, summed. Descriptive: a record of time missed, not an availability forecast.
entries.methodology: Each IL stint counts its days inside Apr 1 to Oct 1 (2020: Jul 23 to Sep 28), ended by the player's next IL move; a stint still open stops at the transaction log's last day. The row details split the total by season.

entries.definition: Every roster move the 30 clubs file with MLB (trades, signings, IL placements and activations, call-ups, options, DFAs, claims, releases), read from the MLB StatsAPI each night. The site keeps one row per player, date and type and prints each description as MLB filed it.
entries.methodology: The log on file runs from 2008 and is thin before 2009. A trade is one deal per date and pair of clubs. It feeds the Timeline on an MLB player page, the MLB rows on MLB News and On This Day, and the IL days column on Free Agency. No injury forecast is drawn from it.

entries.definition: The currently tracked, non-graduated MiLB prospects that every ranking, farm grade and Arkmetric is computed over. MLB-side modules (Free Agency) read prospect data read-only and may not write into it.

Every projected WAR path ships three variants: mean, floor (P10) and ceiling (P90). Veterans take quantile paths; prospects take the 10th / 90th-percentile outcome bucket of the calibrated P(bucket|FV): a prospect's downside is the bust outcome, not a symmetric band.
entries.methodology: Veterans on /projections/ take their floor / mean / ceiling from the proj_lgbm_v1 quantile heads (trained on horizon residual distributions, negatives included). The /fa/ board prices contracts on the Marcel champion path, so its floor and ceiling are the Gate-1 year-1 residual band (fa_gate1_eval.json, player-specific width from band_scale) decayed along the aging curves. Unlike the /projections/ floor, the /fa/ season floor is truncated at 0 WAR: the decay that carries the band forward stops every season at zero, so a member whose band reaches below zero shows a 0.0 floor. Each season's floor and ceiling are that season's own P10 and P90, not a path: no career sits at its P10 every season, and adding them overstates the range. The /fa/ surplus range therefore reads the 10th and 90th percentile of contract value across the correlated simulated careers that also give the downside WAR (the fa_mc copula), for terms of two or more seasons; a one-season term prices that season's P10 and P90 directly, which is the same number. The path-priced range is kept in the artifact as surplusP10Comon / surplusP90Comon. The fa_mc ledger measured the copula WAR total covering held careers less often than the path sum did, because the per-season bands are themselves too narrow; the simulated range inherits that.
entries.formula:
/projections/ veterans: floor / mean / ceiling = the quantile heads' P10 / mean / P90 paths
/fa/: season floor / ceiling = the Gate-1 year-1 band decayed along the aging curves (per-season marginals); the /fa/ floor is truncated at 0 WAR in every season (the decay stops each season at zero), unlike the /projections/ floor
/projections/ guaranteed seasons past the fifth: floor / ceiling = the fifth season's P10 / P90 chained along the champion aging curve, the floor not floored at zero
prospects: floor / ceiling = the 10th / 90th-percentile OUTCOME BUCKET of the calibrated P(bucket | FV) categorical
/fa/ surplus range (term of 2+ seasons) = P10 / P90 over copula draws of SUM_t value(WAR_t) x level_t, minus the predicted guarantee; one-season term = value(season P10 / P90) minus the guarantee
entries.example: A veteran projected at 3.1 WAR next season might carry a 1.2 floor and a 4.8 ceiling. A FV 50 prospect's floor is the bust bucket, about zero WAR.

entries.definition: The /projections/ surface: the FA module's projection engine (proj_lgbm_v1 quantile heads stacked on its Marcel champion) applied to every MLB player with recent history (five-year WAR paths, fWAR basis: trained on published fWAR since the 2026-10 epoch, with floor / mean / ceiling buckets), plus PROSPX prospects joining at their projected ETA through the calibrated FV outcome model.
entries.methodology:
Veterans: proj_lgbm_v1, LightGBM quantile heads for horizons 1-5 stacked on the Marcel champion (Marcel rates, aging curves and the fitted WAR map; its prediction is a feature). The expected path is the median head, lifted toward the quantile-implied mean where it sits below it; floor and ceiling are the P10 and P90 heads. The FA class board prices on the Marcel champion path itself, so the two pages can print different WAR for the same season, and the Team Outlook roll-up sums the champion mean path because quantile points must never be summed. Prospects: P(bucket|FV) x per-bucket WAR trajectories scaled by FV and shaped by projected debut age (bust-inclusive means, outcome-bucket floor and ceiling). Seasons price through the convex tier curve at the ex-ante FA $/WAR level; the board banner states the level and whether it escalates across seasons. Veteran surplus prices every season of the club control window: contracted dollars where a contract exists, the league minimum for pre arbitration seasons, and the projected award for arbitration seasons, discounted at the platform's 7% rate. A guaranteed contract that runs past the fifth projected season is priced through its last guaranteed season, and the seasons after the fifth price on the Marcel champion's aging curve chained from the fifth season's WAR (the FA module's own seam: the champion's relative decay applied to that WAR), so the WAR does not step between the fifth and sixth seasons; the board prints five seasons, so the salary path strip names the WAR each later season priced on. Each of those seasons also carries its own P10 and P90: the fifth season's P10 and P90 chained along the same curve, the P10 not floored at zero, so a fifth season P10 below zero carries on below zero rather than stepping up to zero (a season at or below zero WAR prices at $0). The trade value's P10-P90 range spans every priced season through the last guaranteed one. Each of those seasons also carries its own P10 and P90: the fifth season's P10 and P90 chained along the same curve, the P10 not floored at zero, so a fifth season P10 below zero carries on below zero rather than stepping up to zero (a season at or below zero WAR prices at $0). The trade value's P10-P90 range spans every priced season through the last guaranteed one. Seasons past club control carry a projection and no price, and so does an unsigned club controlled season past the fifth projected season. Prospect surplus is the eFV surplus the Trade Machine board serves for the same prospect (the eFV export's surplus_mm, over the 7-season valuation window from the projected ETA); the board copies it and does not reprice it.

Team Outlook win totals are retro-backtested on 2022-25 with 2025 held out. Each roster sums the engine's mean year-1 projections (the median-like quantile point on player pages is never summed) plus a depth pool of sub-floor players, and every season is recentered uniformly so the league sums to 2,430 wins. Age-cohort corrections fit on 2022-24 residuals were tested as a challenger on the held-out 2025, lost, and are not applied. The Accountability view prints the served roll-up's team MAE and r per season beside a prior-season-wins carry-forward, read from team_outlook_eval.json.

The board shows two different facts about the same player and keeps them apart by name: the Control column prints the last season the club HOLDS him (guaranteed contract seasons, then the remaining pre arbitration seasons, then the projected arbitration seasons) and its sub line prints the last season a signed contract GUARANTEES him. The seasons past the guarantee are projections and are drawn with a dashed border.
entries.formula:
veterans: proj_lgbm_v1 quantile heads stacked on the FA Marcel champion (Marcel + aging + fitted WAR map), five-year WAR paths (fWAR basis, the training label) with quantile floor / mean / ceiling; surplus over the club control window: unsigned seasons inside the five projected seasons, a guarantee through its last season (seasons past the fifth on the champion aging curve chained from the fifth; each such season's P10 / P90 = the fifth season's P10 / P90 chained the same way, the P10 not floored at zero)
prospects: P(bucket | FV) x per-bucket WAR trajectories scaled by FV and projected debut age, joining at projected ETA
team outlook: SUM roster mean year-1 WAR + depth pool, league-normalized to 2,430 wins (age-cohort corrections apply only while they win their holdout gate; today they do not)
entries.example: A 27yo 4-WAR starter shows a declining five-year path with a surplus claim over every season his club controls: his contracted years at their salary, then his projected arbitration years. A FV 55 prospect with ETA 2027 joins his club's 2027 line with a bust-inclusive mean.

entries.definition: The accountability tab on MLB Projections: each model's champion, the baseline it had to beat, the metric, the held-out result, and what is not yet scoreable. Verdicts read from the model registry, refreshed monthly.
entries.methodology: Forward-chained evaluation: fit through year Y-1, score the untouched year Y, repeat, and report pooled and per-year accuracy against a stated baseline. Validated requires that backtest to beat its baseline on the pre-registered metric; partial measurement (short window, descriptive, live-pending) ships provisional. The eval artifacts (data/*_eval.json) hold the tables; the registry (data/model_registry.json) holds the one-line verdict and disclosures, and test_methodology_freshness.py requires every registry model to map to a glossary entry.

entries.definition: The four-way label every registry model carries: validated (a forward-chained backtest beats the baseline), provisional (measured, partially: short window or descriptive), unvalidated (a predictive claim with no measurement yet, listed so it stays visible) or deprecated (failed validation, retired).
entries.methodology: Verdicts are committed with their eval artifact, not auto-derived: validated requires the artifact to exist and beat its baseline on the pre-registered metric; unvalidated must not carry an artifact. The monthly refresh re-stamps freshness (artifact age) and never upgrades a verdict.

entries.definition: Grading a model on history it never saw: train on seasons through Y-1, score the untouched year Y, walk forward a year at a time. No lookahead, so the error is what a reader would have gotten in real time.
entries.methodology: Curves, weights and maps are refit per target year on data through Y-1 (the Gate-1 pattern), predictions are compared with realized outcomes, and accuracy is pooled across folds and reported per year. A held-out season untouched during tuning is the cleanest read; the rest are dev folds. Team-level reads assign each player to his actual season team, isolating engine error from roster churn.

entries.definition: A season (or fold) kept out of every tuning decision and scored once, at the end. Its error is the least biased accuracy estimate; a model that wins on dev folds and loses the holdout does not ship.
entries.methodology: Dev folds are used repeatedly while iterating; the holdout is not. The projections engine reports a touched-once 2022-2024 holdout for veteran WAR paths and a held-out 2025 for team wins; out-years whose labels have not matured are flagged not yet scoreable.

entries.definition: The live scoreboard for a projection whose target has not happened: the number is published now and graded against a stated baseline when the outcome lands.
entries.methodology: Team Outlook win totals are the standing case: only the first projected season is gated, scored as MAE against final standings (baseline = prior-season wins carried forward); out-years are a trajectory, not a scored forecast. The gate stays pending until the season ends, then the result is committed whatever it says. The graded forecast is a frozen copy: the projections file is rewritten nightly, so the last nightly before the season's first game is committed by hand and pinned by its hash, and that copy is the one scored. The first freeze is the 2027 preseason.

entries.definition: The average size of a model's misses in the units it predicts: mean |actual - predicted|. Lower is better. A team-wins MAE of 7.7 means records miss by about eight wins on average.
entries.methodology: Reported with bias (mean signed error) and, for bands, coverage (share of actuals inside P10-P90, target ~80%). MAE weights misses linearly, so the heavy WAR tail does not dominate it the way it would a squared error.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: The behavioral profile on each farm system's Tendencies tab: promotion aggressiveness, draft position and trait preferences, pitch identity of developed arms, per-tool development rates, international pool strategy (quality vs quantity), trade profile (volume, prospect-capital direction, quality vs depth, cash considerations), draft-pool allocation and IL burden. Every value is league-relative.
entries.methodology: Each axis comes from the platform's own records (grade history 2017-present, signed draft picks 2021-present, IFA classes, the trade ledger, MLB transaction text) as a z-score across the 30 orgs; verdict labels fire only at |z| ≥ 0.5. Tool development counts only same-source snapshot pairs ≥ 60 days apart inside one org, so cross-source disagreement never counts as development. Pitch identity profiles the MLB arsenals of players an org developed (per-pitch usage history is not archived yet). Cash-consideration direction is parsed from official transaction text.
entries.formula:
each axis: z = (org value - 30-org mean) / 30-org sd; a verdict label fires only at |z| >= 0.5
tool development counts only SAME-SOURCE snapshot pairs >= 60 days apart inside one org
entries.example: An org promoting hitters 0.8 sd faster than league with an intl class-size z of +0.6 and an average-bonus z of -0.4 reads 'aggressive promoter, quantity buyer': the +0.6 axis gets a label, the -0.4 axis stays unlabeled under the 0.5 gate.

entries.definition: How far a drafted player has outrun his slot, on the Draft tab's Overperformers board. Two lenses: realized outcome (current prospect FV minus the median FV for his pick band, with career MLB WAR beside it) and draft-day value (how many picks past his pre-draft consensus rank he went).
entries.methodology: Realized outcome bins signed picks 2021-present into bands (1-5, 6-10, 11-20, 21-40, 41-75, 76-150, 151+) and takes the median current FV per band as the slot expectation; overperformance is current FV minus that median. Current value joins from the live board and debuts via the promoted / MiLB-key link, falling back to the draft-time grade. Draft-day value = actual overall pick − pre-draft consensus rank. Pooled across completed classes, deduped.

entries.definition: Contract dollars discounted for deferral schedules at the platform's net 7% rate, the basis for every Phase-2 market number. A curated ledger (data/deferrals.json) holds the schedules: Ohtani's $700M prices as ~$274.8M of present liability; deals with no schedule keep their sticker.
entries.methodology: NPV = sum of scheduled payments / (1+r)^years-out, with r the configured net rate 0.07 (value_framework discount_rate, from clemens_2026 params.discount.net_rate) and years-out counted from 0, so a first-season payment is undiscounted; schedules rescaled to the sticker total. The net 7% platform rate is harsher than the CBT's ~4.4% statutory rate, so these NPVs read lower than league-reported figures; one discount rate is used everywhere (prospect surplus, rational value, contracts). Every guarantee ≥ $200M must carry a schedule or an explicit none entry (the Gate-2 coverage audit lists misses); entries are curated and unverified until owner spot-check.

entries.definition: Swing-quality index from Statcast bat tracking (bat speed, swing length, attack angle and direction, swing-path tilt, intercept point), scaled so 100 = league average; higher is better. eephus.io runs the model's scoring on each player's tracked MLB swings.
entries.methodology: Per-swing features are filtered to competitive swings, aggregated per hitter (means and variability), and scored through the model's run-value pipelines with a reliability shrink toward 100 below ~180 swings. Bat tracking exists only at MLB (2024+); no public MiLB tracking exists, so prospects light up after their debut.
entries.example: A debuted prospect at Swing+ 115 over 300+ swings has a plus MLB swing; 95 on 60 swings is mostly shrink.

entries.definition: eephus.io's college baseball percentile module: Savant-style hitter and pitcher dashboards over college TrackMan-era data, with per-metric leaderboards, player pages and search.
entries.methodology: Percentiles are computed within the college dataset's qualified pool per season. The module is in alpha.

entries.definition: eephusFV (eFV) is our Future Value grade and the site's primary prospect ranking. Since 2026-10-15 the board serves eFV v5 COMBINED in its re-fit form: it keeps the consensus FV order inside hitters and inside pitchers, lets a set of drivers move a prospect up or down that order, and the grade is the consensus value at his new rank. For hitters the one driver with weight is the hit tool grade. Pitchers move on Single-A production in groups by level, age and role, scouting grades, injury history and pitch-level strike rates. The re-fit beat the first v5 fit in its backtest and ties consensus. The board order, the displayed grade, the dollars and the outcome odds all read that one number. Prospects no source has graded show the production-only provisional grade instead, and graduates keep the earlier eFV v1 grade described below. The grade reads the latest full minor league season, which can be newer than some consensus lists. Its standing against consensus prints on the Source Comparison page.
entries.methodology:
EFV V5 COMBINED, SERVED FROM 2026-10-15, RE-FIT THE SAME DAY (owner decisions EW3-10 and EFV-REFIT-1). It keeps the order index of V2 below, so consensus still sets the level and the model only reorders. The re-fit (docs/efv-v2/EFV_V5_REFIT.md, variant RT) repairs the league norms of the population translation, ranks that translation inside each year, and drops the columns that read nothing on the live board. It adds training rows read on 15 October with the consensus of that day. The head weights are re-derived out of fold by the project's ratio rule on both development frames. The arrival (timing) head carries no weight on either side. Hitters are consensus plus 0.30 of the hit tool term: the penalty search set every added hitter column to zero. Pitchers keep the joint skill head at full weight. On the live board its columns are built as of today, held to the range seen in training, and a column whose training values all came from one season is withheld. On the development frames the re-fit beat the first v5 fit (within Spearman difference +0.0072 pooled; +0.0326 on the debut cohorts, CI95 +0.0056 to +0.0585) and passed its pre-registered ship rule. Against consensus it ties on both frames. data/xfv.json meta.served_model.receipt carries the live drivers and data/efv5_refit_weights.json the weights.

EFV V5 COMBINED, FIRST FIT, SERVED ON 2026-10-15 BEFORE THE RE-FIT (owner decision EW3-10). Each head was one joint penalized fit of V2's admitted drivers and every candidate the 2026-10 metric atlas produced, at V2's head weights (hitters 0.909 skill and 0.203 arrival, pitchers 1.0 and 0.020). It carried 44 hitter keys and 36 pitcher keys. In the backtest it tied the V2 fit (within Spearman difference -0.0028 pooled over 6,188 rows, every interval spanning zero) and did not meet its pre-registered ship rule. The owner switched it on anyway. data/efv5_combined_weights.json keeps its weights.

EFV V2, SERVED 2026-09-25 TO 2026-10-15. The order index is the prospect's percentile inside his side's consensus FV order plus a weighted sum of drivers, each expressed in consensus-percentile units, and the grade is the consensus value of the side at that rank, so consensus sets the level and the model only reorders. A driver enters only if the sign of its effect held in every training year and its average strength cleared a fixed bar (the admission rule). On the fit served at launch (2026-09-25; data/xfv.json meta.served_model.receipt carries the live one) the hitter drivers are the hit tool grade and the highest level reached; no pitcher driver passed the rule, so pitchers follow the consensus order exactly and carry no driver chips. The weights on the drivers were fixed by a rule over training years up to 2016 before any development read. The fit uses debut classes before 2025 and never reads the reserved frames. Injury, prospect age, a reliever role and Statcast signals show on the card as labelled notes and do not move the grade. The outcome odds are the consensus outcome table read at the eFV grade, and surplus dollars are priced at the same grade. The board labels eFV V2 against consensus from the progress ledger, and it reads as a tie until a reserved read says otherwise.

EFV V1, graduates and busts, and the board until 2026-09-25. A prior-anchored, outcome-grounded model. The prior is consensus FV (raw, pre-rounding); a lean ridge model, with a guarded blend back toward consensus, moves the grade only on signals that add information beyond consensus out of sample. Hitters: level-translated on-base skill (OBP) and contact (K rate and its multi-season peak), an OPS-vs-level read for the fringe tiers, age relative to level and absolute age, track record (pro seasons, a missing-record indicator, IFA / college cohorts), highest level reached, and the hit and speed tools. Pitchers: multi-season peak and final-season strikeout rate, walk rate, K-backed run prevention (the x_era_k interaction behind KRP+), age relative to level and absolute age, and the fastball. Game power is excluded for hitters because scouts over-price it relative to realized WAR; that omission is eFV's power correction.

Training: prospects who debuted 2011-2025 (RESOLVED_THROUGH 2026 from the 2026-10 epoch; boards strictly before debut) against realized first-six-season WAR (published fWAR labels from the 2026-10 epoch, frozen per season; eWAR v2 labels from the 2026-09 epoch to then, bWAR labels before it), busts at zero, forward-chained out of time. The 2024 debut class is right-censored (two of six seasons observed) and enters at reduced weight.

Grade scale (restamped 2026-07-30): the eFV v1 grade is value_framework.outcome_implied_fv(E[6yr WAR]), the inverse of the pooled empirical outcome curve fit on resolved cohorts, so the grade is the FV whose measured first-six-year WAR matches the prediction. A pure function of predicted WAR (no age or position). Below about FV 45 the measured curve is flat, so grades there preserve order but their spacing is not outcome-calibrated. Above about FV 57 the measured cells hold single digits per grade and are blended toward a published industry prior, so the top of the board is closer to the industry table than to our measurement.

Two other grades sit under a graduate's eFV v1 grade. Surplus dollars price through the retired per-side quantile grade, because the surplus and WAR-path curves were fit on the consensus 20-80 scale that map lands on. The star/bust odds stay on the retired realized-implied map, where they were ground-truthed; re-keying them has not been measured.

Level calibration, retired 2026-08-14: the served WAR is the model's WAR. eFV v1's standing against consensus prints on the Source Comparison page, read from the backtest artifact. Its retired steps (the quantile display map, the board overlays and the level calibration) are dated rows on Model Updates.

Registry verdict: provisional.
entries.formula:
ACTIVE BOARD, eFV v5 COMBINED re-fit since 2026-10-15 (grade_basis efv_v2, the same order-index form): eFV grade = the consensus FV value of the prospect's (side, list year) group at the rank of his order_idx
order_idx = u_c + w_skill x e_skill + w_time x e_time, where u_c is his percentile in his side's consensus FV order and the driver terms are in the same percentile units
admitted drivers on the served fit (data/xfv.json meta.served_model.receipt): hitters tool_hit; pitchers scr_g5_pit_A_all_all_k_minus_bb, scr_g5_pit_A_all_all_k_pct, scr_g5_pit_A_young_all_k_pct, scr_g5_pit_A_young_all_k_minus_bb, scr_g5_pit_A_all_SP_k_pct, scr_g5_pit_A_all_SP_k_minus_bb, scr_g5_pit_A_all_SP_bf_per_g, scr_t5_pit_AAA_all_all_fb_fut, scr_w2i_stints_skill_pit, scr_w2i_days_skill_pit, scr_w2i_sixty_skill_pit, scr_w2i_open_skill_pit, scr_w2i_recur_skill_pit, scr_w2p_cstr_p, scr_w2p_csw_p, scr_w2p_k_resid_p, scr_w2p_fstrike_p, scr_w2b_pu_p, scr_w4p_pop_pit, scr_w2s_brk_pit, scr_w2s_cmd_pit; each head one joint sign-bounded penalized fit; the re-fit's weights (data/efv5_refit_weights.json): w_skill hitters 0.297, pitchers 1.0; w_time 0 on both sides (under V2, 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-15: hitters tool_hit and level_rank, pitchers none)
surplus = value_framework( eFV grade ); star/bust odds = the consensus outcome table read at the eFV grade
GRADUATES AND BUSTS, eFV v1 (their locked grade): eFV grade = outcome_implied_fv( E[6yr WAR] ) on the training label (published fWAR from the 2026-10 epoch), the inverse of the pooled empirical outcome curve fit on resolved cohorts; surplus = value_framework( retired per-side quantile grade ); star/bust odds = outcome model( retired realized-implied FV )
entries.example: Take two pitchers on the same list year with the same consensus grade. The one with the better Single-A strikeout rate for starters, or the better minor league line translated to future WAR, moves up the pitchers' consensus order. He takes the consensus grade of the pitcher ranked where he lands, so he can read above consensus while the other reads below it. The card lists the drivers that moved him most, largest first, in percentile points of his group.

entries.definition: Per-tool eFV: each 20-80 tool re-graded by how well it, plus the prospect's relevant production, predicts the MLB outcome the tool is meant to forecast.
entries.methodology: Each tool with a clean realized target is grounded in the MLB stat it predicts: power in ISO, hit in average and contact, speed in steals, the fastball in strikeout rate, command in walk rate. Tool eFV blends the consensus tool grade with pre-debut MiLB production only where production adds signal beyond the grade. Scout grades are already good (power grade to MLB ISO ranks at about 0.52); production adds most for fastball-to-strikeout. Tools with no clean realized metric (raw power, fielding, arm, individual breaking-ball shapes) pass the consensus grade through unchanged.
entries.formula: tool eFV = rank-map( z(grade) + w*z(MiLB production) ), w from the production's partial correlation after the grade
entries.example: A pitcher whose fastball grades 55 but who already misses bats at an elite MiLB rate can carry a higher fastball eFV, because realized strikeout rate adds to the grade for predicting MLB strikeouts.

entries.definition: A PROVISIONAL grade for prospects who have played pro ball but have no grade from any label source (FanGraphs, MLB Pipeline, Baseball America, ESPN, Just Baseball): DSL / CPX breakouts the ranking cycle has not reached, plus deep-system depth. On the PROSPX board these players sit in their own section, 'Not yet graded by any source', below every graded prospect and with no board or org rank, ordered by the chance of a first grade. Their card leads with the expected first grade on the FanGraphs scale and the chance of a first grade by the next list window, and shows this map value beneath them, relabelled the production grade, with a dashed badge. Most land 20-30; real production breakouts reach the 40s, where a soft ceiling compresses the top so an unscouted player cannot run away from the scale. Trade values and the farm top-end and depth pool still read it.
entries.methodology: The flagship eFV is anchored on consensus FV and abstains without a source grade, so ungraded players get a production-only model: a ridge on the same translated MiLB production features (level-relative K / BB / OBP / ISO against contemporaneous norms, age for level, multi-season peaks, track record) without the consensus-FV feature (hitters keep level reached; pitchers drop it because it rewards quad-A org arms). Forward-chained and scored on the source-GRADED labelled pool, the served grade's rank correlation (Spearman) with realized WAR is 0.27 for hitters (n 1,032) and 0.11 for pitchers (n 895), from data/xfv_ungraded_eval.json: that is WAR skill on players a source has already graded, not skill at the grade a source will give an ungraded player. Scored against the first source grade instead (data/provisional_track_eval.json, shown on Source Comparison under Provisional track record), it orders who is graded next but does not predict the level, so the board keeps these players out of the eFV rank. Their section order and the card's lead numbers come from the first-grade model (data/provisional_v2.json): the chance that a label source grades the player inside 6 and 12 months of the anchor, recalibrated to the latest closed anchor's base rate, and the expected first FV if FanGraphs grades him (35+ counted as 37.5). They rejoin the eFV rank only after a frozen window shows that expected first grade beating a constant. The WAR prediction maps through a linear grade curve with a soft knee: above the knee the grade is compressed toward a ceiling, so the order is kept but a thin sample cannot print a top-prospect grade. A typical org filler reads about 22-25. Each card also carries a receipt: the grade frozen on the freeze date and, once it arrives, the first source grade after it.
entries.formula: provisional eFV = max( 20 , BASE + SLOPE * model E[6yr WAR] ), compressed above KNEE toward CEIL (no consensus-FV anchor). Hitters: 27 + 3.8 * WAR, knee 43, ceiling 49. Pitchers: 25 + 4.5 * WAR, knee 34, ceiling 38.
entries.example: Anthony Potestio (NYY, Single-A, age 21.9) has no source grade. A .513 OBP and .351 ISO over 80 plate appearances put his provisional eFV at 46.8 on the 2026-09-24 build, shown as 47: above the hitter knee of 43, so it sits in the compressed band.

entries.definition: Pitcher index for run prevention backed by missing bats: a below-level ERA supported by an above-level strikeout rate. 100 = active-pitcher-pool average, 10 points = 1 standard deviation; higher is better.
entries.methodology:
Puts the eFV pitcher model's run-prevention x strikeout interaction on the shared '+' scale. Raw term = (-era_rel) x k_rel, where era_rel = ERA minus the level-median ERA and k_rel = K% minus the level-median K%, both shrunk by batters faced with w = BF / (BF + 40) (80 before the 2026-07-24c loosen), so a cameo reads pool-neutral. The product is high only when both legs hold: K-backed run prevention, not a low ERA on weak contact.

The display pill and the model feature differ in one quadrant. With both legs bad (ERA worse than level and K% below level) the product of two negatives is positive. The eFV model feature (efv_model._x_era_k) zeroes that quadrant (2026-07-14 owner correction), which suits the fit but collapses roughly 834 doubly-below-average arms onto one league-average value. The display raw (efv_score._krp_display_raw, owner-authorized 2026-07-24) carries the negatively signed magnitude there instead, so those arms spread below the pool. Nothing else differs. For the display raw only, era_rel is winsorized to ±6 so a one-inning blowup cannot drive the pill.

The display raw is z-scored over the live pitcher pool and anchored 100 + 10z (population sigma, as SC+, DvM+ and pStuff+), unclamped (the 40-160 display clamp was removed 2026-07-24b; see the plus_metric_recal registry row). Pitchers with innings on file only. The same signal drives the 'K-backed run prevention' factor in the eFV explainer.
entries.formula:
KRP+ = 100 + 10 x (x_display - pool_mean) / pool_sd over the live pitcher pool, population sigma, no clamp.
x_display = (-era_rel) x k_rel everywhere EXCEPT the double-bad quadrant (era_rel > 0 AND k_rel < 0), where x_display = -abs((-era_rel) x k_rel).
MODEL feature (the eFV input, efv_model._x_era_k) = the same product except the double-bad quadrant returns 0.0. The pill and the model feature agree everywhere else.
era_rel and k_rel are level-relative rates shrunk by BF / (BF + 40); for the display raw only, era_rel is winsorized to plus or minus 6.
entries.example: A AA starter at a 2.90 ERA (level 4.20) with a 29% K% (level 22%) reads KRP+ ~120. The same ERA on a 19% K% reads near 100: run prevention the strikeouts do not support.

entries.definition: Values a trade both ways in one surplus currency: prospects on eFV surplus (calibrated NPV over the 7-season valuation window from their ETA), MLB players on projection surplus (NPV of projected production minus salary over the club control window). Build a package per side; the verdict states the gap in surplus, balanced within $5M, and predicts no club's answer.
entries.methodology:
A package evaluator plus the Bayesian trade-value board. Each player carries the surplus the rest of the site shows: a prospect's eFV-driven surplus over the 7-season valuation window (value_mm) or an MLB player's projection surplus (proj.surNpv, the MLB Projections NPV of convex production value minus salary over the club control window). An MLB Projections player page deep-links into the evaluator with that player loaded; evaluator rows link back. The Transactions Trade Audit prices every party at this same trade value, as of today rather than the trade date, and shares the $5M balanced band; a party with no trade value counts as $0 on his side and the card names him in a footnote. Board ranks are contract-aware (surplus over the seasons still controlled), positional-scarcity and opt-out adjusted.

A club controlled player with no contract for those years is priced on his salary path, not left at zero.

An MLB player's range is the projection P10-P90: every season the value prices at its own P10 and P90 WAR together, with the salary path and the non-tender decision held at the mean path, through the last guaranteed season. Past the fifth projected season it takes the fifth season's P10 and P90 chained along the champion aging curve, the P10 not floored at zero; a declined club option season carries no range.
entries.formula:
side value = SUM player surplus: prospects at value_mm (calibrated eFV NPV over the 7-season valuation window), MLB players at proj.surNpv (NPV of projected production minus salary, the club control window only)
net = side A - side B; |net| < $5M -> balanced, otherwise the verdict names the side that receives less, by $|net| and as a share of the larger side (gap = |net| / max(|A|, |B|)); it predicts no club's answer
entries.example: A FV 55 prospect at $45M plus a FV 40 arm at $6M against a two-control-year MLB starter at $48M: net +$3M, inside the $5M band, verdict balanced.

entries.definition: For one player on the Trade Machine builder, the 29 clubs other than his own ordered by a published rule with every factor printed: need at his slot, contention, the marginal tax his CBT charge carries, and farm surplus as the ability to pay in prospects. A screen, not a rumor board: it makes no claim about any trade.
entries.methodology: Rule partner_v1, registered before any screen output existed: each factor ranks the 29 clubs, ties at their average rank, and scores (29 - rank) / 28; an input not on file scores 0.5. Need is the starter's HEM+ at the position with team DEM+ for a fielder, Offense+ for a designated hitter, Rotation+ for a starter and Bullpen+ for a reliever, lower counting as more need. Contention is Team Outlook's 2027 wins on the served frame before the first regular-season game and playoff odds after. Tax is the marginal tax of the player's CBT charge at the club's payor tier on the Club Ledger's schedule, printed as tax payroll before and after, threshold, bracket and payor tier, never as room under a line. Ability to pay is farm surplus. The Score adds the four with equal weight, 0 to 4. The org trade profile is shown with weight 0. Read from a slim slice of the Franchise board and the CBT sidecar; the daily output is frozen and hashed for one registered read after the 2027 deadline.
entries.formula: Score = Need + Contention + Tax + Ability to pay, each (29 - rank) / 28
entries.origin: Arkmetric rule, original to eephus.io, over numbers the site already serves.

entries.definition: A hitting prospect's projected first-MLB-season K% and BB%, translated from his final pre-debut level-relative MiLB rate. K% is the reliable read (2026-10 fit: r2 0.36); BB% is modest and flagged. Production (OPS / xwOBA) does not translate across the jump and is not projected.
entries.methodology: Matched-pair regression to the mean (the CollegeSavant college-to-Single-A method, applied MiLB-to-MLB): each debuted hitter's final pre-debut level-relative rate (k_rel / bb_rel vs the level mean) is paired with his first-MLB-season rate, and a shrunk slope is fit over the pairs. Leave-one-out validated, 2026-10 fit (n=349): K% LOO MAE 3.9, P10-P90 coverage 0.81, r2 0.36; BB% MAE 2.7, coverage 0.80, r2 0.15 (flagged with *). These are dated readings of the validation block in data/milb_translation.json and move with each refit. The band is the residual spread. OPS and xwOBA were tested and do not translate (r2 ~0.02): first-MLB production is dominated by selection, so only the sticky plate-skill rates are projected. A rate translation, not a value forecast; eFV is the value signal.
entries.formula:
projected first-MLB rate = y_mean + slope x (x - x_mean), where x = the final pre-debut level-relative rate (k_rel / bb_rel vs the level mean) and slope = OLS x n / (n + shrink K), fit on matched pre-debut vs first-MLB-season pairs
band = residual sd around the fit; K% and BB% only, production not translated
entries.example: A AAA bat striking out 4 points below his level's mean projects a first-MLB K% a couple of points better than the debutant average: the shrunk slope keeps only the share of the edge that historically survives the jump.

entries.definition: A reliever's run-prevention skill on a league-relative scale: 100 is an average reliever, 110 is 10 percent better. Built from stabilized strikeout, walk and contact-quality rates, regressed for small samples, anchored to the reliever-only pool. Higher is better. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: A FIP-based skill rate in the ERA+ family, a ratio to the league rather than a z-score. The component rates (K%, BB%, HBP and a heavily regressed home-run rate) are shrunk toward the reliever pool mean by sample size and combined into a sample-shrunk FIP (Skill FIP). REM+ = 100 x pool-average FIP / the reliever's FIP, so a lower FIP scores above 100. The pool is relievers only, so 100 is the average reliever, not the average pitcher. Leverage stays out: gmLI, WPA and Shutdowns minus Meltdowns ride separate Impact columns, because the manager assigns leverage and it does not carry forward as skill.
entries.formula: REM+ = 100 x poolFIP / playerFIP (sample-shrunk FIP; 100 = average reliever)
entries.example: A reliever whose sample-shrunk FIP is 3.20 against a 4.00 reliever-pool mean reads REM+ 125, whatever his gmLI and WPA say.

entries.definition: Team bullpen rating: 100 is an average pen. Relief-innings-weighted REM+ of the pen's relievers. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: Each reliever's REM+ is weighted by his relief innings, so a pen is credited for the quality of the innings it throws, not for how leverage is assigned. Lev Deploy+ weights by innings x gmLI to show how much leverage those innings carried. The board also shows depth (share of above-average arms) and a high-leverage core rating (the top arms by entry leverage).
entries.formula:
Bullpen+ = SUM(relief IP_r x REM+_r) / SUM relief IP_r over the pen's scored relievers
companions: Lev Deploy+ = the same mean weighted by IP x gmLI over gmLI-covered arms (blank when no coverage); depth = share of arms at REM+ >= 100; high-leverage core = mean REM+ of the top 3 arms by gmLI
entries.example: A pen whose top four arms (250 relief IP) average REM+ 112 while the last 150 IP average 92 reads Bullpen+ 105.

entries.definition: Team rotation rating: 100 is an average rotation. Starter-innings-weighted SEM+. On the Team Rotations board in MLB Stats; higher is better. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: Each starter's SEM+ is weighted by his innings as a starter and divided by those innings, so a swingman with 30 innings cannot move the rotation the way a flat average would. Only starters with a scored SEM+ and positive innings enter; the display rounds to a whole point (unrounded as rotation_plus_raw). SEM+ is anchored on the starter pool, so 100 is the average rotation, and Rotation+ inherits SEM+'s shrinkage. Front 3 (mean SEM+ of the three best starters), the count of above-average starters and the durability columns (starter innings, games started) sit beside it as context. Built by starter_export.py from the StatsAPI season pitching leaderboard via sem_plus.score_pool and sem_plus.team_rotation.
entries.formula: Rotation+ = sum(SEM+ x starter IP) / sum(starter IP), over starters with a scored SEM+ (100 = average rotation)

entries.definition: Team lineup rating: 100 is an average offense. Plate-appearance-weighted HEM+ of the club's hitters. On the Team Lineups board in MLB Stats; higher is better. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: Each hitter's HEM+ is weighted by his plate appearances and divided by those plate appearances, so playing time sets how much a bat counts without entering the rate: a bench bat with 40 trips cannot carry a lineup. Only hitters with a scored HEM+ and positive PA enter; the display rounds to a whole point (unrounded as offense_plus_raw). HEM+ is anchored on the hitter pool, so 100 is the average lineup. It rides HEM+'s wider display spread (HEM+ is stretched to the wRC+ deviation width by a fixed monotone gain), so read it at roughly 16 points per standard deviation, not the tighter REM+ / SEM+ bands. Heart 3 (top three regulars by HEM+), the count of above-average hitters and team PA are context; the batting orders against right- and left-handed pitching and the bench list are display only. Built by hitter_export.py via hem_plus.score_pool and hem_plus.team_offense.
entries.formula: Offense+ = sum(HEM+ x PA) / sum(PA), over hitters with a scored HEM+ (100 = average lineup)

entries.definition: HEM+ against one pitcher hand: the hitter's season HEM+ moved by his platoon gap against left- or right-handed pitching, on the same scale. The lead number on the Lineup Charts cards in MLB Stats under the vs LHP / vs RHP toggle, with the season HEM+ beside it, dim. Higher is better.
entries.methodology:
Each hand's counting line comes from the StatsAPI split feed (sitCodes vl and vr, every MLB hitter). The level is the hitter's season shrunk wOBA, the number his season HEM+ is scaled from; the split only sets the gap between his two hands. His ratio of wOBA against left-handers to wOBA against right-handers is regressed toward this season's league ratio for his bat side (left, right or switch), by a constant fitted once on 2016 to 2018, where a hitter's own gap barely carried from one season to the next. So a regular's own gap carries about 5 percent of the weight and the league gap for his side the rest. The two hand numbers average back to his season HEM+, weighted by plate appearances. The anchor is the SEASON hitter pool, not a per-hand pool, so the league platoon effect survives: a left-handed hitter's vs-LHP number reads below his season number.

On the card: a number on fewer than 100 plate appearances against the hand is dimmed with a dotted underline (mostly the league gap). A hitter with no line against the hand shows his season HEM+ with a small s. The batting order is still built on season HEM+ and the handedness stagger; the per-hand number does not reorder it. Positions come from 2026 MLB fielding innings.

The Bench block lists active non-pitcher bats outside the nine, sorted by the per-hand number (lines at 100+ PA first). The Out block lists regulars (the club's top nine by season plate appearances) not on the active roster, labelled from MLB's cached 40-man status: IL-10, IL-60, Minors, Bereavement, Off 40-man, or Not active when the cache gives no reason. A day-to-day injury that is not a roster move does not appear.
entries.formula: vs-hand HEM+ = 100 + 2.28 x (100 x season shrunk wOBA x m / season pool wOBA - 100), where m sets the hand's share of the regressed platoon ratio and the two hands' m average to 1 over the hitter's plate appearances

entries.definition: The PLT chip on a Lineup Charts card: a bench bat with the platoon edge against the toggled pitcher hand, at a position he has played, where the starter he sits behind lacks it, and whose vs-hand HEM+ beats the starter's by 5+ with 100+ plate appearances each against that hand. A read of this season's splits, not a lineup recommendation.
entries.methodology:
All six hold for opposing hand h, starter S and bench bat B: (1) S bats from the same side as h and does not switch-hit; (2) B bats from the other side or switch-hits; (3) B has 30+ 2026 MLB innings at S's primary position (the fielding position with the most innings, or DH when MLB lists the player as DH; DH is open to every non-pitcher); (4) both have a real vs-hand HEM+ against h, never a season fallback; (5) both have 100+ plate appearances against h; (6) B's vs-hand HEM+ minus S's is 5 or more.

The 100-PA floor is the page's thin-sample floor. The margin comes from one recipe: take every hitter with a vs-hand HEM+ on both hands, group them by bat side and by plate appearances against left-handers (20 to 59, 60 to 99, 100 to 149, 150 to 249, 250+; groups of 8 or more), measure the spread (standard deviation) of vs-LHP minus vs-RHP in each group, and round the smallest spread up to a multiple of 5. Under the earlier per-hand construction the spreads ran 13.5 to 22.3 and the margin was 15. Under the current one they run 1.24 to 3.59 over 644 hitters, so the margin is 5: each hitter's own platoon gap is now regressed hard toward the league gap for his bat side, and his two hand numbers differ mostly by that league gap. The spread measures how far one hitter's two hand numbers move apart, not the noise in comparing two players, so the margin is a display threshold, not a significance test. A marked gap mostly reflects the two players' season levels and bat sides and understates the raw split. The thresholds and the margin's derivation ship in the payload (lineup_cards.constants and lineup_cards.margin_basis). Display only: it never changes the batting order, Offense+ or any betting input.
entries.formula: PLT when S lacks the edge vs h, B holds it, B has 30+ innings at S's position (DH open), both have 100+ PA vs h, and vsHEM+(B, h) - vsHEM+(S, h) >= 5, where 5 is the smallest within-side, within-band SD of (vsHEM+ vs LHP - vsHEM+ vs RHP) rounded up to a multiple of 5

entries.definition: A fielder's sprint speed as a range read on the 100 + 10z scale (100 = league-average position player, ten points = one standard deviation). A chip on Position Fit rows in the Pitcher Alchemy Lab, shown ONLY for left-field and center-field destinations. Display only; never enters the position-fit model.
entries.methodology:
Sprint speed from the current-season Statcast leaderboard, falling back one season when a player has no current tracking (the chip names the season). Standardized against that season's MLB position-player pool: Rng+ = 100 + 10 x z(ft/s). The chip also shows the player's percentile among incumbents at the destination (400+ innings there over the trailing three seasons).

Why only LF and CF. Against OAA per 1,000 innings at the position played (400+ innings, 2016-2026), sprint speed tracks range in center field at r = +0.428 (95% CI +0.342 to +0.507) and in left field at r = +0.416 (+0.323 to +0.501). Right field clears the headline bar at r = +0.269 (+0.167 to +0.365) but is excluded, because the signal comes from displaced center fielders: right fielders with under 100 career center-field innings read r = +0.075 (-0.111 to +0.256), lower bound under the +0.15 bar. Left field survives the same pure-corner test (+0.359, +0.163 to +0.528, n = 89). Shortstop (-0.020, -0.122 to +0.083) and third base (-0.004, -0.108 to +0.100) show no signal, so no infield chip renders.

Nothing reaches the model: positional_fit's field() has no sprint term, because OAA already contains the legs (the same reason the arm feature was rejected). build_site.py decides which positions qualify and bakes every number; assets/pal.js computes none of it.
entries.formula: Rng+ = 100 + 10 x z(sprint speed, ft/s) against the current-season MLB position-player pool; shipped for LF and CF destinations only

entries.definition: The average Leverage Index at the moment a reliever enters: how high-pressure his usage is, set mostly by the manager. About 1.0 is average; closers run high, mop-up arms low.
entries.methodology: Computed from the MLB win-probability feed: the Leverage Index of the play where the reliever enters, averaged across his appearances. Deployment, not skill, so REM+ keeps it in a separate column.

entries.definition: Relief-entry-weighted average gmLI over the trailing three seasons, with the pool percentile. Deployment context, not skill. About 1.0 is average; established high-leverage arms run 1.5 and up.
entries.methodology: Each season's gmLI (entry Leverage Index from the MLB win-probability feed) averaged over the trailing three seasons, weighted by relief entries. Year-over-year gmLI rank correlation on qualified relievers is 0.47 pooled over 2018-2025 (ex-2020), with within-season split-half stability of 0.53, so leverage assignment persists. Under 2 seasons or 60 relief entries in the window carries a provisional mark. Never feeds REM+.
entries.formula:
gmLI 3yr = SUM(entries_s x gmLI_s) / SUM entries_s over the trailing three seasons, shown with the pool percentile
provisional under 2 seasons or 60 relief entries in the window
entries.example: Seasons at gmLI 1.85 (62 entries), 1.60 (58) and 1.10 (20 so far) average (1.85x62 + 1.60x58 + 1.10x20) / 140 = 1.64.

entries.definition: The realized, leverage-weighted value a reliever produced this season, 100-anchored (100 = average, higher is more value). The deployment-value companion to REM+: REM+ is run-prevention skill with leverage held out; RIV+ credits the wins a reliever added in the leverage he was given. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
A WPA-primary composite standardized over the season's reliever pool and reported as 100 + 10z. The composite is 70 percent Win Probability Added (which weights every out by the leverage of the moment) and 30 percent shutdowns minus meltdowns (a lower-variance count of high-impact outings). Leverage enters only through value produced, never as credit for the role.

A realized-value measure, not a repeatable skill: its year-over-year rank correlation is 0.20 against 0.36 for REM+ (2018-2025, ex-2020; evaluation v2, data/riv_plus_eval.json generated 2026-08-30), which is why leverage stays out of REM+ and rides here. It is not shown to track free-agent pay any better than REM+: on 232 matched reliever signings the rank correlation with AAV is 0.573 for RIV+ against 0.567 for REM+ (data/riv_market_regate_eval.json, 2026-09-18 re-gate), a gap of 0.005 inside a noise floor of 0.086. Read it as a record, not a forecast: in the same re-gate this season's REM+ predicted next season's RIV+ better than this season's RIV+ did, so the column does not carry forward.
entries.formula:
z = 0.70 x z(WPA) + 0.30 x z(shutdowns - meltdowns), re-standardized on the blend's own pool spread
RIV+ = 100 + 10 x z, over relievers with a leverage feed only
entries.example: A closer at +3.5 WPA with 38 shutdowns and 6 meltdowns lands about two blended standard deviations up: RIV+ near 120. A same-REM+ arm used in mop-up sits in the 90s.

entries.definition: REM+ over the trailing three seasons, innings-weighted. Same run-prevention skill scale (100 = average reliever). A steadier read, not a stronger forecast. On /mlbstats/ the column is the Last 3 window's REM+, the number the Last 3 view prints, shown uncoloured with the percentile inside that window's pool: a value ruler cut on one season's pool does not travel onto a three-season pool.
entries.methodology: Innings-weighted mean of the trailing three seasons' REM+. Single reliever seasons are volatile (within-season split-half REM+ correlation about 0.34 at 100-150 batters faced). The forward test did not separate it from one season: three-year forward Spearman 0.262 against 0.252 for one year on the same relievers, with the 95% interval on the gap reaching below zero. Ships as a steadiness companion. Since 2026-10-01 the served column reads the Last 3 window file built by tools/mlbstats_window_lab.py, rebuilt nightly; this test stays the record (data/rem_plus_multiyear_eval.json).
entries.formula: REM+ 3yr = SUM(IP_s x REM+_s) / SUM IP_s over the trailing three seasons, shown with the pool percentile

entries.definition: A starting pitcher's run-prevention skill on a 100-anchored scale (100 = the innings-weighted average of starters with 20+ innings, the pool the anchor is built on; 110 = 10 percent better). The starter version of REM+: a sample-shrunk, starter-pool-anchored FIP from strikeouts, walks, hit batters and a heavily regressed home-run rate. Durability (innings, games started, average start length) shows beside it, never inside it. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
Each rate is regressed toward the starter-pool average by sample size (REM+'s empirical-Bayes recipe), turned into a fielding-independent ERA, and expressed as 100 x pool-average Skill FIP / the pitcher's own. The pool is starters only.

Validated out of sample: forward-chained over 2018-2025 (ex-2020), SEM+ predicts a starter's next-year runs-allowed rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.42, beating ERA (0.28; gap confidence floor above zero) and edging its raw-FIP parent (0.38) (data/sem_plus_eval.json, generated 2026-08-30). A ground-ball-adjusted variant did not beat plain FIP out of sample. Quality starts and times-through-order are not in the source feed, so average start length carries the durability read.
entries.formula:
SEM+ = 100 x starter-pool FIP / player's sample-shrunk FIP
component K / BB / HBP rates shrunk to the starter-pool mean by sample size, the HR rate heavily regressed, recombined as a fielding-independent ERA; 100 = the innings-weighted average Skill FIP of starters with 20+ innings
entries.example: A starter at a 3.40 sample-shrunk FIP against a 4.10 starter pool reads SEM+ 121. The same raw 3.40 over 50 innings is pulled toward the pool first and reads lower.

entries.definition: A pitch rate against the average for the same role: 100 is average, 110 is 10 percent more pitches, 90 is 10 percent fewer. Pitchers compare on P/IP with starters and relievers kept apart; hitters on P/PA. It describes how a player uses pitches. It is not a forecast and carries no good or bad colour.
entries.methodology: PAR = 100 x the player's rate / the league rate for the same role and season. League rates are pooled (all pitches over all innings, or over all plate appearances), never an average of player rates. MLB starters compare with every start in the league, relievers with every relief outing. Prospects compare with their own level in the same season, and only in league-seasons where MLB's feed logged every pitch (the list is in data/pitch_rates.json); older lines show no PAR. Team PAR compares a club's lineup, rotation or bullpen with the average of the 30 clubs. The tooltip gives the gap in pitches. The scale is a plain ratio like FIP-, so a point is one percent on every board; it is not the 100 + 10z ruler of DEM+.
entries.formula: PAR = 100 x player rate / league rate for the role (P/IP for pitchers, P/PA for hitters), rounded to the nearest point
entries.example: A starter at 15.6 P/IP in a season when starts averaged 16.4: PAR = 100 x 15.6 / 16.4 = 95, or 0.8 fewer pitches an inning.

entries.definition: A hitter's offensive-rate skill on a 100-anchored scale (100 = the plate-appearance-weighted average of hitters with 50+ plate appearances, the pool the anchor is built on), stretched to the wRC+ convention so the league shows real separation (about 15 points per standard deviation). The hitter version of REM+ / SEM+: a sample-shrunk, hitter-pool-anchored wOBA from unintentional walks, hit-by-pitches, singles, doubles, triples and home runs. Volume, baserunning and the slash line show beside it, never inside it. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology:
Each wOBA component rate is regressed toward the hitter-pool average by sample size (REM+'s empirical-Bayes recipe, with a slower pull for extra-base hits, which stabilize late), recombined with one fixed set of FanGraphs-family linear weights (uBB 0.69, HBP 0.72, 1B 0.89, 2B 1.27, 3B 1.62, HR 2.10, the fa_config vintage, applied to every season; FanGraphs publishes season-specific weights), and re-anchored so the pool average scores 100. HEM+ = 100 x shrunk player wOBA / pool wOBA, then stretched: a ratio-to-league index in the wRC+ / OPS+ family, not a z-score.

Validated out of sample: forward-chained over 2012-2024 (ex-2020), HEM+ predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.41, beating batting average (0.23; gap confidence floor above zero) and even with its raw-wOBA parent (0.41) and with OPS (0.41).
