Volume, baserunning and defense stay out of the rate. Accountability artifact: data/hem_plus_eval.json. The stretch is a fixed monotone gain (HEM_SPREAD_GAIN 2.28) that preserves rank exactly, so the validation is unchanged.
entries.formula:
HEM+ = 100 + 2.28 x (100 x shrunk wOBA / pool wOBA - 100)
shrunk wOBA: each component rate (uBB, HBP, 1B, 2B, 3B, HR) regressed to the hitter-pool mean by sample size (slower for extra-base hits), recombined with fixed linear weights 0.69 / 0.72 / 0.89 / 1.27 / 1.62 / 2.10
the 2.28 gain (HEM_SPREAD_GAIN) is a fixed monotone stretch to the wRC+ deviation width; rank order is untouched
entries.example: A hitter whose shrunk wOBA is .365 against a .330 pool sits 10.6 percent above it: 100 + 2.28 x 10.6 = 124.

entries.definition: A hitter's HEM+ over the trailing three seasons, plate-appearance-weighted: a steadier talent read than one season, on the HEM+ scale. On /mlbstats/ the column is the Last 3 window's HEM+, the number the Last 3 view prints, shown uncoloured with the percentile inside that window's pool: a value ruler cut on one season's pool does not travel onto a three-season pool.
entries.methodology: PA-weighted mean of the hitter's HEM+ across the last three seasons (2024-2026), so a partial current season counts by its plate appearances. Established = 2+ seasons and 600+ PA in the window; otherwise provisional. Forward-chained over 2012-2024 (ex-2020), the 3-year read predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.45 against 0.43 for one season on the same hitters, with the same-set gap confidence floor above zero. Accountability artifact: data/hem_plus_multiyear_eval.json. Since 2026-10-01 the served column reads the Last 3 window file built by tools/mlbstats_window_lab.py, rebuilt nightly; this test stays the record (data/hem_plus_multiyear_eval.json).
entries.formula:
HEM+ (3yr) = SUM(PA_s x HEM+_s) / SUM PA_s over the trailing three seasons
established = 2+ seasons and 600+ PA in the window, else provisional

entries.definition: WAR/PA+ with the rate regressed toward the league rate by plate appearances taken, so a hot 100-PA line does not outrank a strong full season. Same 100-anchored, ten-points-per-standard-deviation scale, rebuilt on the regressed pool. Sort the board on this; read what a hitter banked on plain WAR/PA+. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
WAR/PA+ with one change first: the rate is pulled toward the pool rate in proportion to how little the player played, with the pool's median plate-appearance count as the halfway point, and only then indexed. A player at the median sits halfway between his own rate and the league's; a full season barely moves; a player just over the display gate moves a long way. The unadjusted column ranks a hot short sample above a good full season, which is true of what was banked but not what most readers want when they sort.

The scale is rebuilt on the regressed pool, so ten points is still one standard deviation of the hitter pool. Keeping the old spread after shrinking the numerator was a shipped defect: the index stopped being the scale it named.

Not a forecast. On the forward test the pre-registered shrink rule fired for this pool (paired gap 0.0148, 95 percent interval 0.01 to 0.0195), but split into playing-time thirds the gap clears zero only in the high-volume third, so most of the pooled gain is the shrink standing in for sample size rather than better skill measurement. Measurement ledger: data/war_rate_plus_eval.json.
entries.formula:
shrunk rate = (batting WAR + pool rate x K) / (PA + K), K = the pool's MEDIAN PA
WAR/PA+ (adj) = 100 + 10 x (shrunk rate - shrunk-pool mean) / shrunk-pool sd, with the scale REBUILT on the shrunk pool
entries.example: A 110-PA hot streak at an unadjusted 125 keeps w = 110 / (110 + K) of its own rate and lands in the mid-100s on the rebuilt scale; a 600-PA season at 120 barely moves.

entries.definition: Starter WAR/IP+ with the rate regressed toward the starter pool rate by innings, so a short hot stretch does not outrank a full season. Same starter-anchored, ten-points-per-standard-deviation scale, rebuilt on the regressed pool. Not comparable with the reliever board's column.
entries.methodology:
Starter WAR/IP+ with one change first: the rate is pulled toward the pool rate in proportion to how little the player played, with the pool's median innings count as the halfway point, and only then indexed. A player at the median sits halfway between his own rate and the league's; a full season barely moves; a player just over the display gate moves a long way. The unadjusted column ranks a hot short sample above a good full season, which is true of what was banked but not what most readers want when they sort.

The scale is rebuilt on the regressed pool, so ten points is still one standard deviation of the starter pool. Keeping the old spread after shrinking the numerator was a shipped defect: the index stopped being the scale it named.

Not a forecast. The pre-registered shrink rule did not fire for this pool (paired gap 0.0048, 95 percent interval -0.0006 to 0.01), and split into playing-time thirds the gap clears zero in none of them. Measurement ledger: data/war_rate_plus_eval.json.
entries.formula:
shrunk rate = (pitching WAR + starter-pool rate x K) / (IP + K), K = the starter pool's MEDIAN IP
WAR/IP+ (SP, adj) = 100 + 10 x (shrunk rate - shrunk-pool mean) / shrunk-pool sd, scale rebuilt on the shrunk pool
entries.example: A 45-IP hot stretch at an unadjusted 121 keeps w = 45 / (45 + K) of its rate and settles in the mid-100s; a 190-IP season at 118 holds most of its edge.

entries.definition: Reliever WAR/IP+ with the rate regressed toward the reliever pool rate by innings. The column where the adjustment matters most: relief innings are small enough that a good month can top the unadjusted board. Same reliever-anchored, ten-points-per-standard-deviation scale, rebuilt on the regressed pool. Not comparable with the starter board's column.
entries.methodology:
Reliever WAR/IP+ with one change first: the rate is pulled toward the pool rate in proportion to how little the player played, with the pool's median innings count as the halfway point, and only then indexed. A player at the median sits halfway between his own rate and the league's; a full season barely moves; a player just over the display gate moves a long way. The unadjusted column ranks a hot short sample above a good full season, which is true of what was banked but not what most readers want when they sort.

The scale is rebuilt on the regressed pool, so ten points is still one standard deviation of the reliever pool. Keeping the old spread after shrinking the numerator was a shipped defect: the index stopped being the scale it named.

Not a forecast. The pre-registered shrink rule did not fire for this pool on eWAR (paired gap 0.002, 95 percent interval -0.0016 to 0.0055), and split into playing-time thirds the gap clears zero in none of them. Measurement ledger: data/war_rate_plus_eval.json.
entries.formula:
shrunk rate = (pitching WAR + reliever-pool rate x K) / (IP + K), K = the reliever pool's MEDIAN IP
WAR/IP+ (RP, adj) = 100 + 10 x (shrunk rate - shrunk-pool mean) / shrunk-pool sd, scale rebuilt on the shrunk pool
entries.example: A 32-IP hot half at an unadjusted 128 keeps w = 32 / (32 + K) of its rate and reads near 110; a 70-IP season at 124 holds most of its edge.

entries.definition: Total value a hitter banked per plate appearance, on a 100-anchored scale where ten points is one standard deviation of the hitter pool. Batting WAR / PA (eWAR basis; the batting side equals bWAR, so this index did not move at the 2026-09 epoch). HEM+ is offensive rate alone; WAR/PA+ adds fielding, baserunning and the positional adjustment, so a good defender at a hard position can sit well above his HEM+ and a DH well below. Needs 100 plate appearances. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
Anchored at 100 with ten points per standard deviation of the anchor pool (hitters with 50+ PA). A different ruler from the HEM+ / SEM+ / REM+ columns beside it, which are ratios to the pool average (a point is about one percent): 120 is a top-2.5-percent season, 80 a bottom-2.5-percent one. A ratio index cannot be built here, because the league-average WAR per plate appearance is barely above zero and individual values go negative.

Two volume floors: everyone at or above the pool floor sets the pool mean and spread; only players at 100 plate appearances or more get a published value. The value is not shrunk and not clamped, so it reads what the player banked, tail included; at the display gate the sample is still small, which is why the default board view applies its qualified filter.

Source: eWAR, the site-wide series (Baseball-Reference run frame with pitching re-priced on FIP; the batting side equals bWAR), with batting and pitching read from separate keys and never summed. A two-way player carries a batting index on the hitter board and a pitching index on a pitcher board.

Forward-checked out of sample, and it lost. Over 2012-2025 (ex-2020) and 3845 year-to-year pairs, WAR/PA+ predicts next season's WAR rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.3711, while plain season WAR predicts the same thing at 0.4058 (measured on eWAR, which on the batting side reads the same as bWAR). It is not noise (a zero-information control on the same pairs scores 0.0011); a season of playing time is itself a talent signal that a per-trip rate discards. Registered as a descriptive display index with no validated verdict and no eval artifact. It reads what a player banked, not a forecast. Measurement ledger: data/war_rate_plus_eval.json.
entries.formula:
rate = batting WAR / PA (anchor pool: hitters with 50+ PA)
WAR/PA+ = 100 + 10 x (rate - pool mean) / pool sd; published at 100+ PA, no shrink, no clamp
entries.example: 4.0 batting WAR in 600 PA is 0.0067 WAR per trip; against a pool mean near 0.002 and sd near 0.0025 that is about two standard deviations up, WAR/PA+ around 119.

entries.definition: A hitter's WAR/PA+ over the trailing three seasons, weighted by plate appearances. Steadier than one season, because a WAR rate carries fielding and baserunning on top of the bat. Each season is scored against its own pool and the seasons are weighted by plate appearances, so 100 is the average of those pools; the shipped column is NARROWER than one season (standard deviation 6.49 against 8.96 on the 450 hitters carrying both), so ten points here is not one standard deviation. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93, a ladder cut on the one-season pool: FILED as a defect 2026-09-17, because removing a served colour is a separate named change.
entries.methodology:
PA-weighted mean of the single-season WAR/PA+ across the trailing three seasons. Established = two or more seasons and 600 plate appearances in the window; otherwise provisional (star).

The column is a FROZEN vintage: values are read verbatim from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json and never recomputed at build, so a same-day one-year value can sit beside a three-year value frozen weeks earlier, and a player who entered the pool after that file was generated is blank. The payload carries the generation date.

Forward-checked: over 3845 pairs the three-year read predicts next season's WAR rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.4022 against 0.3711 for one season on the same players, gap confidence floor above zero.

Measured on the same eWAR series as the one-year WAR/PA+ beside it, so the two columns share one scale (the lab was re-pointed from bWAR on 2026-09-11).
entries.formula:
WAR/PA+ (3yr) = SUM(PA_s x WAR/PA+_s) / SUM PA_s over the trailing three seasons, values read frozen from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json
established = 2+ seasons and 600+ PA in the window, else a provisional star
entries.example: Seasons at 118 (650 PA), 104 (600 PA) and 92 (250 PA of a partial current year) blend to (118x650 + 104x600 + 92x250) / 1500 = 108.

entries.definition: Value a starting pitcher banked per inning, on a 100-anchored scale where ten points is one standard deviation of the STARTER pool. Pitching WAR / IP, anchored on starters only (eWAR basis: FIP re-priced within role from the 2026-09 epoch). SEM+ is run-prevention rate alone; this adds workload. Not comparable with the reliever board's WAR/IP+ (relievers bank more WAR per inning at equal talent); the pools are never merged. Needs 40 innings. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
Anchored at 100 with ten points per standard deviation of the anchor pool (starters with 20+ innings). A different ruler from the HEM+ / SEM+ / REM+ columns beside it, which are ratios to the pool average (a point is about one percent): 120 is a top-2.5-percent season, 80 a bottom-2.5-percent one. A ratio index cannot be built here, because the league-average WAR per inning is barely above zero and individual values go negative.

Two volume floors: everyone at or above the pool floor sets the pool mean and spread; only players at 40 innings or more get a published value. The value is not shrunk and not clamped, so it reads what the player banked, tail included; at the display gate the sample is still small, which is why the default board view applies its qualified filter.

Source: eWAR, the site-wide series (Baseball-Reference run frame with pitching re-priced on FIP within role), with batting and pitching read from separate keys and never summed. A two-way player carries a batting index on the hitter board and a pitching index on a pitcher board.

Forward-checked out of sample on eWAR, and it does not win. Over 2012-2025 (ex-2020) and 1396 pairs, starter WAR/IP+ predicts next season's WAR rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.4726. That is ahead of plain season WAR (0.4496, paired gap floor above zero) but level with the same rate left unstandardized (0.4705, gap floor below zero), so the within-season scaling adds nothing measurable. It is not noise (a zero-information control on the same pairs scores 0.0167). Registered as a descriptive display index with no validated verdict and no eval artifact. It reads what a player banked, not a forecast. Measurement ledger: data/war_rate_plus_eval.json.
entries.formula:
rate = pitching WAR / IP (anchor pool: starters with 20+ IP)
WAR/IP+ (SP) = 100 + 10 x (rate - starter-pool mean) / starter-pool sd; published at 40+ IP, no shrink, no clamp; never pooled with the reliever board
entries.example: 4.5 pitching WAR over 180 IP is 0.025 WAR per inning; against a starter-pool mean near 0.012 and sd near 0.011 that is a bit over one standard deviation up, WAR/IP+ around 112.

entries.definition: A starter's WAR/IP+ over the trailing three seasons, innings-weighted. Same starter-anchored, ten-points-per-standard-deviation scale.
entries.methodology:
Innings-weighted mean of the single-season starter WAR/IP+ across the trailing three seasons. Established = two or more seasons and 120 innings in the window; otherwise provisional (star).

The column is a FROZEN vintage: values are read verbatim from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json and never recomputed at build, so a same-day one-year value can sit beside a three-year value frozen weeks earlier, and a player who entered the pool after that file was generated is blank. The payload carries the generation date.

Forward-checked and unresolved: over 1396 pairs the three-year read predicts next season's WAR rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.4766 against 0.4726 for one season, and the paired gap does not clear zero. A longer window on the same scale, not a better forecast.

Measured on the same eWAR series as the one-year WAR/IP+ beside it, so the two columns share one scale (the lab was re-pointed from bWAR on 2026-09-11).
entries.formula:
WAR/IP+ (SP, 3yr) = SUM(IP_s x WAR/IP+_s) / SUM IP_s over the trailing three seasons, values read frozen from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json
established = 2+ seasons and 120+ IP in the window, else a provisional star

entries.definition: Value a reliever banked per inning, on a 100-anchored scale where ten points is one standard deviation of the RELIEVER pool. Pitching WAR / IP, anchored on relievers only (eWAR basis: FIP re-priced within role from the 2026-09 epoch). Not comparable with the starter board's WAR/IP+; the pools are never merged. Unlike REM+ it is not leverage-blind: eWAR keeps B-Ref's reliever leverage chaining (the FIP re-pricing replaces the runs component, not the leverage adjustment); gmLI and WPA still carry the deployment story. Needs 30 innings. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.

A ratio index cannot be built here, because the league-average WAR per inning is barely above zero and individual values go negative.

The value is not shrunk and not clamped, so it reads what the player banked, tail included; at the display gate the sample is still small, which is why the default board view applies its qualified filter.

Source: eWAR, the site-wide series (Baseball-Reference run frame with pitching re-priced on FIP within role), with batting and pitching read from separate keys and never summed. A two-way player carries a batting index on the hitter board and a pitching index on a pitcher board.

Forward-checked out of sample on eWAR, and it does not win. Over 2012-2025 (ex-2020) and 1621 pairs, reliever WAR/IP+ predicts next season's WAR rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.2323, level with plain season WAR (0.2267) and with the same rate left unstandardized (0.2319); neither paired gap clears zero. WAR/IP+ (RP) = 100 + 10 x (rate - reliever-pool mean) / reliever-pool sd; published at 30+ IP, no shrink, no clamp; never pooled with the starter board
entries.example: 2.4 pitching WAR in 65 IP is 0.037 WAR per inning; against a reliever-pool mean near 0.008 and sd near 0.014 that is about two standard deviations up, WAR/IP+ around 121.

entries.definition: A reliever's WAR/IP+ over the trailing three seasons, innings-weighted. Same reliever-anchored, ten-points-per-standard-deviation scale.
entries.methodology:
Innings-weighted mean of the single-season reliever WAR/IP+ across the trailing three seasons. Established = two or more seasons and 40 innings in the window; otherwise provisional (star).

The column is a FROZEN vintage: values are read verbatim from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json and never recomputed at build, so a same-day one-year value can sit beside a three-year value frozen weeks earlier, and a player who entered the pool after that file was generated is blank. Measured on the same eWAR series as the one-year WAR/IP+ beside it, so the two columns share one scale (the lab was re-pointed from bWAR on 2026-09-11).

WAR/IP+ (RP, 3yr) = SUM(IP_s x WAR/IP+_s) / SUM IP_s over the trailing three seasons, values read frozen from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json

entries.example: Seasons at 115 (62 IP), 96 (58 IP) and 108 (24 IP so far) blend to (115x62 + 96x58 + 108x24) / 144 = 106.

entries.definition: A hitter's DESERVED offensive rate on the HEM+ scale: HEM+ computed from Savant expected wOBA (xwOBA) instead of results, so it reads contact quality rather than where the balls fell. Luck = Savant xwOBA minus wOBA, in wOBA points. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: xHEM+ = 100 x the hitter's Savant xwOBA / the PA-weighted pool average, on the HEM+ scale. xwOBA is built from each batted ball's launch conditions (exit velocity and angle), which strips BABIP and sequencing luck. Forward-chained over seven season-pairs 2016-2025 (ex-2020, 1871 pairs), the column as served predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.46 against 0.41 for actual wOBA, gap confidence floor 0.024 above zero (the 2026-09-18 re-gate on the served construction, data/xhem_served_regate_eval.json). The original gate's eval-normalized construction reads 0.4543 against 0.4108 on the same pairs; that figure is a labelled reproduction, not the served column's number. A companion for tracked hitters (Statcast is MLB-only; 100+ tracked PA), not the population-complete HEM+. Luck > 0: under-performing his contact; < 0: over-performing. Luck is read on the unshrunk pair, not as xHEM+ minus HEM+: HEM+ is shrunk toward the pool and xHEM+ is not, so that difference partly measured the shrink and disagreed in sign with xwOBA minus wOBA for 126 of 460 hitters on 2026-09-24. Accountability artifact: data/xhem_served_regate_eval.json (the reproduction reference stays in data/xhem_plus_eval.json).
entries.formula:
xHEM+ = 100 + 2.28 x (100 x player xwOBA / PA-weighted tracked-pool xwOBA - 100) (tracked hitters, 100+ Savant PA)
Luck = Savant xwOBA - Savant wOBA, in wOBA points
entries.example: A .352 xwOBA against a .320 tracked pool reads xHEM+ 123. With an actual wOBA of .322, Luck is +.030: his contact deserved more.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: The site's single-number read on a hitter's NEXT-year offense: a 70/30 blend of Savant xwOBA and the HEM+ skill core, on the HEM+ scale (100 = the average tracked hitter). xwOBA carries contact quality; the HEM+ leg adds the shrunk plate-discipline signal contact quality misses. Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: Within the season, the hitter's xwOBA and his unrounded HEM+ core are standardized over the tracked pool (100+ Savant PA), combined 70/30, and mapped back onto the HEM+ display scale by the pool's HEM+ location and spread, a rank-preserving transform. Provisional. The 2026-07 gate scored an eval-normalized version of the blend and found an edge over xwOBA alone. The 2026-09-18 re-gate scored the column as the board serves it, on the same forward-chained season-pairs 2016-2025 (ex-2020), and found it not separable from xwOBA alone on next-year wOBA at this sample, under both bootstrap conventions. It is not refuted: the point estimate still leans to the blend. The served column normalizes its two legs over the board's pool rather than the pair set, and the re-gate traces the smaller edge to that difference. The receipt below prints the served figures from data/xhem_served_regate_eval.json. A multi-year decayed candidate also failed its gate. Tracked hitters only.
entries.formula:
blend z = 0.70 x z(Savant xwOBA) + 0.30 x z(unrounded HEM+ core), each standardized over the tracked pool (100+ Savant PA), then re-standardized on the blend's own spread
xHEM+ Blend = the blend mapped back onto the HEM+ ratio display scale by the pool's HEM+ location and spread (rank-preserving)
entries.example: A hitter +1σ on xwOBA and average on the HEM+ core blends to about +0.8σ after re-standardization: mid-110s on the HEM+ scale.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: A read on a hitter's NEXT-year offense that adds Statcast bat tracking to the xHEM+ Blend recipe: Savant xwOBA, the HEM+ skill core and a bat-tracking contact-quality composite (bat speed, squared-up rate, blast rate), on the HEM+ scale (100 = the average hitter in its pool). Coloured on the value ruler at 130 / 120 / 112 / 100 / 88.
entries.methodology: Within the season, each of the three bat-tracking components is standardized over Savant's full bat-tracking leaderboard (hitters with 100+ competitive swings) and the three are averaged into the composite. Over the joined pool (100+ Savant PA, a HEM+ core, and a bat-tracking row at the swing floor), xwOBA, the unrounded HEM+ core and the composite are standardized and combined 59.5 / 25.5 / 15, re-standardized on the blend's own spread and mapped onto the HEM+ display scale by the pool's HEM+ location and spread, a rank-preserving transform. Provisional. A pre-registered re-read scored the column exactly as the board serves it (the integers, built on the served pools) over two forward season-pairs, 2024 to 2025 and 2025 to 2026, and found it orders next-year wOBA ahead of the served xHEM+ Blend under both bootstrap conventions. On the same pairs it is not separable from xwOBA alone. The re-read covers hitters with 200+ PA in both seasons while the board shows hitters from 100 PA, and two seasons is a small sample. The receipt below prints the figures from data/bat_tracking_served_eval.json. A hitter below the swing floor, or without a bat-tracking row, shows a blank cell.
entries.formula:
BT composite = mean of z(bat speed), z(squared-up rate), z(blast rate), each over the season's bat-tracking leaderboard at 100+ competitive swings
blend z = 0.595 x z(Savant xwOBA) + 0.255 x z(unrounded HEM+ core) + 0.15 x z(BT composite), each over the joined pool, then re-standardized on the blend's own spread
BT Blend = the blend mapped back onto the HEM+ ratio display scale by the pool's HEM+ location and spread (rank-preserving)
entries.example: Two hitters with the same xwOBA and HEM+ core split on bat tracking: the one with the faster, more often squared-up swing reads a few points higher on the HEM+ scale.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat and bat-tracking inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: A hitter's projected NEXT-season wOBA: the site's FA-engine Marcel (the engine that prices the FA class board and drives MLB Projections) blended one part in five with the hitter's current-season Statcast xwOBA. Read it like wOBA: ~.310 league average, .370 a star season, .400+ elite.
entries.methodology: The engine projects each wOBA component (walk rate, strikeout rate, isolated power, BABIP, home runs per PA) as a Marcel weighted average of the trailing three seasons (5/3/2 recency, exposure-weighted), regresses each to the league mean, blends ISO toward Savant xISO where tracked, and ages every rate along survivorship-corrected curves; the components reassemble into a wOBA with fixed run-value weights. Validated by the T1-10 projection gate (data/phem_marcel_lite_eval.json): over predictor seasons 2021-2024 (918 out-of-sample pairs) projected wOBA predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.5189 against 0.4939 for the best trailing-average incumbent, paired-bootstrap floor above zero, confirmed under the player-clustered bootstrap. A purpose-built multi-year challenger lost the same gate. The served number then blends that projection with the current season's Savant expected wOBA (xwOBA) at a frozen weight of 0.2, for hitters with 100+ PA on the Savant leaderboard; everyone else keeps the engine projection. The blend passed its registered re-gate (data/pwoba_blend_regate_eval.json): over predictor seasons 2022-2025 and 953 held-out pairs it reads a Spearman rho of 0.5271 against 0.5166 for the engine projection alone, paired-bootstrap floor +0.0019 above zero, +0.0024 under the player-clustered bootstrap. Shown for tracked hitters with 100+ PA over the trailing three seasons; current boards only (a past season has no next season to project).
entries.formula:
each component (BB%, K%, ISO, BABIP, HR/PA) = Marcel(5/3/2 recency, exposure-weighted), regressed to the league mean, ISO blended toward Savant xISO, aged along survivorship-corrected curves
wOBA_proj = the projected components reassembled with fixed run-value weights
pWOBA = 0.8 x wOBA_proj + 0.2 x current-season xwOBA (Savant est_woba, 100+ PA), else wOBA_proj; shown at 100+ PA over the trailing three seasons
entries.example: Trailing component rates worth wOBA .355 / .345 / .330 blend to about .347; the league pull and a year of aging settle the engine near .340, and a current-season xwOBA of .360 lifts pWOBA to 0.8 x .340 + 0.2 x .360 = .344.
entries.origin: Projection column from the site's FA-engine Marcel. The Marcel weighted-rates framework is Tom Tango's; the engine that produces this number (survivorship-corrected aging curves, Savant xISO blend, league re-anchoring) is an Arkmetric, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: SEM+ over the trailing three seasons, innings-weighted. Same scale as SEM+ (100 = the innings-weighted average of starters with 20+ innings). A steadier read, not a stronger forecast. On /mlbstats/ the column is the Last 3 window's SEM+, the number the Last 3 view prints, shown uncoloured with the percentile inside that window's pool: a value ruler cut on one season's pool does not travel onto a three-season pool.
entries.methodology: Innings-weighted mean of the trailing three seasons' SEM+. The forward test did not separate it from one season: three-year forward Spearman 0.425 against 0.410 for one year on the same starters, with the 95% interval on the gap reaching below zero. Ships as a steadiness companion with the numbers published. Since 2026-10-01 the served column reads the Last 3 window file built by tools/mlbstats_window_lab.py, rebuilt nightly; this test stays the record (data/sem_plus_multiyear_eval.json).
entries.formula: SEM+ 3yr = SUM(IP_s x SEM+_s) / SUM IP_s over the trailing three seasons, shown with the pool percentile

entries.definition: The total change in a player's team win probability across every play he was in, credited to the BATTER on offense and the PITCHER on defense (opposite signs on the same play). A counting stat of in-the-moment impact, scaled by the leverage of his spots.
entries.methodology: Summed from the MLB win-probability feed: each play's change in win expectancy, credited to the pitcher on the mound; the batter's credit is the negation on the same play. A run prevented in a tie game in the ninth moves win probability far more than the same out in a blowout, so WPA rewards high-leverage usage as much as performance.
entries.formula:
WPA = SUM of each play's change in team win expectancy over the player's plays; credited to the pitcher on defense, and the batter's credit is the negation of the pitcher's on the same play
per-play home-team win-probability delta, sign-flipped to the involved player's team
entries.example: A go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth might move win probability from 35 to 78 percent: +0.43 WPA to the batter, -0.43 to the pitcher. The same swing in a 10-1 blowout moves a point or two.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Win Probability Added, from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango and coauthors, The Book); implemented by FanGraphs.

entries.definition: Win Probability Added with the leverage of each play divided out, so it measures performance independent of how important the situations were. The leverage-stripped companion to WPA.
entries.origin: Industry metric. WPA divided by leverage index, a context-neutral wins measure from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango).

entries.definition: How important a game situation is, from inning, score, outs and baserunners; 1.0 is average. Below 0.85 is low leverage, 2.0+ high.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Leverage Index, created by Tom Tango (The Book): how much the current game state can swing win probability, 1.0 = average.

entries.definition: Per-appearance reliever outcomes. A Shutdown adds at least 0.06 to the team's win probability in an outing; a Meltdown subtracts at least that much. Shutdowns minus Meltdowns is a cleaner reliever record than saves and holds.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Reliever WPA thresholds proposed by Tom Tango and implemented by FanGraphs.

entries.definition: The bullpen leverage ladder, assigned from entry leverage (gmLI) and usage: Closer finishes games at the highest leverage; High-leverage and Setup pitch the tightest middle innings; Middle relief works average spots; Long and Mop-up cover multi-inning or low-stakes work.
A 0-100 candidate score for how well a current reliever would profile as a starter; higher is a better fit. A screen for candidates, not a probability of success.
entries.methodology: A weighted blend led by arsenal depth (a starter must survive a lineup three times, so a third and fourth pitch matter most), then command (walk rate), fastball reliance, platoon neutrality, contact quality and stuff. Fastball velocity is projected down about 1 mph for the longer role. Weights are literature priors, not fitted. The per-direction backtest does not validate the ranking in this direction: pre-conversion FIT ran against realized WAR change at rho about -0.21 on 25 gated events on the bWAR gate basis, and about +0.024 on the eWAR v2 series this page serves, a change of SIGN on a sample that resolves nothing either way. Read the list as arms with starter traits, not a forecast of who converts.
entries.formula: FIT = weighted blend, literature-prior weights: arsenal depth (largest weight), command (BB%), fastball reliance (penalized), platoon neutrality, contact quality, stuff; fastball velocity projected about -1 mph for the longer role
entries.example: A reliever with four usable pitches, a 6 percent walk rate and modest fastball reliance scores in the 80s.

entries.definition: A 0-100 candidate score for how well a current starter's stuff would play up in one-inning relief; higher is a better fit.
entries.methodology: The traits that hurt a starter help a reliever: a thin, fastball-heavy arsenal that leaks runs the third time through is fine for one inning. The score rewards a dominant putaway pitch, projected relief velocity (about +1 mph in short bursts), stuff quality and times-through-order leakage (the complement of arsenal depth). A display-only projected relief REM+ shows roughly what the arm might post in relief. This direction passes its registered gate: in the per-direction backtest, pre-conversion FIT out-ranked every registered same-event baseline against realized WAR change (rho about +0.29 on 61 gated events on the bWAR gate basis, about +0.271 on the eWAR v2 series this page serves, gap over the best baseline positive at the 95 percent floor). The pass carries a caveat. Every registered baseline assumes a better pre-season means a bigger gain, while a WAR change pays out on a bad one (regression to the mean), and FIT itself scales with starter ERA through its conversion-need term. Sorted on high pre-season ERA, the same 61 gate events rank at about +0.62, above FIT. The gate never tested that reading, so the pass is owed a re-gate at the fWAR season-close epoch.
entries.formula:
FIT = weighted blend: putaway pitch quality, projected relief velocity (about +1 mph in short bursts), stuff quality, times-through-order leakage (the complement of arsenal depth)
companion display: a projected relief REM+, display-only
entries.example: A two-pitch starter with a wipeout slider and a third-time-through collapse scores in the 80s, with a projected relief REM+ near 115 against a starting SEM+ in the 90s.

entries.definition: The model behind the Alchemy Lab: two candidate scores (RP->SP FIT and SP->RP FIT) plus a history of past role conversions that doubles as the backtest. SP->RP passes its registered gate, with a regression-to-the-mean caveat (a sort on high pre-season ERA ranks the same events higher); RP->SP is a structural screen.
entries.methodology:
Conversions are detected from season starting shares across 2018-2026 (a role flip between qualified seasons). The outcome is the change in realized WAR (eWAR basis from the 2026-09 epoch: Baseball-Reference run frame with pitching re-priced on FIP) from the pre-role to the post-role season, scored within each direction and never pooled; a held-the-role label (one full closed season in the new role) is a sensitivity check.

Two bases, and they disagree on reliever-to-starter. The registered gate ran on bWAR (data/pal_eval.json, 2026-07-15): SP to RP +0.2916 on 61 gated events (passes), RP to SP -0.2062 on 25 (fails). Every FIT score, history delta and live rho this module serves is on eWAR v2, where the same backtest returns SP to RP +0.271 and RP to SP +0.024. The reliever-to-starter number changes sign between the gate basis and the served basis on a 25-event sample that resolves nothing; data/pal.json records backtest.gate.same_basis_as_live = false. The SP to RP pass carries a caveat: its registered baselines all assume a better pre-season means a bigger gain, and a sort on high pre-season ERA ranks the same 61 gate events at +0.62, above FIT (the SP->RP FIT entry has the detail). The SP to RP pass carries a caveat: its registered baselines all assume a better pre-season means a bigger gain, and a sort on high pre-season ERA ranks the same 61 gate events at +0.62, above FIT (the SP->RP FIT entry has the detail). The RP to SP list is a structural screen on either basis. The sample is small and selection-biased (only pitchers teams chose to convert), so neither score is a success probability, and the model ships provisional with a downgraded registry verdict.
entries.formula:
two candidate scores: RP->SP FIT and SP->RP FIT, 0-100 weighted blends with literature-prior weights (not fitted)
backtest, per direction and never pooled: rho(pre-conversion FIT, post-role minus pre-role WAR change) over detected role flips 2018-2026; SP->RP passes its gate, RP->SP fails it and ships as a structural screen
entries.example: A fastball-heavy starter with third-time-through leakage scores high on SP->RP FIT and low on arsenal depth; the history tab shows the real conversions the backtest scored.

entries.definition: How many distinct pitches a pitcher throws at least ten percent of the time. The main trait for surviving a lineup more than once, and the core of RP->SP FIT.
A pitcher's decline each time he faces the same lineup in a game. A deep, varied arsenal blunts it; a thin fastball-heavy mix collapses by the third time through. A reliever faces the order once.
entries.origin: Industry concept. The times-through-order penalty, quantified by Mitchel Lichtman and coauthors (The Book).

entries.definition: The change in fastball velocity when a pitcher changes roles: a starter stretching out loses about 1 mph; a pitcher moving to one-inning relief gains about that much. Studies put the central number near 1 mph, larger for pure power arms, so the Lab projects it modestly rather than the three or four of folklore.
A pitcher's best swing-and-miss pitch by whiff rate. A dominant one lets a starter's stuff play up in one-inning relief, so it drives SP->RP FIT.
The gap in OPS allowed to left- versus right-handed hitters. A flat split lets a pitcher face a full lineup, which supports starting; a large split is a conversion blocker.
The non-pitcher positions a player has real game experience at, from MLB and MiLB fielding logs rather than a projected multi-position tag.
entries.methodology: Built from StatsAPI game fielding, not a reported position string. A position counts at 10+ games or 5+ starts there. DH is excluded (not a fielding position). A listed shortstop with real innings at second and third shows all three.
entries.formula: Position qualifies at >= 10 G or >= 5 GS at that spot; DH excluded
entries.example: A shortstop with 40 G at SS, 12 G at 2B, and 6 GS at 3B shows Versa: SS / 2B / 3B.

entries.definition: A draft prospect's board rank as an index (100 = middle of the class, higher = more valued), nudged a few points by a college-performance signal.
entries.methodology: Maps consensus draft rank to roughly 70-130 (best of class near 130, back of the board near 70), on the raw fractional ranks so bunched prospects stay distinct. A z-scored college-performance term moves it up to about six points, then it is clamped. A heuristic stock indicator, not a validated projection. Draft Overperformance, by contrast, compares realized FV to slot after the fact.
entries.formula: DS+ = rank-to-index (about 70-130) + college-performance nudge (up to about +-6), clamped
entries.example: A prospect ranked 8th in a class of 250 with a strong statistical spring might carry a DS+ near 126.

entries.definition: How much better a pitcher holds opposite-handed hitters than same-handed ones, the reverse of the normal platoon pattern. A reverse split supports a full-lineup starter role, because the batters who would platoon against him lose their edge.
entries.methodology: For a right-hander: OPS allowed to righties minus OPS allowed to lefties (mirrored for a lefty). Above zero is a reverse split. The radar flags > 0.03 and extreme at ≥ 0.15, counting only pitchers with 100+ batters faced on the lighter side.
entries.formula: reverse index = own-hand OPS-against minus opposite-hand OPS-against (RHP: vsR minus vsL); reverse if > 0.03; requires >= 100 TBF
entries.example: A righty allowing .720 to righties and .560 to lefties has a reverse index of +0.16.

entries.definition: A 0-100 read on whether a pitching prospect's tools fit a starting or relief role, from scout grades only (arsenal depth and command). A shape screen, not a stuff projection: it flags prospects whose listed role conflicts with their grades.
entries.methodology: Rewards arsenal depth (distinct pitches graded 55+, since a starter needs a third weapon) and command, about 60/40. A high score on a reliever-labeled prospect, or a low score on a starter-labeled one, is flagged as a role mismatch on the PAL Prospect Watch. No minor-league stats; descriptive, not a validated outcome model.
entries.formula: Starter Shape = 0.60 x arsenal-depth score (pitches graded >= 55) + 0.40 x command score, on scout grades only
entries.example: FB 60 / SL 55 / CB 45 / CH 40 with 40 command: thin depth, light command, low Starter Shape; a starter-labeled version is flagged as profiling in relief.

entries.definition: Expected wOBA: what a hitter's contact and plate results are worth from how the ball was struck, without defense and luck.
entries.methodology: Estimates wOBA from contact quality (exit velocity and launch angle) plus strikeouts and walks, at the run value of each outcome. xwOBAcon is the contact-only version. PROSPX prints a different number for MiLB hitters, the site's own estimate from launch speed and angle: see Est. xwOBA (PROSPX).
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant). Displayed here as an estimate.

aliases: Batting Average on Balls In Play
entries.definition: Batting average on balls in play: how often balls put in play become hits. Read as a hot or unlucky line indicator.
entries.methodology: BABIP = (H - HR) / (AB - K - HR + SF). League average is near .300. Large gaps from a hitter's own norm usually regress; speed and hard contact sustain higher marks for some hitters.
entries.origin: Standard sabermetric rate; the DIPS insight that pitchers have limited control over BABIP is due to Voros McCracken.

entries.definition: Vertical approach angle: the steepness of a pitch's descent as it crosses the plate; VAAoe is that angle over expectation given the pitch's release and velocity.
entries.methodology: The angle of the ball's path at the plate. Flatter four-seam approach angles at the top of the zone tend to get more swing-and-miss, so VAA and VAAoe (over expectation, adjusting for release height and velocity) are fastball shape context, not a grade.
entries.origin: Derived here from Statcast pitch tracking (Baseball Savant); the approach-angle family was popularized across the public pitching-analysis community.

entries.definition: Whether a farm's prospects arrive while the big-league core is still under team control. Negative = the farm lands inside the window; positive = help arrives after the core has left for free agency.
entries.methodology: System Duration (etaMean) is the surplus-weighted average arrival season of a farm: each prospect's projected ETA weighted by his expected surplus dollars. The core center (coreCenter) is the WAR-weighted midpoint of the org's controlled-core production over 2027-2031. Window Alignment = etaMean − coreCenter. The arrival curve (etaByYear) shows the share of farm surplus landing each season.
entries.formula:
Window Alignment = etaMean - coreCenter
etaMean = SUM(surplus_i x ETA_i) / SUM surplus_i over the farm's prospects; coreCenter = WAR-weighted midpoint of the org's controlled-core production over 2027-2031
entries.example: A farm arriving (surplus-weighted) in 2028.4 under a core centered on 2029.1 reads -0.7: inside the window. +1.5 means the help arrives after the core has left.

entries.definition: Surplus weighed against its downside. Only the chance of falling short counts as risk; upside does not. Higher Sortino = more expected surplus per unit of downside.
entries.methodology: From the eFV surplus distribution the trade board carries (a p10-p90 fan plus the mean). Downside deviation is the semi-deviation below the mean. Sortino = (mean − p10) / that downside deviation, so a high-floor profile outscores a boom-or-bust one at the same mean. The tooltip adds a risk-adjusted surplus (mean minus half the downside deviation; a display haircut that does not re-rank the board) and the bust probability. Descriptive: it changes no shown surplus.
entries.formula:
DD = sqrt(SUM w_i x min(q_i - mean, 0)^2) over the p10/p25/p50/p75/p90 surplus fan, w = (0.15, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.10)
Sortino = (mean - p10) / max(DD, 0.1), clamped 0-99
tooltip risk-adjusted surplus = mean - 0.5 x DD (local display haircut, never re-ranks)
entries.example: Two prospects at $30M mean: a high-floor profile (p10 $20M, downside deviation $4M) reads Sortino 2.5; a boom-or-bust fan (p10 $5M, downside deviation $14M) reads about 1.8.

entries.definition: A market-structure overlay on a prospect's consensus FV history: candlesticks plus trader-style indicators (momentum, an RSI on grade changes, volatility). Descriptive, not predictive.
entries.methodology: One candle per consensus snapshot: open = prior grade, close = current consensus FV, wick = the range of source grades that period. Momentum = net grade change over the last three intervals. RSI = balance of upgrades to downgrades over recent grade changes only (flat re-confirmations dropped, so a static grade never pins it); above 70 overbought, below 30 oversold. Volatility = standard deviation across sources on the latest grade. Candles need 4+ snapshots and RSI 6+ grade changes, otherwise hidden.
entries.formula:
candle: open = prior consensus FV, close = current consensus FV, wick = that period's source-grade range
momentum = net grade change over the last 3 intervals; RSI = balance of upgrades vs downgrades over recent GRADE CHANGES only (70 overbought / 30 oversold); volatility = sd across sources on the latest grade
gates: 4+ snapshots for candles, 6+ grade changes for RSI
entries.example: Consensus 45 -> 50 -> 55 over three snapshots prints green candles, momentum +10 and an RSI near 70.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Candlestick and RSI conventions are borrowed from financial technical analysis.

entries.definition: A live draft-night board: each pick as it happens, priced against our board and the historical value of the slot, so a reach or a steal shows in surplus dollars.
entries.methodology: During the draft a poller reads the MLB Stats API every minute and writes a read-only feed. Each pick joins our board by name and carries consensus FV, the reach-or-steal gap (spots earlier or later than our board rank; a faller past his rank is a steal for the drafting team), the slot's expected first-six-year WAR from the realized pick-value curve, the slot surplus in dollars, and the signing bonus against slot value. A live view over published models; empty before the draft.
entries.formula:
per pick: reach / steal gap = our board rank - pick number (positive = steal for the drafting team); expected first-6yr WAR = the realized pick-value curve at the slot; slot surplus $ = that WAR through the surplus machinery; signing bonus shown against slot value
feed: MLB Stats API polled every minute on draft night, rendered read-only
entries.example: Our No. 14 prospect going 29th overall reads a 15-spot steal, with the slot's expected first-six-year WAR and surplus beside his consensus FV.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Pick data from the MLB Stats API.

entries.definition: Option sensitivities on a prospect's value: Delta = dollars from a one-grade upgrade; Vega = the dollar swing implied by scouting disagreement; Theta = surplus lost per year of arrival delay.
entries.methodology: All three read off the surplus board's value framework. Delta: change in expected surplus when the grade moves up one full grade (5 FV points), on the FV-to-surplus curve at the prospect's grade, so a jump on the steep part is worth more. Vega: the local slope of that curve times the spread of source grades. Theta: the framework's annual discount applied to expected surplus. Implied volatility is the grade spread itself. Descriptive: no dollar figure changes.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. The Greeks framing is borrowed from options pricing.

entries.definition: The probability a prospect becomes a star: two or more seasons of 4+ WAR during his team-control years. Hitters run higher than pitchers, because a bullpen outcome rarely clears 4 WAR.
entries.methodology: The displayed figure is the FanGraphs 2026 published tier value for the player's FV and role, from the published valuation set. It matches the published table at the published knots (FV 37.5 through 70); between knots it is interpolated, below the lowest knot every grade takes the '35+' value, and above FV 70 the FV 70 value. The in-house mixture also computes a per-player version from the outcome-bucket distribution (per-season WAR profile per bucket, chance of 2+ control seasons at 4+ WAR, weighted by bucket odds, starter and reliever paths blended for pitchers). That version runs below the published tiers under the current bust-heavy anchors, so it is a diagnostic being calibrated toward them, not a replacement.
entries.formula:
star = 2+ seasons of 4+ WAR during the team-control years
displayed value = the FanGraphs 2026 published tier value at the player's FV and role, linearly interpolated between knots and clamped at FV 37.5 and 70
diagnostic model version = SUM_bucket P(bucket | FV) x P(2+ control seasons >= 4 WAR | bucket WAR profile), starter and reliever paths blended for pitchers
entries.example: A FV 60 hitter shows the published FV 60 hitter tier; a FV 60 pitcher shows a lower one. A FV 52 hitter shows the value interpolated between the 50 and 55 knots.
entries.origin: Published star-odds tiers from FanGraphs 2026; the per-player mixture model is Arkmetric, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The share of a prospect's grade value that comes from the chance of UPGRADING before he graduates, rather than from the likeliest outcome at today's grade. A low FV is worth more than its modal result because it can still improve.
entries.methodology: A role-split absorbing Markov chain over FV tiers 35-70 plus graduated and out, with an annual step estimated from dated grade history (FanGraphs and MLB Pipeline pooled to one grade per player per year, Laplace-smoothed). Graduation is a real MLB debut; out is a washed-out player; a still-active player's last observed year is censored. total = expected payoff under the full chain; intrinsic = payoff with the grade frozen; option = total − intrinsic; PLUS% = option / total. Payoff is the clemens_2026 table value of the grade a player graduates from. Low tiers are option-rich (a 45 FV hitter runs about 60 percent); high grades run low or negative, because mobility at the top is mostly downgrade risk and the top-tier samples are thin. Provisional and descriptive: negatives are shown, and no surplus changes.
entries.formula:
total(g0) = SUM_g N[g0, g] x P(graduate from g) x payoff(g), over the absorbing Markov chain on FV tiers 35-70 (annual step fit on dated grade history)
intrinsic(g0) = P(graduate | grade frozen at g0) x payoff(g0); payoff = clemens_2026 table value at the graduating grade
PLUS% = (total - intrinsic) / total
entries.example: A FV 45 hitter draws most of his expected dollars from paths that upgrade to 50 or 55 before debuting: PLUS% near 60 percent. A FV 65 reads near zero or negative.

entries.definition: Expected slugging: the slugging a hitter's contact deserved from how the ball was struck, without defense and park luck.
entries.methodology: Baseball Savant estimates SLG from exit velocity and launch angle at each outcome's run value. Shown on MLB player cards as a percentile against the season's qualified-hitter pool.
entries.origin: Baseball Savant (MLB Statcast), Tom Tango and the Statcast team; our card value is a percentile reconstruction from the tracking inputs available.

entries.definition: Expected isolated power: deserved extra-base power, computed as xSLG minus xBA, so it isolates the power a hitter's contact earned from the singles.
entries.methodology: xISO = xSLG - xBA, both from Savant's contact-quality model (exit velocity + launch angle): the deserved-power analog of ISO (SLG - AVG). Shown on MLB player cards as a percentile against the Savant expected-stats pool, beside the Luck chip (xwOBA minus wOBA, the xHEM+ sign).
entries.origin: Baseball Savant (MLB Statcast), Tom Tango and the Statcast team; our card value is a percentile reconstruction from the tracking inputs available.

entries.definition: A reliever's DESERVED run prevention on the REM+ scale: REM+'s 100-anchored convention applied to Savant expected wOBA allowed instead of FIP, so it reads the contact a reliever gives up rather than where the balls fell. Luck = actual minus expected wOBA allowed. A companion to REM+. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: xREM+ = 100 x reliever-pool expected wOBA allowed / the reliever's own (inverted: lower allowed scores higher), anchored on the reliever board so 100 is the average reliever. Expected wOBA from each batted ball's launch conditions strips balls-in-play and sequencing luck. Statcast expected wOBA allowed was tested against FIP for the pitcher run-prevention models and did not forward-predict better, so REM+ stays FIP-based; xREM+ is a deserved read plus a luck residual, not a sharper predictor. Tracked relievers with 80+ batters faced only. Luck > 0: allowed more than his contact deserved; < 0: over-performed.
entries.formula:
xREM+ = 100 x reliever-pool xwOBA allowed / player's xwOBA allowed (INVERTED: lower allowed scores higher), tracked relievers with 80+ BF
Luck = actual wOBA allowed - expected wOBA allowed
entries.example: A .270 xwOBA allowed against a .310 pool reads xREM+ 115. An actual .300 beside it is +.030 of bad luck.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: A starter's DESERVED run prevention on the SEM+ scale: SEM+'s 100-anchored convention applied to Savant expected wOBA allowed instead of FIP. Luck = actual minus expected wOBA allowed. A companion to SEM+. Coloured on the value ruler at 140 / 120 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: xSEM+ = 100 x starter-pool expected wOBA allowed / the starter's own (inverted), anchored on the starter board so 100 is the average starter. Statcast expected wOBA allowed was tested against FIP for the pitcher run-prevention models and did not forward-predict better, so SEM+ stays FIP-based; xSEM+ is a deserved read plus a luck residual. Tracked starters with 150+ batters faced only. Luck > 0: allowed more than his contact deserved; < 0: over-performed.
entries.formula:
xSEM+ = 100 x starter-pool xwOBA allowed / player's xwOBA allowed (INVERTED: lower allowed scores higher), tracked starters with 150+ BF
Luck = actual wOBA allowed - expected wOBA allowed
entries.example: A .295 xwOBA allowed against a .320 starter pool reads xSEM+ 108. An actual .270 beside it is -.025: over-performing his contact.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: An org's international-amateur spending efficiency: bonus dollars per projected FV point over the graded (tracked) signees in a class. Lower is more efficient. A projected-FV proxy, not realized value; recent classes have no outcomes yet.
entries.methodology: Per org, over graded signees only: covered bonus dollars / their current projected FV points (raw FV, as in fv_per_m_pool and surplus_per_fv_pt). The Coverage column shows the graded subset's share of total class spending. Orgs with fewer than 3 graded signees in view are listed, not ranked. Provisional; no surplus changes.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. IFA signing bonuses from Spotrac.

entries.definition: Roster-decision exposure for the trade board: Rule 5 must-protect, on the 40-man, out of options. Flags players an org may have to move or protect. Deterministic, not a predictive model.
entries.methodology: From roster status: on_40_man, option years used and left (3 to start), Rule 5 exposure (off the 40-man and past the exposure-year threshold since signing: protect by November or risk losing him for about $100K), and service phase. The 0-100 score is additive: +55 Rule 5 must-protect or in the November window, +30 on the 40-man and out of options, +12 one option left, +10 occupying a scarce 40-man slot. The per-org summary counts only that org's rostered and MLB board players, not a full 40-man census. No outcome to backtest, so no predictive gate.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Roster status from the MLB Stats API.

entries.definition: Average Leverage Index of the situations a player was in: how high-stakes his plate appearances (batters) or entries (relievers) were. 1.0 is neutral.
entries.methodology: Leverage Index (Tom Tango, The Book) measures how much one play can swing win probability relative to an average situation; pLI averages it over the player's plays, from the MLB StatsAPI winProbability feed (every PA for batters). It contextualizes WPA: high WPA at high pLI is expected; high WPA at low pLI is not. Descriptive.
entries.formula: pLI = mean Leverage Index over the plays a player was in (every PA for batters, a reliever's outings for pitchers), LI from the MLB StatsAPI winProbability feed; 1.0 = neutral
entries.example: A setup man whose entries average LI 1.7 pitched at nearly double neutral stakes; a bench bat at pLI 0.8 hit mostly in low-pressure spots.
entries.origin: Industry metric; average Leverage Index faced (Tom Tango, The Book), computed here from the MLB StatsAPI winProbability feed.

entries.definition: Pitches a batter saw in one game divided by his at-bats, in the Scores / Standings box score. A plate appearance that ends without an at-bat (a walk, a hit by pitch, a sacrifice, catcher's interference) adds its pitches to the top of the rate and nothing to the bottom.
entries.methodology: The denominator is at-bats by choice, not plate appearances, so a game with walks reads higher here than the same pitches per plate appearance would. Pitches seen are MLB's pitch events in each completed plate appearance, credited to the batter at its end, because MLB's box score batting line carries no pitch count; at-bats are the box score's. A batter with no at-bat (a pinch runner, or a game of walks only) shows a dash. One decimal, half up. Descriptive: one game's count, not a skill rate.
entries.formula:
P/AB = pitches seen / AB
a dash when AB = 0
entries.example: A batter who saw 19 pitches in 3 at-bats and a walk reads 6.3 P/AB (19 / 3); the same 19 pitches over his 4 plate appearances are 4.8 a trip.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Pitches a pitcher threw in one game divided by his innings pitched, in the Scores / Standings box score. Innings are outs recorded divided by 3, so 6.1 innings is 19 outs, or 6.33 innings.
entries.methodology: Pitches are the box score's pitch count (MLB's numberOfPitches, the PC in the PC-ST column); innings are outs / 3, so a partial inning counts its thirds exactly. A pitcher who recorded no out shows a dash. One decimal, half up. Descriptive: one game's count, not a skill rate.
entries.formula:
P/IP = pitches / (outs / 3) = 3 x pitches / outs
a dash when outs = 0
entries.example: 95 pitches over 19 outs (6.1 IP) reads 15.0 P/IP (95 x 3 / 19).
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: MLB's own live estimate of each team's chance to win after every plate appearance, from its public feed. It starts every game at 50 percent, so it is not a pregame forecast; inside a game it moves with the situation and, by this site's own check, also carries some team strength. The site measures it and does not fit it.
entries.methodology: The Scores / Standings page reads MLB's number for the home team after each plate appearance from the StatsAPI winProbability feed and prints it as MLB serves it. A plate appearance MLB gives no number for is a gap in the chart; no house number fills it. The site's check scores the feed on regular-season plays against a constant base rate (Model Accountability, scores_mlb_wp); no postseason game is in that check.
entries.origin: MLB's own live model (MLB Advanced Media), read from its public StatsAPI feed; not an eephus.io model.

entries.definition: Three players chosen by a published rule, not by a vote: win probability added from MLB's live model, with a workhorse pitcher credited for runs prevented when that is larger, and the first star from the winning team.
entries.methodology: The rule is stars_v1. Each play's win probability added from MLB's feed goes to the batter and, with the opposite sign, to the pitcher at the end of the plate appearance. A pitcher with 15 or more outs and no net loss of win probability is credited with his runs prevented against the league rate when that is larger. The first star is the top player on the winning team, so he can rank below the second; ties go to the player whose plate appearances had the higher average Leverage Index. Final games only, and none when MLB's feed covers under 95 percent of the plays. Descriptive: what happened in one game, not skill; never ranked across games or seasons.
entries.origin: Arkmetric rule, original to eephus.io, over MLB's live win probability.

entries.definition: The five plate appearances that moved win probability most in a game, each with MLB's video of that play when MLB has posted one.
entries.methodology: The rule is bp_v1: completed plate appearances with an MLB number that moved the home team's win probability by at least 3 points, largest first, then the higher Leverage Index, then the earlier plate appearance. Five in the game view (so far, while the game is live), the top one on a final game's card. Each row reads from the batting team's side: its win probability before and after, and the signed swing. Withheld when MLB's feed covers under 95 percent of the plays.
entries.origin: Arkmetric rule, original to eephus.io, over MLB's live win probability.

entries.definition: A challenge of a ball or strike call, reviewed by the automated ball-strike system. Each club has a limited number; a successful challenge is kept.
entries.origin: MLB rule; the Scores / Standings game view lists each club's challenges won and lost from MLB's game feed.

entries.definition: What a player's challenges of ball and strike calls were worth this season, in runs, for batters, catchers and pitchers. eABS raw is the runs his overturned challenges won minus what his failed ones cost; eABS compares that with what the league's overturn rate on the same mix of counts would have earned. Descriptive: what happened, not a forecast, and not part of any WAR.
entries.methodology: Every ABS zone challenge of the MLB regular season is read from MLB's game feeds, and each club's totals match MLB's own count in every game. An overturned call is worth a ball against a strike at the challenged count, bases and outs, on that season's run expectancy by count (RE288). A batter's win turns a strike into a ball; a catcher's or pitcher's turns a ball into a strike. A call that stands is worth nothing by itself, but it spends one of the club's two challenges (a successful one is kept). That cost is the value of a held challenge at that half-inning, score margin and number of challenges left. It is measured as the extra runs clubs went on to gain from their challenges with one more in hand. eABS weighs each challenge by how far its result sits from the league's overturn rate for the same side of the ball and count, so a player who only challenges full-count pitches is measured against full-count challenges. Season-to-season persistence was tested once on AAA 2022 to 2026 against a shuffled twin; the board says whether it held.
entries.formula: eABS raw = runs won - failed-challenge cost; eABS = sum over challenges of (overturned - league rate for the cell) x (run value + failure cost)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How much better or worse a player did in high-leverage spots than his own overall rate predicts. Positive = more win probability added when it mattered than a context-neutral version of himself. A timing measure, not a skill.
entries.methodology: FanGraphs Clutch = WPA/pLI - WPA/LI. WPA/pLI rescales his win probability added by his average leverage; WPA/LI is his context-neutral production; the difference says whether his value clustered in high-leverage spots. From the MLB StatsAPI winProbability feed. Unstable year to year.
entries.formula:
Clutch = WPA / pLI - WPA/LI
WPA / pLI = win probability added rescaled by the average leverage faced; WPA/LI = the context-neutral per-play deleveraged production
entries.example: 2.4 WPA at pLI 1.2 with a context-neutral WPA/LI of 1.6: Clutch = 2.4 / 1.2 - 1.6 = +0.40.
entries.origin: Industry metric (FanGraphs), from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango). Clutch = WPA/pLI - WPA/LI.

entries.definition: The Statcast upgrade inside eFV: for AAA seasons from 2023 on, a prospect's stat line is moved toward what his contact quality says it should have been before eFV converts it to level-relative features. Expected stats from exit velocity and launch angle predict the next season better than results. Players without a qualified Statcast season are untouched.
entries.methodology: For each AAA season since 2023 with 100+ Savant plate appearances, S-XLINE takes the gap between expected and actual within Baseball Savant (xBA − BA, xOBP − OBP, xSLG − SLG for hitters; the xwOBA-against gap for pitchers) and applies half of it to the line eFV reads. Measuring the gap inside one source cancels cross-source level bias. Validation before shipping: on 776 AAA hitter season pairs the blended line predicted next-season wOBA better than the actual line (delta Spearman +0.025, CI95 +0.005 to +0.045); on 491 pitcher pairs the blend cleared at +0.051 (CI95 +0.012 to +0.091). Bounds: per-stat gaps are capped (25 points of BA or OBP, 50 of SLG, at half weight) and the pitcher ERA correction is clamped to ±25 percent, so one partial season cannot move a served grade more than 3 FV points; the shipped run moved 97 active grades, largest 2.7. Gate record: registry row xfv_statcast_line. Public MiLB Statcast exists where tracking hardware is installed (currently AAA); the blend extends if tracking reaches AA.
entries.formula: Hitters: adjusted stat = actual + 0.5 x capped(x_stat - stat). adjusted OPS = adjusted OBP + adjusted SLG. Caps: 0.050 for BA and OBP, 0.100 for SLG. Pitchers: adjusted ERA = ERA x clamp(1 + 0.5 x (xwOBAa - wOBAa) / wOBAa, 0.75 to 1.25). Applies only to AAA seasons 2023+ with 100+ Savant PA.
entries.example: A AAA hitter slugs .556 on contact that supports .357. With S-XLINE roughly half of the capped gap comes off before the features are built, and his grade settles about 2 FV lower.

entries.definition: Descriptive ladder-speed index for hitters: how fast a prospect has climbed the affiliated minors against peers on a comparable path. 100 = typical pace, 110 = one standard unit faster, display capped 70-130. Hitters only; never a model input.
entries.methodology: Raw pace = PA-weighted average ladder height (Complex 1 to Triple-A 5) per active season, counting only meaningful assignments (30+ PA at a level-season) and freezing at the MLB debut. Expected pace = a joint fixed-effects fit over starting-level x experience cells plus entry age, era, position group and entry pathway, so every cohort margin centers near 100. AP+ = 100 + 10 x the standardized residual, shrunk toward 100 for thin samples; the percentile compares hitters with the same number of active seasons. Tiers: Insufficient (suppressed), Early, Developing, Established. The cancelled 2020 season never counts. By the source method's contract it feeds no eFV, projection, valuation or ranking.
entries.formula: AP+ = 100 + 10 x z, where z = (area pace - peer expected pace) / experience-year SD, shrunk by m/(m+1) on m meaningful assignments; display capped 70-130.
entries.origin: The Advancement Pace method (descriptive display charter), rebuilt for eephus.io from the platform's own MiLB season data; the Masthead (/team/) carries the credits.

entries.definition: Card chip for premium-position prospects (listed C, SS, CF, 2B, 3B): the modeled probability his primary MLB home stays at the listed position, banded Likely stays / Split risk / Likely moves. Risk context; never in a grade, rank or sort.
entries.methodology: From the position-migration defense model: the listed position's migration base rate (roughly 47 percent of shortstops stay at short, 94 percent of catchers stay behind the plate), with body frame (BMI) and age moving probability down the defensive spectrum. Bands are tercile cuts of stay probability among tracked prospects at the same listed position; the cut points ship with the data and show in the tooltip. Base rates plus frame, not scouting reports.
entries.formula:
P(stay) = migration base rate at the listed position, shifted down the defensive spectrum by body frame (BMI) and age
bands = tercile cuts of P(stay) among tracked prospects at the SAME listed position; the cut points ship with the data and show in the tooltip
entries.example: A 19yo listed shortstop with an average frame starts near the 47 percent shortstop stay rate; a thicker frame at 21 moves him toward Likely moves.
entries.origin: Position-migration thesis with chip banding built for eephus.io; the Masthead (/team/) carries the credits.

entries.definition: Per-pitch-type pitch-quality display on CollegeSavant pitcher pages, scored from TrackMan physics (velocity, movement, release, spin). Its own class-relative ratio scale (100 = college-average expected run value, 0 = the worst observed college xRV), NOT a z-score: the payload spread is about 23-24 points per season, observed range 3.4 to 185.4. Draft-evaluation context, not a projection.
entries.formula:
per pitch type: expected run value modeled from TrackMan physics (velocity, movement, release, spin), rescaled class-relative: 100 = college-average xRV, 0 = the worst observed college xRV
its own ratio scale (payload sd about 23-24 points per season), NOT a z-score index
entries.example: A 130 College Stuff+ slider is a shade over one class-sd above average on this scale; a 130 aStuff+ would be three sigma.
entries.origin: Industry metric. External model lineage built for CollegeSavant (college TrackMan xRV family); eephus.io vendors the already-scored payloads and displays them, and does not fit or re-derive the model. Registered for governance 2026-07-23 (data/collegesavant_stuff_eval.json).

entries.definition: Card pill for A-ball and complex-level prospects: whiff share (hitters) or four-seam velocity (pitchers), and the part of that signal his own strikeout rate does not already explain. Display context: not a grade, not a projection, no adjustment of its own.
entries.methodology:
Coverage is the bake in data/statcast_alevel_signals.json: 635 player-seasons at A or CPX with 100+ pitches of signal exposure (330 A hitters, 144 complex hitters, 96 A pitchers, 65 complex pitchers), 2026 only.

Each signal is z-scored in its side-level-season qualified pool, then regressed on the same player's strikeout z with coefficients FROZEN on the 2023-2025 lab populations: hitters whiff_z on k_z, slope 0.887, intercept 0.014, r 0.872, n 788; pitchers velo_z on k_a_z, slope 0.218, intercept -0.009, r 0.219, n 227. The pill reads the RESIDUAL: a positive hitter residual is swing-and-miss the strikeout rate has not charged for yet; a positive pitcher residual is velocity the strikeout rate has not converted yet.

Measured once as an incremental Spearman against the out-of-fold residual of a cross-fitted stat-line ridge: whiff on next-season K% +0.0965, CI95 [+0.0277, +0.1604]; FB velo on next-season K%-allowed +0.1423, CI95 [+0.0196, +0.2704] (data/xfv_statcast_line4_eval.json). The hitter wOBA channel read null (-0.0266, CI95 crossing zero), so the whiff residual is strikeout information only.

Limits: one live season, no resolved out-of-sample fold, a forward correlation rather than a WAR backtest. Registered provisional (statcast_alevel_display). Whether the residual also leans the eFV grade is a separate registered decision (xfv_statcast_overlay_uncapped).
entries.formula: residual_z = signal_z - (slope x strikeout_z + intercept), coefficients frozen 2026-07-23; hitters signal = whiff share, pitchers signal = four-seam velocity.
entries.example: A Single-A hitter at 35.2% whiff sits at whiff_z +1.17 with K% z +1.08: residual +0.20, about what his strikeout rate already says. The same whiff share with a pool-average strikeout rate reads +1.15.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. The inputs are MLB Statcast and zone tracking; the residualization against the stat line and its frozen coefficients are ours.

entries.definition: Historical strata a prospect falls into (age for level, level, level-relative production and so on) with what those groups realized. Descriptive only: the predictive version failed, so nothing here adjusts or forecasts a grade.
entries.methodology:
Population: hitters with a MiLB track record and a decision year of 2016-2024, 904 rows. WAR and bust figures use the 527 whose six-year window has closed (decision years 2016-2020). Baseline: 1.90 mean WAR, 76.7% bust rate (≤ 0.5 WAR). A stratum is one to three axis cuts intersected; 3,957 clear the 25-player reporting floor. Each reports n, mean and median realized WAR, a 95% interval on the mean, and the bust rate. Hitters only. 130 strata carry a zero-width interval because every closed member realized the same WAR (0.0, none reached the majors): degenerate, not precise.

Why it is not a model: nested cross-validation put stratum selection inside the fold and the effect did not survive. Every hitter arm's rank-correlation delta against the shipped eFV blend sits inside its null band (-0.0106 to +0.0082) against the 0.017 gate standard. Between 45 and 141 percent of the in-fold effect is selection bias (inner-fold 0.86 to 1.85 WAR collapse to -0.60 to +0.50 out of fold), permuted controls invert, and eight nested folds pick eight different top strata (mean pairwise axis Jaccard 0.135).

Auditability: stratum MEMBERSHIP is re-checked every build (all 3,957 ids and resolved-row counts match the pre-registered outcome-blind enumeration). The outcome columns are a frozen quote of a 2026-07-25 measurement: the script that produced them (tools/_comb_sweep_desc.py) is absent from the tree, so mean WAR, median WAR, bust rate and residual t cannot be regenerated.

Reliability tag. The source artifact's health_warning claims every stratum has a statistically zero out-of-fold residual against eFV. That is false and is not carried forward: 477 of 3,957 strata sit at |t| ≥ 2 (about 180 expected under a null), 124 at |t| ≥ 3 (about 11 expected), max 4.91. Each stratum ships a tag from its own t: PRICED (3,193) = comps and grade agree; WATCH (687) = nominally off-model but not surviving Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 across all 3,957 tests; OFF-MODEL (77) = survives that correction at |t| ≥ 3.30, comps and grade disagree, neither authoritative. 76 of the 77 have a negative residual and 43 busted at 100 percent, because WAR floors near zero for a player who never debuts; that is the outcome scale bottoming out, not an eFV defect. Registered unvalidated with no eval artifact (archetype_comps); the failed model lane is archetype_search.
entries.example: Stratum 'very young for level, above-average level-relative OPS': 26 closed-window players, mean 11.7 WAR, CI95 [8.6, 14.9]. What those 26 did, not a projection for the 27th.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Built from the 2026-07-25 combinatorial archetype sweep (tools/_comb_sweep.py family) and registered as a descriptive surface rather than a model.

entries.term: MiLB Park Factor (Run PF / HR PF)
entries.definition: In-house run and home-run park factors for every affiliated minor-league venue, 2021 forward. 1.00 is neutral for the venue's league and season; 1.10 means about 10% more runs than the league-season baseline. The displayed number is a trailing three-season window, unclamped. Reference only: no grade, rank or dollar on the site is park-adjusted.
entries.methodology:
Team-season factor = (home runs scored plus allowed per game) / (road runs scored plus allowed per game), from StatsAPI final scores, regular season. Each team-season is centered on the unweighted league-season mean and shrunk toward 1.00 with K_G = 70 home games. A venue takes its modal home team; a venue-season is the home-game-weighted mean of its team-seasons; the window uses only seasons at or before the season read.

Coverage: 1,211 team-seasons from Triple-A through the complexes and the DSL, 969 venue-seasons, HR factor on 930. 2026 is in progress, so it mixes a partial schedule with the 2024-2025 legs.

Window, not season: single-season venue factors repeat under the registration's 0.50 bar, while an odd-against-even split-half of the multi-season aggregate clears it. Both reads are computed on the /parks/ Method & Sample tab from the served table, so the figures there are the current ones.

Unclamped: the source method's clamps ([0.90, 1.10] run, [0.80, 1.25] HR) are a safety rail for a model formula that is switched off. Clamping the display would move 13 venues on runs and 17 on HR (Hodgetown's 1.209 would read 1.100), so the measured value ships and the bounds travel beside it. HR factor feeds no formula (ISO and SLG neutralize through the run factor). StatsAPI venue 401 'TBD' is not a ballpark: it is the unlabeled-DSL bucket, the club-seasons the feed reports with no venue. The board keeps it as one row flagged 'pooled' on the windows that reach its 2021 to 2023 seasons; read it as league context.

Model status: the eFV lane that would park-neutralize MiLB lines with this table failed its registered gate (hitters +0.0005, lo95 -0.0011; pitchers -0.0021, lo95 -0.0051) and stays off. Registry rows: milb_park_factors (table and display) and xfv_park_line (the failed correction).
entries.formula: run_pf = shrink( (home RS+RA per game) / (road RS+RA per game) / league-season mean, K_G = 70 ); venue-season = home-game-weighted mean over its team-seasons.
entries.example: Hodgetown (Amarillo) reads 1.209 run / 1.428 HR; Dickey-Stephens Park (North Little Rock) reads 0.840 / 0.751. Both Double-A.
entries.origin: Park factor is a shared industry concept; this table is an in-house build from StatsAPI schedule scores, original to eephus.io. No external park-factor source is used.
