entries.definition: Every source's published FV is quantile-mapped onto one common scale before averaging, and the result is rounded UP, so the consensus can sit above or below the arithmetic mean of the printed grades. The per-source grades shown are always the raw published ones.
entries.methodology:
Three steps between the card's grades and the consensus.

1. NORMALIZE. Each source's grade distribution is quantile-mapped onto the FanGraphs scale using only players both graded, per role per cycle, so a source that covers only the top of the board is not called hot for skipping low tiers. Hot sources map DOWN, cold sources UP. Measured per cycle (data/grade_normalization_eval.json, 2026 hitter cycle, median shifts): MLB Pipeline and ESPN -5, Pipeline International -10, draft-signing grades -3.3, Baseball America +5 (n 520), performance-ingest grades +5; FanGraphs, Just Baseball and tjstats 0. The reference source maps to itself.

2. AVERAGE. Equal weight as of 2026-07-25 (the 2026-06 accuracy weights were reverted when the hardened re-measurement put the weighted arm inside the noise floor). A player only one source has ever graded is pulled one third toward FV 35 until a second grade lands.

3. DISPLAY. Clamped to 20-80 and rounded UP to a whole grade (the site rule for FV and tool grades). A raw 50.05 prints 51.

The gap between printed grades and consensus is mapping first, the single-source pull second, the round-up last (worth up to a full grade). Registered as model_id grade_normalization (provisional); the map is refit each cycle and deterministic.
entries.formula: consensus FV = ceil( mean( map_source(published FV) ) ), clamped 20-80; single-source case shrunk = (n_obs x src_FV + k x 35) / (n_obs + k).
entries.example: Three sources print 45, 50 and 50; a reader averages 48.3. The model averages each grade after its own scale map and prints the ceiling: a mapped mean of 50.05 displays as 51.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Paired quantile map of each source's grade distribution onto the reference source, fit on the same-player overlap.

entries.definition: The model behind /arbitration/: the one-year salary an arbitration-eligible player receives in a season his club tenders him and the figure is settled or awarded.
entries.methodology:
Two stages. The first arbitration year has no prior salary, so it is a level model on log deflated salary, fit by ridge with a Duan smearing correction so the served figure is a conditional mean, not a median. Its features are known when the award is set: WAR, playing time, position and the Arkmetric skill indices from the platform season (the one before the award), plus age and service class. Later years are a raise problem, and the CBA caps a cut at 20% of the prior salary, so the target is the log of the raise above that floor: every prediction and band endpoint is legal by construction. The board serves an empirical raise multiplier for those later years. On the first measurement, which read the award season itself, the per-player model did not beat it; on the platform-season re-run it does, and switching the board to it is a separate change. Only seasons whose arbitration year comes from published service time are scored.

The projected award is also the salary leg of surplus for every club controlled player on the board, and it prices a prospect's arbitration seasons too: the first from a league-minimum prior salary, with the platform season's playing time and skill indices read from first-time arbitration players of his role at that WAR.
entries.formula:
arb-1: ln(deflated salary) = ridge(platform-season WAR, playing time, position, Arkmetric indices; age, service class); served salary = exp(prediction) x Duan smearing factor
arb-2+: served salary = prior salary x empirical raise multiplier by (arb step, prior-salary band), floored at 0.80 x prior and the league minimum; the per-player raise model lost to the multiplier on measurement and does not serve there
entries.example: A first-time-eligible 3-WAR outfielder projects near $4M from the ridge on his rate and volume features. A second-trip player at a $4M prior in a band whose median multiplier is 1.6 serves near $6.4M, and no served figure can fall below $3.2M: the 20 percent maximum cut is legal by construction.

entries.definition: Actual arbitration salary minus what this model expected. It asks whether the arbitration system paid a player more or less than players with a comparable case.
entries.methodology: The model's own residual, so it sums to roughly zero across the league; negative means the model expected more than the player received. A statement about the model, not an underpaid verdict. Kept separate from the value residual (salary against production priced at that winter's $/WAR), which does not sum to zero because arbitration pays below the open market; the two are never combined.
entries.formula:
residual = actual arbitration salary - model expectation; league sum ~ 0 by construction
kept strictly separate from the value residual (salary - production x winter $/WAR), which does not sum to zero
entries.example: A player awarded $5.5M whom the model expected at $4.8M reads +$0.7M: the system paid him above comparable cases. It does not say he is overpaid against the open market; arbitration pays below that market systematically.

entries.definition: The mean of a player's career WAR and his WAR7, so a long good career and a short great one meet in the middle. Jay Jaffe's metric; the /hof/ leaderboards reproduce it from the daily WAR file Baseball-Reference publishes from.
entries.methodology: JAWS = (career WAR + WAR7) / 2, WAR7 = the sum of the seven best seasons (not necessarily consecutive). Both halves are Baseball-Reference bWAR, a deliberate pin that differs from the site's eWAR. On the five players checked by hand the reproduction is exact on all fifteen published figures. Across the 1,322 players who have appeared on a Hall of Fame ballot page it agrees exactly on career WAR for 1,251 and within a tenth for 1,262. The largest gaps are players who also pitched: the site sums batting and pitching WAR per season (John Ward 62.3 against the published 34.3, Babe Ruth 182.6 against 162.3, Rick Ankiel 9.1 against 5.5), while the published shelf carries the position-player figure. A two-way career is therefore not comparable to the published positional shelf. Not an opinion about who belongs: /hof/ publishes a JAWS quantile ladder rather than a Hall-sized line, because a Hall-sized line needs the count of players inducted AS PLAYERS and no field in the source data says what a plaque says.
entries.formula: JAWS = (career WAR + WAR7) / 2
entries.origin: Jay Jaffe, Baseball Prospectus and FanGraphs

entries.definition: The sum of a player's seven best WAR seasons: the peak half of JAWS.
entries.methodology: Sort every season's bWAR descending and sum the top seven. The seasons need not be consecutive: WAR7 is a best-seven, not a best-consecutive-seven. A player with fewer than seven seasons sums what he has, so WAR7 and career WAR converge for short careers.
entries.formula: WAR7 = sum of the seven largest single-season WAR values
entries.origin: Jay Jaffe, as the peak component of JAWS

entries.definition: Ours, NOT Bill James's Black Ink or Gray Ink. Four points for a league-leading WAR season and one for a top-ten WAR season, ranking hitters and pitchers in one pool per league-season.
entries.methodology: Within each league-season, rank every player by WAR in one pool, hitters and pitchers together; 4 points for rank 1, 1 point for ranks 2-10, summed over a career. Black Ink counts league-leading finishes in traditional counting categories (home runs, RBI, wins, strikeouts) and Gray Ink top-ten finishes in the same; this counts WAR only. On the Hall of Fame bake-off it is the weakest of the eleven arms (AUC 0.8907 against HoF Monitor's 0.9697) with the highest tie share on the board (only 30 distinct values).
entries.formula: ink = 4 x (league-leading WAR seasons) + 1 x (top-ten WAR seasons)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io. Not Bill James's Black Ink or Gray Ink, which count traditional counting categories; this counts league-leading and top-ten WAR seasons only.

entries.definition: How long after the writers are done with a player the site waits before calling a non-induction final: 25 years by default, because the era committees never formally close.
entries.methodology: A writers' window closes by election, by falling off the ballot, or by exhausting it. If the player is not in the Hall by that close plus the horizon, the any-route label reads a resolved zero; before that it reads CENSORED. The label is non-monotone in the year you ask: a player enshrined by a committee more than a horizon after his window closed reads zero for decades and then flips to one. Forty-four players in the eligible universe do this (Joe Gordon: window closed 1945, inducted 2009). The sensitivity table at 15, 20, 25, 30 and 40 years ships beside the label.

entries.definition: The FIP-scale number on the MLB Stats bullpen and starter boards (the Skill FIP column) and on a free agent's current-season line. It is not the standard FIP. Each of the four FIP inputs, the strikeout, walk, hit-batter and home-run rates per batter faced, is pulled toward the average of the pitcher's own ROLE pool (relievers on the bullpen board, starters on the starter board) by sample size, and the constant is solved on that role pool rather than on the whole league. The result is a skill estimate: it sits closer to the role average than the pitcher's actual line, most of all over a short sample. REM+ and SEM+ are ratios of it. Lower is better.
entries.methodology:
Each rate is shrunk with the same empirical-Bayes recipe: shrunk rate = (BF x rate + k x pool rate) / (BF + k), where BF is the pitcher's batters faced and k is a pseudo-count of 70 batters for strikeouts, 170 for walks, 170 for hit batters and 400 for home runs, so the home-run rate is regressed hardest. The shrunk rates are turned back into expected counts over the pitcher's own batters faced and divided by his own innings with the standard FIP weights (13 per home run, 3 per walk or hit batter, minus 2 per strikeout). The constant is solved so the unshrunk FIP of the whole role pool equals that pool's ERA: relievers with 50 or more batters faced set the reliever constant, and starters with 20 or more innings set the starter constant. The result is floored at 1.00.

Against standard FIP: FanGraphs FIP uses the pitcher's actual counts with no shrink and one league-wide constant per season. The two converge as the sample grows, but a reliever season rarely reaches the 400 batters the home-run term needs to carry even half its own weight, so a reliever's home-run rate stays pulled toward the pool over a full year. The reliever and starter constants also differ from each other and from the league constant, so the bullpen and starter boards' Skill FIPs do not share an exact baseline.

REM+ is 100 times the reliever-pool average Skill FIP divided by the pitcher's own, and SEM+ the same on the starter pool, so this column is what those indexes are built from. In the data files the field is still named fip so existing readers do not break. For the standard statistic, see FIP.
entries.formula:
shrunk rate = (BF x rate + k x role-pool rate) / (BF + k); k = 70 (K), 170 (BB), 170 (HBP), 400 (HR) batters faced
Skill FIP = max(1.00, (13 x HR' + 3 x (BB' + HBP') - 2 x K') / IP + role-pool constant), with each X' = shrunk rate x BF
role-pool constant = pool ERA - (13 x HR + 3 x (BB + HBP) - 2 x K) / IP, summed over the unshrunk role pool
entries.example: Take a hypothetical reliever pool at 22 percent strikeouts, 9 percent walks, 1 percent hit batters and 2.5 percent home runs per batter faced, with a 3.10 constant. A reliever who faces 60 batters over 15 innings with 24 strikeouts, 3 walks, no hit batters and no home runs has an unshrunk FIP of 0.50 on that constant, and a Skill FIP of 2.85: 60 batters is too few for the strikeout rate to stand alone, and with no home runs yet the 400-batter home-run term pulls him most of the way to the pool. The same rates over 240 batters and 60 innings read 1.89, nearer his line but still well above it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric component, original to eephus.io. Built on FIP (Tom Tango) with an empirical-Bayes shrink toward the role pool.

entries.definition: A fielder's glove per inning on a 100-anchored scale: 100 is the average fielder with 200 or more defensive innings, ten points is one standard deviation. The fielding member of the HEM+ / REM+ / SEM+ family: FanGraphs' published fielding runs per 1,000 defensive innings, catcher framing included, pulled toward average by sample size. Positional credit and innings show beside it as context and never move it. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology:
The runs are FanGraphs' fielding runs (Statcast range and arm, catcher blocking and throwing), read verbatim from MLB's sabermetrics feed. Catcher framing is not a field in that feed but sits inside its run line, so it is recovered exactly as the residual: rar minus batting, baserunning, fielding, positional, league and replacement runs. No Outs Above Average or Defensive Runs Saved: one source, no blend.

Each rate is shrunk toward zero, which is the position average because FanGraphs zeroes fielding runs within every position and season. The pull uses a per-position constant fixed on 2016-2018 before the test window was read: catchers (framing measured on every pitch) are trusted fastest, first basemen slowest. The scale is ten points per standard deviation of the pool's shrunk rates, the WAR/PA+ ruler, not the ratio ruler of HEM+, REM+ and SEM+, because a rate centred on zero cannot be divided by its average. A point of DEM+ is not a point of HEM+. Board bands follow that ruler (the WAR/PA+ breaks): 120+ elite, 107+ above average, 93-106 average, under 93 below; leaderboard-qualified at 400+ innings.

Gate (pre-registered, passed): over 2021-2024 (1,255 pairs) DEM+ ranks next season's fielding rate at a Spearman correlation of 0.4597, against 0.4531 for the unshrunk rate, 0.0111 for fielding percentage and 0.089 for innings; a shuffled twin scores 0.0228. It beats fielding percentage and innings with the gap's lower bound above zero and is no worse than the unshrunk rate (gap 95 percent interval -0.0039 to 0.0172). Framing inside the catcher number is parity with FanGraphs WAR, not an improvement on it. Not an eWAR, eFV, betting or projections input. Accountability artifact: data/dem_plus_eval.json.
entries.formula:
rate = (fielding runs + framing runs) x 1000 / defensive innings
shrunk rate = (fielding runs + framing runs) x 1000 / (innings + k), k the innings-weighted per-position constant
DEM+ = 100 + 10 x (shrunk rate - pool mean) / pool sd, over fielders with 200+ innings
entries.example: A shortstop at +12 fielding runs over 1,100 innings with k = 616: shrunk rate 12 x 1000 / 1716 = 7.0. Against a pool mean of 0.1 and sd of 3.3: 100 + 10 x 6.9 / 3.3 = 121.

entries.definition: A club's fielding on the DEM+ scale: the innings-weighted DEM+ of everyone who fielded for it this season, catchers and their framing included. Coloured on the value ruler at 120 / 113 / 107 / 100 / 93.
entries.methodology: Every fielder counts by the innings he played, including players now hurt or traded, because the number describes the season as played (the Offense+ rule). Catchers roll up like everyone else, framing included: the club's fielding runs carry its catchers' framing, which also shows as its own Frm column. The Defensive Alignment card beside it answers tonight's question instead: for each position, the active-roster player with the most innings there, and the catcher slot carries his framing.
entries.formula: Team DEM+ = sum(DEM+ x innings) / sum(innings) over the club's fielders, catchers included

entries.definition: Innings-weighted DEM+ over the last three seasons, each season scored against its own pool. A steadier glove read than one season. On /mlbstats/ the column is the Last 3 window's DEM+, the number the Last 3 view prints, shown uncoloured with the percentile inside that window's pool: a value ruler cut on one season's pool does not travel onto a three-season pool.
entries.methodology: Tested against one-season DEM+ on the same fielders: 3-year rho 0.4893 against 1-year 0.4786. The gap does not clear zero, so it ships provisional with the numbers published. The column reads the Last 3 window's DEM+ (tools/mlbstats_window_lab.py, rebuilt nightly), the number the Last 3 view prints; data/dem_plus_multiyear_eval.json stays the record of this test. Established needs two seasons and 1,000 innings in the window; otherwise provisional (star). Since owner answer M17WIN-1 (2026-10-01), the Defense window publishes every fielder with window innings. A fielder under the 400-inning floor is provisional: marked prov, with his window innings beside the value. So the column has a value for every fielder on the board. The window percentile ranks every published fielder, those under the floor included. The rule is stated in data/mlbstats_window_l3.json (pool_stats and qualified_rule_window).

entries.definition: FanGraphs' fielding runs above average: Statcast range and arm for fielders, blocking and throwing for catchers, zeroed within each position and season. Published by MLB's sabermetrics feed; we display it and compute no version of it.
entries.methodology: Since FanGraphs' 2022 and 2024 updates, applied back to 2016, range and outfield arm come from Statcast. Seasons before 2016 are on a different basis and are not pooled. MLB's feed publishes this number without catcher framing; the DEM+ board adds framing back for catchers (Fld ex-Frm is this number alone).
entries.origin: Industry metric, FanGraphs' fielding runs as published by MLB. We display it and compute no version of it.

entries.definition: Runs a catcher saves by getting borderline pitches called strikes, as FanGraphs credits them.
entries.methodology: MLB's feed carries framing inside a catcher's run total rather than as a field, so it is recovered as that total minus every published component. It matches FanGraphs' own framing column exactly on the seasons checked, and it is zero for every non-catcher. It is counted in DEM+ because FanGraphs WAR counts it.
entries.origin: Industry metric, FanGraphs' catcher framing runs, recovered from MLB's published run line. We display it.

entries.definition: The runs a player is credited for the difficulty of the position he plays: a shortstop gains, a first baseman loses. Two versions show on the Defense board and the MLB player page: Pos (ours), the value inside Def, is the site's positional ladder; Pos (FG) is FanGraphs' published value, for comparison.
entries.methodology: Value, not skill, so it sits beside DEM+ as context and never moves either version. Pos (ours) is Position Fit's fitted ladder, in runs per 650 plate appearances and inverted from Baseball-Reference's positional runs, pro-rated by the innings a player spent at each fielding position at the innings-per-650-PA conversion that artifact states. Designated-hitter time has no fielding innings, so it is left out; FanGraphs' value includes it, which is why a part-time DH reads far lower in Pos (FG). Pos (FG) sits in no sum. Added to fielding runs and framing, Pos (ours) makes Def (see Def runs).
entries.origin: Industry concept. Pos (ours) is the site's Position Fit ladder, computed here; Pos (FG) is FanGraphs' positional adjustment as published by MLB, which we display.

entries.definition: The runs a position is worth against the average defensive position, per 650 plate appearances. The site's ladder is fitted on Baseball-Reference's positional runs; Position Fit in the Alchemy Lab values positions with it.
entries.methodology:
A least squares fit of Baseball-Reference's positional runs per 650 PA on each player-season's innings shares at the nine positions, no intercept, over a rolling six-season window, recentred so the exposure-weighted sum is zero. It recovers the constants Baseball-Reference uses, so a rung is what Baseball-Reference prices the position at, not an independent measure of how hard the position is to play.

A second ladder, measured on players who changed position (the position-switcher ladder, v2), was read once on 2026-10-15 and valued Position Fit for that day. It is withdrawn. Its test compared it only with this ladder. Run on the same players and seasons, a ladder with every fielding position at zero scores about as well: its error was 0.049 runs per 650 PA higher than v2's (95% CI -0.005 to 0.103), so the test measured this ladder's spread, not v2's. Two more things the check found: Statcast's fielding runs do not net to zero within a position, and the gap between the infield and the outfield is set by a few dozen players who moved between them. A corrected re-read (v3, 2026-10-15) measured only the gaps inside the infield and inside the outfield on the same players, with Statcast centred, and took the other levels from the offense gap among regulars. It did not pass: against the zero ladder its error was 0.037 runs per 650 PA lower (95% CI -0.076 to 0.150), not a separation, so Position Fit keeps this ladder. The Library's Positional Ladder view has the read, the check and the re-read.
entries.formula: positional runs per 650 PA = sum over positions of innings share_p x ladder_p, fitted by least squares with no intercept on Baseball-Reference's positional runs; zero = the exposure-weighted average defensive position
entries.example: A shortstop moved to first base gives up the gap between the two rungs in positional value; the Position Fit tab in the Alchemy Lab prints the current rungs.
entries.origin: Arkmetric fit, computed here from Baseball-Reference's positional runs. The position-switcher ladder (v2) is measured from Baseball-Reference, FanGraphs and Statcast fielding runs.

entries.definition: Which hitters are worth more runs at a different position, per 650 plate appearances: the bat plus the fielding at that position plus the positional ladder. The bat is the same everywhere, so fielding and the ladder decide. A valuation of where a hitter fits, not a forecast of where his club puts him.
entries.methodology: The glove is read from Statcast fielding runs prevented over up to three seasons, shrunk per position by how reliable a season is there, and carried to a new position through the difficulty Statcast measures on players who play two positions in a season; that part predicts the size of a move. In the value, the ladder and the difficulty share one run scale (since 2026-10-15): an average glove is worth the same at every fielding position, so a move between two fielding positions is priced by the player's glove alone, and only a move to DH carries a league-wide part. Before, the two came from different run scales and an average glove gained or lost up to 13.6 runs on a move (left field -7.51 against third base +6.06). A hitter is flagged when the gain clears 3 runs per 650 PA and one standard error. The demotion backtest, how well the read ranks the hitters clubs moved down the next season, is a check inside the model's artifact, not a registered gate; the page prints its result.
entries.formula: value at a fielding position p = bat + mean of the seven Statcast-position rungs + s(p) x glove z x innings per 650 PA / 1,000; value at DH = bat + ladder(DH); gain = value(best) - value(now); flag: gain >= 3 runs per 650 PA and >= 1 standard error

entries.definition: Total defensive value in runs: FanGraphs' published fielding runs plus catcher framing plus the site's positional ladder, Pos (ours). The Def column on the Defense board and the Def row on the MLB player page. It is not FanGraphs' own Def, whose positional term is FanGraphs' (shown as Pos (FG)).
entries.methodology: Fielding runs (Statcast range and arm, catcher blocking and throwing) and framing are FanGraphs' published values, read verbatim; they are the glove. The positional term is credit for the position's difficulty, and it is ours: Position Fit's ladder pro-rated by the innings at each fielding position (see Positional adjustment). DEM+ rates the glove per inning and ignores the positional term, so a first baseman can read DEM+ 115 and still post negative Def, as a DH can post a high HEM+ and a low WAR.
entries.formula: Def = fielding runs + framing runs (FanGraphs, per season) + Pos (ours) (Position Fit ladder x innings at each position / innings per 650 PA)
entries.origin: Industry concept, assembled here: FanGraphs' fielding and framing runs as published through MLB's feed, which we display, plus the site's positional ladder, which we compute.

entries.definition: Seven colour steps that rank a number against its own metric: elite, great, good, above average, average, below average, and a red step for values below zero. The colours are shared across the site; the cuts belong to the metric.
entries.methodology: Cuts are round numbers chosen from the served distribution so that the page a reader sees is split rather than painted one colour, and a cell is tiered on the number it PRINTS, so a cell reading 4.0 is never painted below the 4 cut. Cuts a house rule locks never move: the 100 + 10z indexes keep 93, 107 and 120 with the tier names they carry today, HEM+ keeps 88, 112 and 130, and published wRC+ keeps 85, 120 and 145. Per-season eWAR bands at 6, 4, 3, 2.5 and 1.5; a multi-season total bands on the average of the seasons it paints, so a row with fewer seasons in the window can print a smaller total in a brighter step. Red is reserved for numbers below zero, so no above-average index can take it. Every step clears 4.5:1 on the page and card surfaces in both themes; the above-average step sits at 4.3 on the alternate panel, unchanged from the green it already used.
entries.example: A 3.2 WAR season and a 2.6 WAR season are one step apart; both were the same colour before 2026-09-16.

entries.definition: A window of seasons on the MLB Stats boards. Counts add over it. Rates are pooled once, numerator over denominator, never the average of the seasons. A "+" index does not travel by itself: 100 on one is the average of one season's pool, so a window index is a different statistic and only appears on a window the lab actually computed. On any other window the column is absent with its reason in its place, and no window index carries a value-ruler colour.
entries.methodology:
Two mechanisms, and which one you are looking at is stated on the board. (1) The Overall board folds data/war_seasons.json in the browser: one row per player-season, the two eWAR sides summed UNROUNDED and rounded once, an absent denominator contributing nothing rather than a zero. Any from/to span works, because every column on it is a count or a count over its own denominator. (2) The five role boards read data/mlbstats_windows.json and its per-window files, which tools/mlbstats_window_lab.py builds offline for a fixed set of windows (Last 3 and Last 5) by the recipe the shipped 3-year columns already use: the denominator-weighted mean of the per-season index, each season scored against its own pool. So 100 is the average of those pools and not of the window's, and ten points is not one standard deviation of it either - the payload ships pool_stats and the column tooltip reports what both actually are.

Measured on the two artifacts this page reads, which is why the window index carries no ladder. The 2026 hitter board (data/hitter_leaderboards.json) is rebuilt nightly, so its figures are dated: on the 2026-09-24 build, 661 rows, HEM+ averaged 95.3 with a standard deviation of about 14, and the value ruler's elite cut of 120 took 6.5% of it. On the Last 5 window built 2026-09-18 (data/mlbstats_window_l5.json, 746 rows, whose pool_stats block is what the column tooltip and the board note print) the same index averages 95.41 with a standard deviation of 13.15, and 120 takes 4.2%. Same numeral, same word, a third fewer players: painting the one-season ladder on a window pool would call a different share of the league elite by the same name.

A longer window is a steadier DESCRIPTION of what happened. Nothing measured in this repo says it is a better prediction of what happens next: four of the seven shipped trailing-window columns (REM+ 3yr, SEM+ 3yr, DEM+ 3yr, WAR/IP+ 3yr) did not clear zero against their one-season gate and ship as steadiness companions.

2020 and the season being played are disclosed rather than dropped: the exporter publishes season_share (that season's league eWAR over the mean of the last three complete seasons) and the board's note reads it, so the window says 2020 produced 37% of a normal season instead of quietly counting as one.

entries.definition: Batting eWAR per 600 plate appearances, a full season's worth for a regular. A division, not an index: there is no pool behind it, so it carries no colour and no value ruler. Over a window it is the window's batting eWAR over the window's plate appearances.
entries.methodology: Bat/600 = batting eWAR / PA x 600, on the Overall board's own served numbers. Its denominator is PA and PA only. A single eWAR/600 over total eWAR would charge a two-way player's pitching to his plate appearances, which is why the pitching side has its own column over its own denominator (Pitch/200).

entries.definition: Pitching eWAR per 200 innings, a full starter's season. A division, not an index: no pool behind it, so no colour on it. A reliever's 70 innings and a starter's 200 sit on the same ruler here, which is why IP is shown beside it.
entries.methodology: Pitch/200 = pitching eWAR / IP x 200, on the Overall board's own served numbers, with IP as its only denominator. Over a window it is the window's pitching eWAR over the window's innings.

entries.definition: The win-probability value of an in-game decision priced against a league-wide alternative from the same pre-decision state, so what the manager chose is worth what it is worth regardless of how the play turned out. Exists for two families on eephus.io: the stolen-base attempt (management.py) and the sacrifice bunt (mgmt_bunt.py).
entries.methodology: Steal: DV = E[WE | attempt with the league success rate] - WE[hold], priced off the win-expectancy model with a league-average runner, so a fast roster cannot flatter a manager. Bunt: DV(S) = E[change in WE | bunt from state S] - E[change in WE | any other plate appearance from S], league-wide, MIN_CELL 25, two outs excluded. Both are expectations over league outcomes, never the realized change of the play in front of you. The per-club sum of steal DV FAILED its frozen gate (bounded null), so no club is ranked by it.
entries.formula:
DV = E[WE | decision, league rate] - WE[alternative]
realized change = DV + ER (execution residual)

entries.definition: What happened minus what the decision was worth: the realized win-probability change of a priced play minus its decision value. The runner's speed, the catcher's arm and the luck of the throw live here, not in the manager's column.
entries.methodology: For a steal attempt: ER = (WE of the state that actually resulted) - (expected WE at the league success rate). The identity DV + ER = realized change holds exactly on every priced attempt and is checked in the artifact rather than asserted in prose. ER does not sum to zero across the league because the league's success rate is measured over the same attempts it prices.

entries.term: Realized mWPA (realized value of a decision)
entries.definition: Realized value, not skill. Each figure is the win probability that actually moved after the decision, credited to the club that made it, from the decision to the last play it governed. What the alternative would have produced, the reliever not used, the batter not lifted, the pitch not thrown, is not observed, so this is a record of what happened after a manager acted and not a measure of how well he chose. A reliever who pitched well after a poor choice and a hitter who homered after a bad matchup are both in these numbers.
entries.methodology: mWPA(d) = s * (wp_home_after[last play of the window] - wp_home_before[first play]) / 100, with s = +1 for the home club and -1 for the away club and wp in the MLB feed's percentage points. An ENDPOINT DIFFERENCE, never a sum of per-play wpa rows: consecutive plays do not chain on about three percent of plays (in-PA events move the state and are credited to neither), so a row sum misses part of the game's journey. Windows per family: the reliever's stint (pitching change), the plate appearance (pinch hit, bunt), the rest of the half-inning (pinch runner), the walk plus the on-deck plate appearance (intentional walk), the rest of the game (defensive sub, stored and never summed). THE STEAL IS THE EXCEPTION: it happens between two plays, where the feed carries no win probability, and the feed's plate-appearance row starts after it, so that row's endpoint difference is the batter's result with the steal left out. A steal's realized value is therefore the change of the steal itself on the house win expectancy table, WE(after the attempt) - WE(hold), which is DV + ER exactly. Per-family sums only; the windows overlap across families, so no cross-family total exists. The agent is the club-season until the manager ledger lands.
entries.formula: mWPA(d) = s(club, half) * (wp_home_after[p1] - wp_home_before[p0]) / 100; for a steal, WE(after the attempt) - WE(hold) on the house win expectancy table
entries.example: A reliever enters with the home club's win probability at 62.0 and leaves it at 71.5 two innings later: +0.095 wins to the home club's pitching-change column, whoever else contributed inside the window.

entries.definition: A decision's realized value minus what the league realized from the same spot: the realized mWPA of the window less the league mean realized value over every window of the same shape from the matched state (season, inning bucket, half, outs, bases, score bucket). Removes the level of the state, not player quality and not selection, so it is still descriptive and still not skill.
entries.methodology: The bunt recipe generalised. baseline_f(S) is the league mean window mWPA over every window from state S, decision or not (every stint start for the pitching change, every plate appearance for the pinch hit, every half-inning remainder with a runner on for the pinch runner, every two-plate-appearance span for the intentional walk), MIN_CELL 25 with thin cells published as excluded. DVS(d) = mWPA(d) - baseline_f(S(d)). Selection caveat: intentional walks are given to the hitters a manager least wants to face and pinch hitters replace the batters he least wants at the plate, so the state-matched mean is measured over a different population and the bias is stated, not solved. For single-plate-appearance families the baseline sits near zero, so DVS there is not an independent second number. DVS lives on the per-decision drill-down and the League census only, never on a club-season or manager row: a sortable per-club column of value above state would be the rank the frozen gate withheld. A steal carries no DVS: its realized value is the steal itself on the house win expectancy table, not a feed window, and its value above holding is its DV.
entries.formula: DVS(d) = mWPA(d) - mean over league windows from S(d) of mWPA(window)

entries.definition: The success rate at which attempting a steal and holding the runner are worth the same win probability from a given base-out-score state. Above it, running pays; below it, holding does. Three are published per target base: the mean, the median and the swing-weighted break-even, and only the swing-weighted one predicts the sign of the league's summed decision value.
entries.methodology: p* = (WE[hold] - WE[caught]) / (WE[success] - WE[caught]) from the win-expectancy model, with the third out priced off the measured half-inning-start table. The swing-weighted break-even weights each attempt's p* by its swing (WE[success] - WE[caught]), which is why the league's summed decision value is positive exactly when the league success rate beats it. Two-out attempts are excluded because the caught case crosses the half-inning boundary where two estimators meet.
entries.formula: p* = (WE_hold - WE_fail) / (WE_success - WE_fail)

entries.definition: The probability the batting team wins the game from a given state (inning, half, score difference, outs, bases). Every break-even and decision value on the In-Game Management page is a difference of two win expectancies.
entries.methodology: eephus.io fits its own model (win_expectancy.py) on the play corpus rather than reading a cell table: the base-out state enters only through run expectancy with a positive coefficient, so the model is monotone by construction and safe to difference; the half-inning boundary is read from a measured half-inning-start table because a smooth model is free to be discontinuous across a boundary it was never constrained at. Smoothing costs the ninth-inning tails and the page says so. The MLB StatsAPI feed ships its own win probability on every play (wp_home_before, wp_home_after in percentage points); the realized figures on the page come from that feed, the priced figures from the model, and the two are never averaged.
entries.origin: Industry concept. Win expectancy tables from the win-probability framework (Tom Tango and coauthors, The Book); the model here is fitted in-house on the play corpus.

entries.definition: The average number of runs scored from a base-out state to the end of the half-inning: the 24-cell matrix (eight base states by three out states). Bases empty with nobody out is worth about half a run; bases loaded with nobody out more than two.
entries.methodology: Measured on the play corpus per season and published with the sample size behind every cell. It is the only channel through which the base-out state reaches the win model, which is what makes the model monotone and its differences safe. The matrix ships on the Run Expectancy tab because it needs no gate.
entries.origin: Industry concept. The run-expectancy matrix (Tom Tango and coauthors, The Book), measured here on the eephus.io play corpus.

entries.definition: Style z-score, not an index, not skill: the z of a club-season's median starter pitch count at removal across the thirty club-seasons of its season. A NEGATIVE z is an earlier hook. Sign as measured, no ladder, no plus sign; a hook has no good direction on its own.
entries.methodology: The starter hook is the first pitching change for a fielding side in a game; the removed pitcher's pitch count is the count of pitches over the plate appearances he pitched (derived, because the events table names the lineup-slot occupant rather than the pitcher on a double switch). Median per club-season, then a population z across the season's clubs, mean zero and sd one by construction. Repeats because it is policy.

entries.definition: Style z-score, not an index, not skill: the z of pitching changes per game across the thirty club-seasons of its season. Sign as measured, no ladder, no plus sign; more changes is not better.
entries.methodology: Pitching changes (events.pitching_substitution) divided by the club-season's games, then a population z across the season's clubs. Descriptive; it repeats because bullpen usage is policy.

entries.definition: Style z-score, not an index, not skill: the z of pinch hitters plus pinch runners per game across the thirty club-seasons of its season. Sign as measured, no ladder, no plus sign.
entries.methodology: Offensive substitutions with position code 11 (pinch hitter) and 12 (pinch runner) divided by the club-season's games, then a population z across the season's clubs. Descriptive; it repeats because bench usage is policy.

entries.definition: Style z-score, not an index, not skill: the z of intentional walks per game across the thirty club-seasons of its season. Sign as measured, no ladder, no plus sign; an intentional walk has no good direction as a frequency.
entries.methodology: Plays with event type intent_walk credited to the fielding club, divided by the club-season's games, then a population z across the season's clubs. Descriptive; it repeats because it is policy.

entries.definition: Style z-score, not an index, not skill: the z of mound visits per game across the thirty club-seasons of its season. Sign as measured, no ladder, no plus sign. Mound visits are counted and never valued.
entries.methodology: Events of type mound_visit credited to the fielding club of the half, divided by the club-season's games, then a population z across the season's clubs. Descriptive; it repeats because it is policy.

entries.term: LI at decision (mean leverage at decision)
entries.definition: The mean Leverage Index of the plate appearance at which a club's decisions were made, across every family, on the MLB feed's scale (1.0 is average). A number on its own scale: a cut and a style axis, never a weight in the value column.
entries.methodology: leverage_index of the plays row at the decision point (null on the leadoff plate appearance of every game, carried as null and never as zero). Leverage is never multiplied into realized value: a high-leverage state already moves win probability more by itself, so weighting by it would count leverage twice.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Leverage Index (Tom Tango), read from the MLB StatsAPI win-probability feed; the decision-point cut is eephus.io's.

entries.term: Manager agent (club-season until the ledger lands)
entries.definition: The agent is the club-season until the manager ledger lands; a club that changed managers during a season is one row here and two in reality. There is no manager entity anywhere on disk, so no row on the In-Game Management page is a manager.
entries.methodology: Every decision is attributed to a club through the play corpus's club-of-record map (mgmt_teams.build_map, validated at 0.99+ against the 2026 truth): offensive decisions to the batting club, pitching and defensive decisions to the fielding club. The manager entity needs the StatsAPI coaches endpoint per team-season with schedule-date bisection (a network ingest, plan lane M-MWAR-2); the ejection rows that name a manager with an mlbam id are that ingest's validation fixture, not a source. A team-season is an UPPER BOUND on a manager: managers change and teams do not, so a null at the club-season level decides the manager question too.

entries.definition: A club's payroll as the competitive balance tax counts it: the average annual value of every contract on the 40-man roster plus benefits, the basis the threshold is measured against.
entries.methodology: Read from Spotrac's tax page into storage.fa_team_payroll (tax_payroll_usd) and served by ledger_export.py; the Club Ledger prints it beside the season's threshold from data/cba_rules.json and never mixes it with the cash allocation basis.
entries.origin: 2022 MLB collective bargaining agreement; Spotrac's payroll tables

entries.definition: A club's cash payroll for a season as Spotrac allocates it, active plus injured plus retained plus buried, which differs from the CBT basis because it counts cash paid rather than average annual value.
entries.methodology: storage.fa_team_payroll total_payroll_usd and the four-way split where Spotrac's page carries it (2027 only today); ledger_export.py serves the split for 2027 and says the 2026 page has none.
entries.origin: 2022 MLB collective bargaining agreement; Spotrac's payroll tables

entries.definition: Which band of the competitive balance tax a club's tax payroll falls in: under the threshold, the base band, or the first, second or third surcharge band at fixed dollar offsets above the threshold.
entries.methodology: The offsets and the threshold come from data/cba_rules.json through fa_cba; ledger_export.py names the band from the club's Spotrac tax payroll and prints the 2027 band on both the platform carry-forward basis and Spotrac's basis.
entries.origin: 2022 MLB collective bargaining agreement; Spotrac's payroll tables

entries.definition: The tax a club would owe under the published schedule, computed here from its Spotrac tax payroll, its payor tier and the rate table, and printed beside Spotrac's own estimate where one exists.
entries.methodology: ledger_export.computed_cbt_bill applies the base rate for the payor year and the surcharge rates by band, all read from data/cba_rules.json; a rule application, not a forecast, and never the actual bill paid, which no source carries.
entries.formula: bill = base x min(over, t1) + (base + s1) x clip(over - t1, 0, t2 - t1) + (base + s2) x clip(over - t2, 0, t3 - t2) + (base + s3) x max(over - t3, 0)

entries.definition: How many consecutive seasons a club has paid the competitive balance tax, which sets its base rate: non-payor, first time, second time, or third time and beyond.
entries.methodology: Spotrac's payor status per season in storage.fa_team_payroll; for 2027 the Club Ledger serves Spotrac's token where the page carries one and derives the next step from the 2026 status only where it is blank, labelling which.
entries.origin: 2022 MLB collective bargaining agreement; Spotrac's payroll tables

entries.definition: Salary a club still owes to players it has released or bought out, counted against its payroll though nobody is on the roster for it.
entries.methodology: Spotrac's dead-money table on each club page; the Club Ledger block is dark until the read side tags rows with their table id, so the priced contract set cannot widen by accident.
entries.origin: 2022 MLB collective bargaining agreement; Spotrac's payroll tables

entries.definition: Money a club keeps paying on a contract it traded away, which sits on the paying club's books and is never folded into the employing club's average annual value.
entries.methodology: Spotrac's retained table per club page; the Club Ledger serves the 2027 club total from the allocation split as a cross-check and keeps the per-player block dark until the table id tag lands.
entries.origin: 2022 MLB collective bargaining agreement; Spotrac's payroll tables

entries.definition: The season's salary total across a club's contracts that Spotrac has on file, the one segment of the commitments timeline that is a record rather than a projection.
entries.methodology: Summed by ledger_export.py from mlb_projections.json salPath cells whose source is contract; printed beside projected arbitration steps and pre-arbitration minimums as three labelled segments that no key sums into a payroll.

entries.definition: The sum of a club's arbitration ladder steps for a season: projected arbitration awards plus pre-arb seasons at the league minimum, for every player on the club's ladder. Not a payroll forecast: it assumes every player is tendered; a non-tender lowers the figure, and extensions are absent.
entries.methodology: ledger_export.py and franchise_export.py sum the 2027 ladder step of every data/arbitration.json row for the club, pre-arb rungs included; the /arbitration/ Team View shows the arbitration and pre-arb parts in separate columns. The arb_award model is provisional and every 2027 step is a CBA carry-forward, both of which the cell says.

entries.definition: The first season in which a club's contract dollars on file fall below half of its current season's figure, a plain reading of when today's commitments roll off.
entries.methodology: Derived by ledger_export.py from the commitments timeline's contract segment only; arbitration steps and minimums are not part of it, and a club that never crosses the half-line within the horizon prints beyond it.

entries.definition: Descriptive, not a model: next season's projected wins above replacement, less the projected WAR of the club's locked free agents, per million dollars of three cost parts printed beside it (guaranteed salaries, the platform's projected arbitration awards and the pre-arbitration minimum rungs), indexed so that 100 is the league mean and each 10 points is one standard deviation across the thirty clubs.
entries.methodology: ledger_export.py takes team_outlook 2027 WAR, subtracts the 2027 WAR (champion mean) of every fa_class member whose status is locked, from the club the projection rolls him into, and divides by the sum of three parts in millions: guaranteed 2027 salaries (Spotrac's 2027 tax payroll, or the club's own guaranteed contract AAV where that is larger), the club's projected 2027 arbitration rungs from data/arbitration.json and its pre-arbitration minimum rungs from the same ladders. A rung for a player whose 2027 salary is already a contract on file is left out, since the guaranteed part carries him. It standardises the ratio across the 30 clubs and rounds to the nearest point. The three parts are printed apart and never added into a payroll figure; the numerator is a provisional projection, the index carries no registry row because it predicts nothing, and any efficiency skill claim would need an eval first. The ledger prints the index's rank correlation with the summed cost and with the numerator, measured each build, beside it.
entries.formula: Cost+ = 100 + 10 x z((projected WAR - locked free agents' WAR) / ((guaranteed + arbitration + pre-arb minimums) in $M))

entries.definition: The expected value of a club's controlled talent above what it is paid, in millions: the MLB leg from the projections' contract surplus plus the farm leg from the org's active prospect surplus, both sums of means.
entries.methodology: ledger_export.py converts each vet's surNpv from mlb_projections.json to millions, adds the org_summary active surplus from timeseries.json, and prints the total plain: the surplus ladder was cut on player rows and a club total would paint every club elite. Quantiles are never summed.

entries.definition: A club's international bonus pool inferred from the pool percentages Spotrac attaches to its signings, since the published allocations are not on file anywhere in the tree.
entries.methodology: For each signing in data/ifa_timeseries.json carrying both a bonus and a pool percentage, bonus divided by the percentage gives an implied pool; ledger_export.py serves the median with the count of signings behind it and labels it as implied.

entries.definition: The expected wins above replacement over the first six seasons of a draft pick at a given slot, read off the realized slot curve, used here for a club's projected first-round pick.
entries.methodology: data/draft_slot_curve.json fitted_first6_by_bucket (validated) at the bucket holding the projected slot from the latest lottery snapshot; not lottery-weighted because the snapshot carries only the odds of pick one and of a top-six pick, and not priced in dollars.

entries.definition: What a club's free agent contracts have returned so far, valued at each elapsed season's dollars per win, beside what has been paid to date: realized value, not a measure of how well the club chose.
entries.methodology: Each archived signing carries WAR to date, paid to date and surplus to date. Realized WAR is the displayed eWAR, valued at each elapsed season's dollars per win; paid to date is the deferral-adjusted guarantee prorated over the elapsed years. The ledger is rebuilt once a year after the regular season. The Club Ledger sums the rows by signing club and winter with a coverage count. The counterfactual, what the same dollars would have bought elsewhere, is not observed, so no club is ranked by it.

entries.definition: Retired 2026 by owner answer FS-Q4: F-SCORE (franchise_score) replaced the Franchise Index as the root score on /franchise/, and the Index is no longer served. What it was: A descriptive rank of a club's realized standing plus one provisional projection: the weighted mean of the ROSTER, OUTLOOK and FARM branch scores, re-standardised to 100 + 10z across the 30 clubs.
entries.methodology: franchise_export.py: branch scores (100 + 10z of team eWAR, projected 2027 wins and the PROSPX farm composite) are combined at ROSTER 0.40 / OUTLOOK 0.30 / FARM 0.30, and the weighted mean is re-standardised by the same formula before any rank or letter is taken, because a weighted mean of z-scores has sd below 10 unless the branches are perfectly correlated. Letters follow rank (storage._letter_grade) and print in neutral ink; only the score takes the z ladder. Thirty percent rests on the provisional team_win_projections row. Retired 2026 by owner answer FS-Q4 (2026-10-01): its three branches count inside F-SCORE, ROSTER and OUTLOOK in STRENGTH and FARM in PIPELINE; the method above is kept as the record.
entries.formula: index = 100 + 10 * (w - mean(w)) / sd(w), w = 0.40 * roster + 0.30 * outlook + 0.30 * farm
entries.origin: original to eephus.io (Franchise, franchise_export.py); registry row franchise_index, unvalidated (descriptive); retired 2026 by owner answer FS-Q4 (the registry row is now deprecated), replaced by F-SCORE (franchise_score)

entries.definition: A descriptive score of each club over the last seven seasons and today: what it won (regular-season wins, division titles, postseason rounds, titles), how strong it was and is (run differential, the current roster, projected 2027 wins), what is coming (the farm and its development) and what its payroll bought. 100 is the league average and 10 points is one standard deviation across the 30 clubs. Not a forecast.
entries.methodology: fscore_export.py. RESULTS: each season a club earns its wins above .500, plus 8 wins for a division title and 8 for each postseason step reached (a berth 8, the division series or a bye 16, the LCS 24, the World Series 32, a title 40), centred on the season's league average. STRENGTH: run differential per 162 games over the same seasons (half), the Franchise ROSTER score of team WAR on the current roster (three tenths; its WAR label is the one the served provider stamp names, payload copy.roster_leg) and projected 2027 wins (a fifth, a provisional projection). PIPELINE: the PROSPX farm composite (six tenths) and 7yDvM+ (four tenths). OPERATIONS: wins above replacement per million dollars of payroll above a minimum roster, ranked within each season. The seasons are averaged with a three-season half-life; 2020 counts as played, 60 games. Each pillar is standardised across the 30 clubs, weighted RESULTS 50, STRENGTH 25, PIPELINE 20, OPERATIONS 5, and the weighted mean is re-standardised before any rank or letter is taken. In-game management is shown and not scored: the one decision family the site has gated, the running game, did not repeat between halves of a club's own season (per-agent decision value).
entries.formula: F-SCORE = 100 + 10 * (s - mean(s)) / sd(s), s = 0.50 RESULTS + 0.25 STRENGTH + 0.20 PIPELINE + 0.05 OPERATIONS, each pillar a z across the 30 clubs
entries.origin: original to eephus.io (Franchise, fscore_export.py); registry row franchise_score, provisional (descriptive)

entries.definition: How F-SCORE counts October: each step a club reaches is worth a stated number of regular-season wins. A berth 8, the division series or a bye 16, the LCS 24, the World Series 32, a title 40; a division title adds 8.
entries.methodology: Read from the StatsAPI postseason series by season, joined by team id. A bye counts as reaching the division series. The values are a published choice, not an estimate: no scale was fitted. Steps not yet played count nothing until they are.
entries.formula: ladder(step) = 8 * step, step 0 missed to 5 title; division title + 8
entries.origin: original to eephus.io (fscore_export.LADDER, owner answer FS-Q1 of 2026-10-01)

entries.definition: Wins above a replacement-level club per million dollars of payroll above a minimum roster, in the season the money was spent. Realized, not a forecast; the forward-looking ratio is Cost+ on the Club Ledger.
entries.methodology: Payroll is Spotrac's total payroll allocations for the season (prorated to 60 games in 2020, and the floor with it), read from the cached pages only; the floor is 26 league-minimum salaries; replacement is 47.7 wins per 162 games (the Team Outlook league accounting). Ranked within each season and read as a normal score, because the ratio is skewed: a club a few million above the floor would otherwise dominate its season.
entries.formula: eff = (W - 0.2944 * G) / ((payroll - 26 * league minimum) in $M), then Phi^-1(rank / 31) within the season

entries.definition: One served value re-expressed as 100 + 10z across the 30 clubs: team eWAR on the current roster (ROSTER), projected 2027 wins (OUTLOOK, a provisional projection) and the PROSPX farm composite (FARM, whose letter and rank pass through from PROSPX unchanged).
entries.methodology: franchise_export._score_100: population sd over the 30 served values, one decimal, None stays None. The FARM score is re-standardised because farm_score measures sd 6.36 across the 30 and would tier at two thirds of the z ladder if passed through raw. Nine further branches are descriptive nameplates with no score, letter or weight.
entries.formula: score = 100 + 10 * (v - mean(v)) / sd(v) over the 30 clubs
entries.origin: original to eephus.io (Franchise, franchise_export.py); registry row franchise_branch_score, unvalidated (descriptive)

entries.definition: A club's wins and losses in the season, with games played, run differential and division rank as the standings carry them.
entries.methodology: Read from the cached StatsAPI standings, joined by team id (stable across relocations) for 2000 to 2026; the Franchises page prints it as a descriptive section and grades nothing on it.

entries.definition: The share of a club's projected 2027 to 2031 core WAR that is under club control (signed, arbitration or pre-arbitration seasons), a share of a projection rather than a measurement.
entries.methodology: mlb_projections.team_outlook.lockedPct (proj_export): controlled WAR over the five-season horizon divided by the full projected WAR of the same players; team_win_projections is provisional and the share inherits that.
entries.origin: original to eephus.io (MLB Projections Team Outlook, proj_export.py)

entries.definition: A 100 + 10z index of how a bullpen's best relievers are deployed into leverage, a deployment fact about the manager's usage and not a measure of reliever skill.
entries.methodology: bullpen_export: relief-entry-weighted gmLI of the pen's high-leverage core across the 30 clubs, anchored 100 + 10z; the Franchises page labels it deployment index, not skill (registry row leverage_consistency, provisional) and never folds it into a grade.
entries.origin: original to eephus.io (MLB Stats bullpen leaderboards, bullpen_export.py)

entries.definition: The gap between a club's competitive balance tax payroll and the threshold it is measured against; negative when the club sits over the line. A capacity fact, never coloured on a ladder.
entries.methodology: Spotrac's 2027 page computes space against a 247M basis while the platform's cba_rules carry 244M forward as explicitly unknown; the Club Ledger and the Franchises page print both, each labelled with its basis, and never mix them. Where Spotrac's 2027 tax payroll sits below the AAV of the club's own guaranteed 2027 contract rows, that AAV stands in for it and the cell is flagged.

entries.definition: How much a ballpark inflates or deflates a statistic relative to a neutral park, indexed at 100: a runs factor of 110 means ten percent more runs than average in that park.
entries.methodology: fa_meta.park_factors from Baseball Savant's statcast park factors, default three-season view (wOBA, HR, runs), with a rolling two-season row for a venue the default view drops (Sutter Health Park) flagged as a short window. Printed plain on the Franchises page and never tiered: a hitter's park is not better.
entries.origin: Baseball Savant statcast park factors (MLB Advanced Media)

entries.definition: The winning percentage a club's runs scored and allowed imply, which tracks true talent more closely than the actual record over a season.
entries.methodology: mlb_projections.team_outlook.current.pythagPct, computed in proj_export from the season's runs scored and allowed and blended with the actual record and a talent prior under the current overlay; the Franchises page prints it beside the actual percentage under the label current overlay, blended.
entries.formula: RS^e / (RS^e + RA^e), e near 1.83

entries.definition: An expected value: the eFV expected surplus of an active prospect, in millions, on the clemens_2026 valuation set over the prospect's own seven-season window, priced through the platform's calibrated engine (prospect_surplus, validated). It is the mean of a distribution whose 10th and 90th percentiles print on the row; net of the signing bonus it is what the club roll-up sums.
entries.methodology: It is not a trade price (the Trade Machine re-anchors debuted players and adds a roster crunch), not a quantile, and not a realized figure: no farm dollar has been earned. The MLB Projections board prints this same eFV surplus, the figure the trade board serves, for the prospects it carries and does not reprice them. Quantiles on the rows are never summed, and a row's number is never added to a number on another basis. The Club Ledger farm rows carry the trade board's trade_value_mm, equal to the eFV export's surplus_mm, and reconcile to the PROSPX fin_active_surplus leaf to a stated tolerance with both artifacts' stamps printed.
entries.formula: net_mm = eFV expected surplus ($M) - signing bonus ($M); the leaf sums net_mm over active prospects

entries.definition: The PROSPX pricing of a graduate after his debut: a trade value in millions, the value realized so far (realized_mm) and the remaining club-control years, served on the debuted rows of the prospect tracker and repeated on the Club Ledger graduates block.
entries.methodology: Two engines price a graduate and the ledger prints both under their own names: debuted_player_value (the PROSPX debuted rows) and the trade board's posterior (bayes_trade_value, surplus_source named per row). They are never averaged or summed. debuted_player_value carries no registry row of its own; its parent prospect_surplus is validated, so the debuted column reads as a served number without its own eval. The realized figure is value delivered, not skill: the counterfactual is not observed. The remaining club-control years are the seven-season valuation window less the player's MLB service time, counted from the transaction history with the CBA day count (registry row service_time, provisional); a graduate with no control year left carries no remaining value.

entries.definition: The low and high figures beside every projected arbitration award on the Club Ledger ladder: a fixed spread around the projection set from the champion's observed error by arbitration step, deliberately not published as a calibrated interval and never a P10 or P90.
entries.methodology: arb_export.py widens the band by a constant per rung so a later rung carries a wider spread than the first; no per-rung residual quantiles, comps, filing figures or hearing outcomes exist on any served row, and the ledger says so beside the ladder. The band prints per row and enters no sum; the by-season split sums projections only.
entries.formula: lo, hi = projection x (1 -/+ (base spread + step increment x (step - 1))), constants in arb_export.py

entries.definition: The signing bonus on file, the only dollar cost the site carries per prospect. The farm roll-up nets it from eFV expected surplus in full, not amortized, and the Club Ledger prints the count of rows with no bonus on file beside every cost figure.
entries.methodology: Draft rows carry the bonus and, where the pick is on the draft results table, its slot value joined on draft year and overall pick, never on name; international signings carry the bonus where the pipeline captured it and count a cost of zero where it did not, which is why the ratio of net surplus to cost basis is printed with its coverage. The trade channel has no dollar cost basis and none is invented: what a trade cost is the value given up, which the Trade Machine prices.

entries.definition: Model probability minus the de-vigged market probability for the same side of the same bet. A +6% edge means the model gives the side six points more chance than the market does once the book's cut is removed. It is a disagreement, not a profit: the model has to be right about the disagreement for it to be worth anything.
entries.methodology: Both terms must describe the SAME wager. Books do not all post the same runline or total, so the line is chosen first by book count and prices are shopped only among the books posting it. Pairing one book's line with another book's price for the opposite side once produced a fabricated edge on this site, which is why the pairing is enforced in code and pinned by a test.

entries.definition: The book's cut, built into the price rather than charged as a fee. Both sides of a coin flip are priced around -110, so the two implied probabilities add to about 105% instead of 100%; that extra 5 points is the vig, also called the hold or the overround.
The price with the book's margin removed: the market's implied probability. This site uses the proportional method: divide each side's implied probability by their sum so the pair adds to 100%.
entries.methodology: The de-vig is always taken from ONE book's two-sided market. Mixing the best price on one side with a different book's price on the other manufactures a fair line with a negative hold, which is a number no market ever offered. The payload names the book each fair line came from for exactly this reason.

entries.definition: The price that would exactly match a probability with no cut taken. A 60% chance is a fair line of -150. Two different fair lines appear on the betting board: the model's, from its own probability, and the market's, from the de-vigged book prices.

The win rate a price needs just to break even. -150 implies 60%, +150 implies 40%. Because the vig is inside the price, the implied probabilities of two opposite sides always sum to more than 100%, which is why they are de-vigged before anything is compared to them.

Expected profit on a one-unit bet under the MODEL's probability: p times the profit if it wins, minus (1 - p) times the unit if it loses. +0.20 means the model expects to make a fifth of a unit per bet on average over many repetitions of the same wager.
entries.methodology: EV is probability times payout, and payout dominates. Ranking a board by EV alone therefore selects the longest price on it almost every time, which is why the headline Pick of the Day is chosen on model probability inside a normal price band and long prices are judged on EV in their own slot. On a whole-number total the EV is scaled by the share of games that do not push. An EV computed from an unvalidated model is an expectation under an assumption, not a forecast.

entries.definition: One bet's worth of bankroll, whatever size a reader chooses. Results are reported in units so they mean the same thing at any bankroll. Every pick on this site's public record is recorded at a flat 1 unit.
entries.methodology: The stake is flat on the record on purpose. A record kept in variable stakes cannot be audited from its own rows: a reader has to take it on trust that the sizing was decided before the result and not after it. A pick card may show a different suggested size, but the RECORDED stake never changes.

entries.origin: John L. Kelly Jr. (1956), the Kelly criterion.
entries.definition: The stake fraction that maximizes long-run bankroll growth given a probability and a price. This site shows it as INFORMATION and never as a stake, and it shows a quarter of it.
entries.methodology: Full Kelly is only optimal if the probability is right. It is very sensitive to overestimating an edge, and an unvalidated model is by definition a model whose edge estimate has not been checked, so a full-Kelly stake on one of these picks is a fast way to lose a bankroll. Quarter Kelly is served pre-divided so nobody has to do the arithmetic under the impression the site endorsed the larger number.

entries.definition: A bet on which team wins the game, with no margin attached. Priced in American odds: -150 means risk 150 to win 100, +150 means risk 100 to win 150.
Baseball's spread, almost always 1.5 runs. The favourite at -1.5 has to win by two or more; the underdog at +1.5 wins the bet by losing by one or winning outright.
entries.methodology: Runline probabilities on this site come from a Poisson-difference margin model, which puts too little weight in the tails: baseball scores in clumps, so the real margin distribution is wider than the model assumes. A one-parameter dispersion correction has a pre-registered gate and is served only if it passes; until then a published runline pick carries the caveat on its row. Games the model leaves tied after nine are split between the two sides at the measured extra-innings home rate.

entries.definition: A bet on the combined runs scored by both teams, over or under a posted number. A total that lands exactly on a whole-number line is a push and returns the stake.
entries.methodology: Totals carry the same Poisson underdispersion as the runline, and the same caveat rides any published total pick. Over 8.5 at one book and Under 9.5 at another are not two sides of one bet, so a total is priced only across books posting the same number.

entries.definition: One bet chaining several legs, all of which must win. The payout multiplies, and so does the book's cut: a parlay compounds the vig on every leg.
entries.methodology: Multiplying leg probabilities is only valid when the legs are INDEPENDENT, and legs from the same game never are. The parlay builder blocks a moneyline and a runline on the same team (one bet with two prices) and prints a warning beside the other correlated combinations it knows: legs from the same game, a moneyline with that game's total, two props from one lineup, and a starter's strikeout prop with his team's moneyline.

entries.definition: Whether a bet's price when posted beat the same bet's price at the moment the game started. Beating the close means the market moved toward the pick after it was posted.
entries.methodology: This site stopped serving CLV on 2026-09-07 (owner decision). The record is graded on realized results, and the CLV panels say they are retired rather than printing an empty grade.

entries.definition: A published pick from a model that has NOT cleared its validation gates. No minimum edge has been measured yet, so the pick cleared the policy floor instead, and the card says so.
entries.methodology: The alternative was showing nothing for a season, and the owner chose to publish with the label instead. Every provisional pick carries the flag, the floor it cleared and the basis of that floor in the payload itself, so a row lifted out of the page is still self-describing. The Validation tab shows which gates are shut and how far each clock has run. Every game behind the model's evidence is a regular-season game. Postseason games are priced by owner decision of 2026-10-01, although the model has never been fitted or graded on one: each postseason card, selection and record row says 'never graded on a postseason game', and the record reports those rows as a postseason sub-ledger beside the regular-season record, never inside it.

entries.definition: During the postseason, each playoff club's chance to win its current series, reach the League Championship Series, win the pennant and win the World Series, computed from the posted bracket and every game already played. Labelled implied, no market: no book price sits beside it and none is derived from it.
entries.methodology: Each remaining series is walked game by game in its real format (best of 3, 5 or 7, with the posted home field), so the result is exact rather than sampled and carries no simulation interval. A game the betting board prices uses the board's own home-win probability, unchanged; every other game uses a results-only Elo rating (base 1500, K 4, a 24-point home edge) walked over the 2026 regular season and frozen on the simulator's first day, so a postseason result never moves a rating. Both inputs were built on regular-season games only, and neither has been graded on a postseason game. The Futures board and the Franchises page show the day's frozen entry with its date; the division, playoff and bye columns stay with the season simulator. Every day's entry is kept in a chain-hashed forward record, and nothing in it is scored until one read after the World Series, under rules registered on 2026-10-01 before the first number existed.

entries.definition: The edge a side must clear before it can be published while the model is unvalidated. It is a POLICY, set well above anything the model's measured skill supports, and it is NOT a measurement. Each pick card prints the value it cleared.
entries.methodology: Requiring a large edge means a pick appears only when the model disagrees with the market by far more than the skill there is evidence for, so the failure mode is publishing nothing on most slates rather than something weak on all of them. Every slot on the page reads this same floor. When the validation gates open, a measured threshold replaces it automatically.

entries.origin: Glenn W. Brier (1950), verification of probability forecasts.
entries.definition: The standard accuracy score for probability forecasts: the mean squared error between the stated probability and the outcome (1 or 0). Lower is better, and it rewards being confident only when confidence is warranted.
entries.methodology: A Brier score means nothing without a baseline scored on the same games, which is what the benchmark ladder provides. It also means nothing if the model saw the games it is being scored on, which is why every graded block on the betting page is labelled with the mode that produced it.

entries.definition: Forecasts binned by stated probability; each bin's mean probability against its win rate. A calibrated model sits on the diagonal: its 60% calls win about 60% of the time.
entries.methodology: The Validation tab draws it from the calibration ledger, beside the bin table it is built from. It is a diagnostic only: no calibration correction is applied to the probabilities the page serves.

entries.definition: A one-parameter widening of the Poisson-difference margin model, which puts too little weight on lopsided scores. It would move runline and total prices, not the moneyline.
entries.methodology: The correction was fitted and registered against a held-out gate before it was scored. The page reads the gate's verdict from the eval artifact: while the correction is not served, a runline or total price is the plain Poisson difference and the pick row says so. The alpha grid is on the Validation tab.

entries.definition: Paper bets the model would have made under each candidate selection rule, recorded at board prices and settled against the result. None of them is a published pick, and none counts toward the public record.
entries.methodology: Each selection rule keeps its own tag and its own ROI. Tags are never pooled, because a combined ROI measures a mixture of rules nobody bet. The settled rows feed Clock B on the Validation tab.

entries.definition: The counters that decide when the betting model can be called validated. Clock A counts games graded out of sample; Clock B counts settled paper bets per selection rule; Clock C is the gradable pool that caps Clock A.
entries.methodology: Clock A and Clock B open different gates and are never added together. Until the gates open, picks are provisional and publish against the policy floor.

entries.definition: The out-of-sample way the betting model is graded: every past game is priced on a dated leaderboard snapshot taken before that game, so no graded game sits inside its own inputs.
entries.methodology: A game with no earlier snapshot is skipped, not graded on today's numbers. The other mode, contaminated, prices games on season-to-date leaderboards that already contain them; it measures calibration only and cannot validate anything, and the page labels every block with the mode that produced it.

entries.definition: The model's Brier score beside simpler forecasts scored on the same vintage games: a home-field constant, a published Elo, and the de-vigged market at the open and at the close. Its place on the ladder is the plain answer to whether it knows anything the simpler forecasts do not.
entries.methodology: Every full tier is scored on one shared window of games, and the panel says so when the model sits last. A tier measured on fewer games renders apart, and a tier with no measurement prints its status instead of a number.

entries.definition: Projected fantasy points per $1,000 of salary. The projection is ours and the salary is the one you entered, so the column fills only for players you priced.
entries.methodology: Read it with the start rate: a high value on a low start rate is a cheap bench bat.

entries.definition: The projected chance a hitter is in the starting lineup, from his playing-time projection against a league plate-appearances-per-start anchor. A posted lineup card replaces it.
How much the opponent and the park move a projection for one game: the inverse of the opponent's innings-weighted pitching index (the starter's SEM+ plus the club's Bullpen+), times the park factor.
The market's expected runs for one club: the posted game total split by each side's price with the book's margin removed, from a cached odds snapshot.
entries.methodology: Shown for context. Nothing on the DFS page is priced off it: the points are our projections.

entries.definition: Share of all pitches that draw a swing and miss. Per pitch, where Whiff% is per swing.
entries.methodology: On /mlbstats/ both pitcher boards, Starters and Relievers, this season and past seasons, derive it from the Baseball Savant custom leaderboard as whiff% x swing% (whiffs per swing times swings per pitch), so a starter and a reliever are read on one count. Display only: no Arkmetric reads it.
entries.formula: SwStr% = swinging strikes / pitches x 100 (on /mlbstats/: Whiff% x Swing% / 100, from Baseball Savant)
entries.origin: Industry metric. Swinging strikes per pitch from pitch tracking; the /mlbstats/ figure is Baseball Savant's on both pitcher boards.

entries.definition: Share of plate appearances that start with a strike (called, swinging, foul or put in play). Higher is better for a pitcher.
entries.methodology: From the Baseball Savant custom leaderboard. Display only on the /mlbstats/ pitcher boards: no Arkmetric reads it.
entries.formula: F-Strike% = plate appearances whose first pitch is a strike / plate appearances x 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): first-pitch strikes per plate appearance.

entries.definition: A pitcher's average fastball speed in mph over the season.
entries.methodology:
From the Baseball Savant custom leaderboard (fastball_avg_speed). Display only on the /mlbstats/ pitcher boards: no Arkmetric reads it.

The PROSPX Leaderboards print a separate MiLB figure: the mean speed of the pitcher's most-thrown fastball type (four-seam, sinker, two-seam or cutter) in the MLB Stats API game feeds, with 20 tracked pitches needed.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): average fastball speed.
