entries.definition: Share of a hitter's batted balls with a launch angle of 8 to 32 degrees, the band where line drives and carrying fly balls live.
entries.methodology: From the Baseball Savant custom leaderboard. Display only on the /mlbstats/ Hitters board: no Arkmetric reads it.
entries.formula: Sweet spot% = batted balls at 8 to 32 degrees / batted balls x 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): batted balls in the 8 to 32 degree launch-angle band.

entries.definition: Share of a hitter's batted balls hit to his pull side.
entries.methodology: From the Baseball Savant custom leaderboard. Display only on the /mlbstats/ Hitters board: no Arkmetric reads it.
entries.formula: Pull% = batted balls to the pull side / batted balls x 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): batted balls to the pull side.

entries.definition: How many pitches in the dirt a catcher keeps in front of him against what an average catcher would, and the runs that saves.
entries.methodology: From the Baseball Savant catcher-blocking leaderboard, read by season. Blocks above average compares each scored pitch with its expected block rate; blocking runs is Savant's run value of those blocks. The pitch count beside it says how many pitches the model scored. Display only on the /mlbstats/ Defense board (Catching view): DEM+, eWAR and the team totals do not read it; framing stays FanGraphs'.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant) catcher blocking.

entries.definition: How many runners a catcher throws out against the count an average catcher would, given the runner, the pitcher and the jump, and the runs that saves.
entries.methodology: From the Baseball Savant catcher-throwing leaderboard, read by season. The attempt count beside it is the sample. Display only on the /mlbstats/ Defense board (Catching view): DEM+, eWAR and the team totals do not read it; framing stays FanGraphs'.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant) catcher throwing.

entries.definition: The runs a catcher saved or cost at C in a season by Statcast's own count: framing (called strikes on borderline pitches), blocking (pitches in the dirt kept in front) and throwing (runners thrown out), and their total.
entries.methodology: Statcast's run values as FanGraphs publishes them on the player's catcher row of its fielding leaderboard (fFRP, bFRP, tFRP and their total FRP), read by season from 2016 and carried verbatim in whole runs. The total equals the three parts within one run of rounding. Statcast blocking begins in 2018, so 2016 and 2017 show framing and throwing only. Statcast's framing number is not the FanGraphs framing column (Frm) the Fielding total carries. Shown on the /mlbstats/ Defense board (Catching view) and the player page's Defense tab as Statcast's public number: not computed, shrunk or validated here, and DEM+, eWAR and the team totals do not read it.
entries.formula: Statcast runs at C = framing + blocking + throwing, as published
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant) catcher framing, blocking and throwing run values, as FanGraphs publishes them.

entries.definition: Seconds from the pitch hitting the catcher's glove to the throw reaching the fielder at second base. Exchange is catch to release; arm strength is the throw's speed in mph.
entries.methodology: From the Baseball Savant catcher-throwing leaderboard, averaged over his throws that season. Lower pop and exchange times are better. Display only on the /mlbstats/ Defense board (Catching view): DEM+, eWAR and the team totals do not read it; framing stays FanGraphs'.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant) pop time, exchange and arm strength.

entries.definition: The minor-league Statcast line on a PROSPX hitter card: Baseball Savant's minors aggregates (xwOBA, exit velocity, hard-hit%, whiff% and a luck gap) from the parks that carry Hawk-Eye tracking, which are every AAA park and the Single-A Florida State League. The card names the level the line came from beside the season: AAA, A (FSL), or both.
entries.methodology:
Source: the Baseball Savant statcast search for the minors, regular season, one aggregate row per batter. Only tracked parks report, so the line is not a full-season line for a player who also played in an untracked league (A+, AA, the complex leagues, or a non-FSL Single-A league). The card shows each hitter's latest season with 100 or more tracked PA, from 2023 on.

The level comes from the player's MiLB season lines that season (MLB StatsAPI), keeping the lines in a tracked league: AAA in any league and A in the Florida State League only. Savant's aggregate has no level column. The rule is checked against the data: each row's Savant PA must equal the PA of those lines for nearly every row.

Luck gap = xwOBA minus wOBA. Positive means the results trail the contact quality.

The current season refreshes monthly and the card prints the last game date it covers. This display copy is separate from the copy eFV (S-XLINE) and SC+ read, which moves to the full season at the fWAR label epoch. Descriptive only; no forward claim.
entries.origin: Industry data. MLB Statcast minor-league tracking (Baseball Savant); the level label is derived here from MLB StatsAPI season lines.

entries.definition: Stolen bases: the bases a runner gains by advancing on his own during a pitch, as the official scorer credits them. A season count, not a rate.
entries.methodology: The PROSPX Leaderboards read it from the MLB Stats API season line at each level, with caught stealing (CS) carried beside it. A combined MiLB row adds the counts of the levels played.
entries.formula:
SB = stolen bases in the season line
Combined MiLB row: SB = sum over the levels played
Success rate = SB / (SB + CS)

entries.origin: Industry metric. Plate-discipline rate popularized by FanGraphs (swings at in-zone pitches).
entries.definition: Share of pitches in the strike zone that the batter swings at. For a hitter it reads how often he offers at hittable pitches; for a pitcher it is the in-zone swing rate he induces.
entries.methodology: In-zone swings divided by in-zone pitches, counted pitch by pitch from the MLB Stats API game feeds of the player's MiLB games. A pitch is in the zone when the feed labels it so. Where the feed has no zone label, a classifier trained on MLB pitches places it from its plate coordinates and the batter's zone top and bottom. Complex-league games use a model fit on that league's own called strikes and balls. The PROSPX Leaderboards need 200 pitches.
entries.formula:
Z-Swing% = in-zone swings / in-zone pitches x 100
swing = swinging strike, foul, foul tip, bunt attempt or ball in play

entries.definition: The 90th percentile of a hitter's exit velocities, in mph: the speed his hardest tenth of batted balls reaches. It rests on many balls, so one swing moves it less than it moves Max EV.
entries.methodology: Taken over every tracked batted ball in the MLB Stats API game feeds of the season at that level, with linear interpolation between the two nearest balls. The PROSPX Leaderboards need 10 batted balls.
entries.formula:
90th EV = the value at rank 0.9 x (n - 1) of the sorted exit velocities, interpolated
n = tracked batted balls

entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant) publishes max exit velocity; the MiLB figure here is read from the game feeds.
entries.definition: The hardest-hit ball of a hitter's season at the level, in mph off the bat.
entries.methodology: The single highest exit velocity among the tracked batted balls in the MLB Stats API game feeds. One swing sets it, so it tends to rise with the number of batted balls. The PROSPX Leaderboards need 5 batted balls.
entries.formula: Max EV = max(exit velocity) over tracked batted balls

entries.definition: Share of a hitter's batted balls that are fly balls, line drives or popups hit to his pull side.
entries.methodology: The denominator is every tracked batted ball, not air balls alone. The trajectory comes from the game feed's tag; a ball with no tag counts as in the air at a launch angle of 10 degrees or more. The pull side comes from the hit coordinates: 15 degrees or more toward left field for a right-handed batter, toward right field for a left-handed one. The PROSPX Leaderboards need 10 batted balls.
entries.formula: Pull-air% = pulled (fly balls + line drives + popups) / batted balls x 100

entries.origin: Industry metric. Pitch-tracking measure published by MLB Statcast; the MiLB value here is the game feed's induced vertical break.
entries.definition: Induced vertical break on a pitcher's main fastball, in inches: the vertical movement the pitch's spin creates, with gravity taken out. A higher number means the ball drops less than gravity alone would make it.
entries.methodology: The main fastball is the most-thrown of his four-seamers, sinkers, two-seamers and cutters at the level, and the value is that pitch's mean break in the MLB Stats API game feeds. Sinkers and cutters run lower than four-seamers, so the number compares best between pitchers whose main fastball is the same type. The PROSPX Leaderboards need 20 tracked pitches.
entries.formula: FB IVB = mean(induced vertical break) of the most-thrown pitch type among four-seam, sinker, two-seam and cutter

entries.definition: A PROSPX Leaderboards season line is qualified when it reaches the minor-league rate-title bar at its level that season: 2.7 plate appearances per team game for a hitter, 0.8 innings per team game for a pitcher.
entries.methodology: Team games is the median number of completed regular-season games per club at the level that season, read from the MLB Stats API schedule. A combined MiLB row sums its levels and is measured against their team games averaged by exposure: plate appearances for a hitter, outs for a pitcher.
entries.formula:
Hitter: qualified when PA >= 2.7 x team games
Pitcher: qualified when IP >= 0.8 x team games
Combined MiLB row: team games = sum(exposure x level team games) / sum(exposure), exposure = PA (hitter) or outs (pitcher)

entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. The nearest-neighbour shape follows the public TJStats (Thomas Nestico) approach of predicting batted-ball outcomes from launch speed and angle.
entries.definition: The site's estimate of expected wOBA for MiLB hitters, built from the launch speed and launch angle of each tracked batted ball. It is a different number from MLB's Statcast xwOBA and comes from a different model.
entries.methodology:
The estimator is a k-nearest-neighbour average with k = 61. Each batted ball takes its value from the 61 nearest points of a fixed grid of launch speed and angle outcomes, weighted by inverse distance. The grid scores an out at 0 and a single, double, triple and home run at their wOBA weights. It encodes public batted-ball priors, and no Statcast training data ships with it.

The mean over a hitter's batted balls is Est. xwOBAcon. At 25 or more balls a bounded profile correction lifts barrel-heavy and hard ground-ball profiles and caps soft-contact ones. Est. xwOBA then adds plate results from the level's BB% and K%: walks at 0.69, strikeouts at zero, and Est. xwOBAcon on the remaining plate appearances. Hit-by-pitch is left out because several MiLB lines lack it. The PROSPX Leaderboards need 25 batted balls.
entries.formula:
per ball: v = sum(w_i x value_i) / sum(w_i) over the 61 nearest grid points
w_i = 1 / (d_i + 0.75), d_i = ((EV - EV_i) / 4)^2 + ((LA - LA_i) / 8)^2
grid values: out 0, 1B 0.88, 2B 1.25, 3B 1.58, HR 2.03
Est. xwOBAcon = mean(v) over batted balls + profile correction (25+ balls, bounded at -0.45 and +0.08)
Est. xwOBA = 0.69 x BB rate + (1 - BB rate - K rate) x Est. xwOBAcon

entries.definition: A club's share of all the guaranteed money free agents signed for across the league, by the winter each deal was signed: realized spending, not a forecast.
entries.methodology: ledger_export.club_fa_spend_profile sums the nominal guarantees of every signing whose destination is the club in fa_archive.json, the same dollars the Club Ledger's Spend by winter table prints, and divides by the thirty clubs' total for the window (the last three winters, and every winter since 2015), so the thirty shares of a window sum to one; rank 1 is the largest outlay. Franchise MARKET prints the same figures.
entries.formula: club guarantees in the window / sum of the thirty clubs' guarantees in the window

entries.definition: How a club's free-agent signings split by the size of the guarantee: under $10M, $10M to $50M, $50M to $100M, and $100M and up, with the deals and the dollars in each.
entries.methodology: Major-league deals only, each counted in the band of its nominal guarantee in fa_archive.json (a band includes its lower edge); minor-league deals carry no guarantee and are counted apart. Served beside the FA $ share for the same two windows.

entries.definition: Of a club's own free agents who signed a major-league deal, the share who signed back with that club, over the same windows as the FA $ share.
entries.methodology: Counted from fa_archive.json: a departure is a major-league signing whose previous club is this club, and a re-signing is one whose new club is the same club. A minor-league deal is not counted either way. Descriptive, no forward claim.
entries.formula: re-signed / departed (major-league deals)

entries.definition: Baseball Prospectus's public contract sheets, one per club, listing each player's contract, its history, option and deferral terms and arbitration results. Used here as a reference to check deferred signings against the deferral ledger and, later, to backfill arbitration cases.
entries.methodology: One scripted capture of the 30 club sheets (tools/ingest_cots.py), then manual drops. The deferral check lists deferred signings on the sheets with no ledger entry. It is a coverage check only and moves no valuation. Players no longer on a club sheet are absent.

entries.definition: The share of a graduate's development that each club gets credit for. The club that signed him is credited with his value at signing (the expected WAR of his first listed grade) and every club that held him with the grade growth that happened while he was there; the shares sum to one. The farm grade's graduate leaves, the Club Ledger graduates block and the PROSPX farm page credit graduates by this share, not to the club he plays for now.
entries.methodology: His history is cut into org tenures from his dated transactions (signings, trades, waiver claims, Rule 5 moves and returns open a tenure with the receiving club; a release or an election of free agency opens an unaffiliated stretch that credits nobody), ending at his MLB debut. Growth counts only on same-source pairs (one outlet's list to its next list on him), valued on the FV-to-expected-WAR table DvM+ uses, and a pair that spans a club change is split by days. A tenure's growth is the mean over the outlets that saw it; a tenure that lowered his grade earns zero, never a negative share. It is accounting, not a causal estimate: it says where the measured grade growth happened, not what a club added.
entries.formula:
credit(c) = V0 [c = signing club] + Σ max(g(k), 0) over club c's tenures k
share(c) = credit(c) / Σ credit
V0 = W(first listed grade), g(k) = mean over outlets of Σ split pair steps W(b) - W(a), W = FV_EXPECTED_WAR
entries.example: Tarik Skubal: drafted and developed by Detroit (2018 to his 2020 debut), traded to the Dodgers in 2026. Detroit's share is 1.00; the Dodgers are his current club, not a developing club.

entries.definition: The site's Top 3 for an MLB award, chosen by a rule published on the Awards page: one metric family, one frame, one playing-time floor and one tie rule per award. Frozen after the regular season, before the writers' results. Not a forecast of the vote.
entries.methodology: Before the freeze the cards read 'Current leaders on the rule'. The freeze runs once, on the exporter's first run after the regular season's last game, into a write-once record; later changes to the site's WAR show beside the frozen value as 'Now' and never move the order. The WAR it reads is the series the site displays, named on every card.

entries.definition: The published rule behind the eephus selection for MVP: in-league eWAR, batting plus pitching, summed before rounding.
entries.methodology: Floor: in-league PA of at least 252 or IP of at least 81 in a 162-game season (1.55 PA and 0.5 IP per scheduled game). Ties: the unrounded score, then in-league WPA, then MLBAM id. A player traded across leagues is a candidate in each league with that league's share only, and both shares print on his row.

entries.definition: The published rule behind the eephus selection for the Cy Young Award: in-league pitching eWAR, which prices pitching on FIP.
entries.methodology: Floor: in-league IP of at least 41 in a 162-game season (0.25 IP per scheduled game), so relievers stay eligible. Ties: the unrounded score, then in-league IP, then SEM+ for a starter or REM+ for a reliever, then MLBAM id.

entries.definition: The published rule behind the eephus selection for Rookie of the Year: in-league eWAR, both sides, among players who pass the site's rookie test.
entries.methodology: Floor: PA of at least 100 or IP of at least 30 in the season. Rookie test: at most 130 career AB and 50 career IP through the prior season, and at most 45 estimated active days; a player removed by the days estimate alone is listed under the card with his days.

entries.definition: The published rule behind the eephus selection for Manager of the Year: the club-season's wins above the club's own earned eWAR. The agent is the club-season; manager names join when the manager ledger lands.
entries.methodology: Score: W minus (47.7 plus the club's earned eWAR) times games played over 162, with no floor, so a losing club can lead. It splits into W minus Pythagorean wins and Pythagorean wins minus the eWAR line, printed beside the score. The decision values on In-Game Management are realized value, not skill, and are never summed across families.

entries.definition: The site's test for rookie status: MLB's at-bat and innings limits from prior seasons, and an estimate of MLB's 45-day active-roster limit built from MLB's transaction log until the site measures service time.
entries.methodology: At-bats and innings come from MLB's season lines through the prior season. The days count open on a selection, purchase, recall, reinstatement or activation to an MLB club and close on an injured list placement, option, outright, designation, release, trade, waiver claim, assignment, free agency, suspension or retirement, counted only from Opening Day to September 1.

entries.definition: The writers' award ballot: 30 voters per league, two per city. MVP lists 10 places (14, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 points), Cy Young 5 (7, 4, 3, 2, 1), Rookie and Manager 3 each (5, 3, 1). Ballots are due before the postseason, so the vote covers the regular season.
entries.origin: The Baseball Writers' Association of America, which votes the four awards.

entries.definition: Where each of the three finalists stood week by week, drawn as lamps: tall for 1st, middle for 2nd, short for 3rd. Through the 2026 season it is their order among the three on realized win probability added, which is not the selection metric; from 2027 it is the place on the selection rule among every eligible player, from the site's nightly snapshots. Weeks with no record are marked, never filled in.
The three finalists on each metric's own value ruler, with the numbers beside them.
The eephus selection beside the writers' result, season by season. A record of both lists; it scores neither.
entries.methodology: Winners come from MLB's public StatsAPI awards feed. Seasons before the site published a selection are computed after the fact by the same rule from the same files and say so.

entries.definition: Your own ballot for each award, with the BBWAA places and points and the site's statistics beside every candidate. Kept in your browser only; share it as a link or an image.

entries.term: Former prospects against the grade at debut
entries.definition: Former prospects against their grade at debut: where a player's season eWAR places him in the pool beside where his eFV at debut placed him. Open to debut seasons before 2020: the site holds out the 2020 and 2021 prospect list vintages, whose players debut in 2020 or later, and the debut cohorts from 2025 for registered checks of eFV, and each opens once its check is recorded.
entries.methodology: Both places are mid-rank percentiles inside the season's pool, ties shared; the pool is players with PA of at least 300 or IP of at least 80 and an eFV at debut. One player at a time: nothing is averaged or counted by grade band. Rows at eFV 20 carry 'graded at the floor'.

entries.definition: Season WAR minus the WAR projected for the season in the projection file frozen the day before Opening Day, one player at a time, with that file's P10 to P90 band beside it. No file was saved before the 2026 season, so the card is dark for 2026; from 2027 it reads the frozen file once that season's registered checks are recorded.

The projections engine's WAR for next season minus the season's realized WAR on the same WAR series, one player at a time, naming the projections build it read. The engine's path pulls unusual seasons back toward a player's longer record, so both lists are mostly that.

The League tab's League column: every counted event in the pool is summed and run through the formula the boards use, so a league AVG is total hits over total at bats, not the mean of player averages. Beside it sit the player mean, median and standard deviation over the players with at least 100 PA or 20 IP.
entries.methodology: One row per player-season from MLB's season lines, 2000 to the live season. A traded player's season sits under his last club, which is why the tab has no club filter: Teams is the club view. AVG, OBP, ERA, K% and the other rates come back through the boards' own derivations; P/PA, P/IP and P/BF are pitches over plate appearances, innings (outs / 3) or batters faced; FIP uses the season constant from the league totals. The HEM+, SEM+, REM+ and DEM+ rows are PA-, IP- or innings-weighted means of the served per-player values, so nothing is rescored. Every number is a count or a pooled rate of what happened, not a forecast.
entries.formula: League rate = the stat's formula over the summed counts of every player in the pool

entries.definition: The Teams tab's default club basis: each player's season index weighted by the plate appearances or innings he took for each club, so a traded player counts for every club he played for, in proportion. Club today, labelled beside it, is the boards' basis: a traded player's whole season counts for the club that holds him now.
entries.methodology: Earned splits a player's season exposure (the PA, IP or fielding innings his board row carries) across his clubs by his Baseball-Reference stint rows: PA for hitters, outs for pitchers, innings for fielders. A player with one club keeps his whole weight, so the two bases differ only by who holds a traded player. It re-weights the served per-player values and scores nothing new. Club today copies the rollups the Hitters, Starters, Bullpen and Defense team tabs serve, unchanged. Past seasons show the earned basis only.
entries.formula: Earned rollup = sum(index x exposure at the club) / sum(exposure at the club)

entries.definition: MLB's published expected won-lost record over the games a club has played: the record its runs scored and allowed imply. The Teams tab prints it as MLB publishes it.
entries.methodology: Read from the StatsAPI standings' expected records (xWinLoss) through the site's one standings parser. A club whose expected wins plus losses differ from its games played is refused rather than printed.
entries.origin: MLB, the StatsAPI standings' expected records (xWinLoss).

entries.definition: Wins minus MLB's expected wins over the same games: the gap between a club's record and the record its runs imply. Printed signed and never coloured; it describes the games played and nothing else.
entries.methodology: Both terms come from the same standings read, so the gap covers exactly the games played. No fit, correlation or slope against it is computed anywhere on the tab.
entries.formula: W - xW = wins - expected wins (xW-L)

entries.definition: How a lineup's HEM+ is spread: Heart 3 is the mean HEM+ of the club's top three qualified hitters, Rest is the PA-weighted HEM+ of its other hitters, Gap is Heart 3 minus Rest, and PA at 100+ is the share of the club's plate appearances taken by hitters at HEM+ 100 or better.
entries.methodology: Same rows and club basis as Offense+ (club today), so the columns read beside it. Gap prints signed and is never coloured. Descriptive: the spread of the season's served HEM+ values, not a rating of the lineup.
entries.formula: Gap = Heart 3 - Rest; PA at 100+ = PA of hitters at HEM+ 100 or better / team PA

entries.definition: The share of a club's innings thrown in relief: the outs its relievers recorded over every out its staff recorded.
entries.methodology: Earned by the club, from MLB's reliever split of the club pitching line; the league row pools the thirty clubs the same way. A usage share, drawn without a value colour.
entries.formula: Relief IP % = relief outs / staff outs

entries.definition: The player drawer's game-by-game line for the live season: each point pools the last 15 games for a hitter, 5 starts for a starter or 10 appearances for a reliever, and a toggle doubles the window to 30, 10 or 20. A point is drawn only once its window is full, so no line opens on a one-game rate.
entries.methodology: Read from the player's own game file: raw counts per game from the play-by-play frame in first-pitch order. Each window sums the counts and computes the rate once; it never averages per-game rates. Defense and Leverage draw no rolling window, because fielding runs and per-game WPA are not in the game logs the drawer reads. Descriptive: each point is what happened over that stretch, nothing projected.
entries.formula: Window rate = the stat's formula over the counts of the last N games, starts or appearances

entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MLB Projections component lines, proj_export.py).
entries.definition: A veteran's projected runs by part on FanGraphs' WAR frame, per season: batting, baserunning, fielding, positional, league and replacement runs. Each is a mean, the average outcome, not the most likely one.
entries.methodology: Batting, league and replacement runs follow from the projection engine's PA and rate line with FanGraphs' formulas, park-neutral, with league constants held at the last completed season. Baserunning runs and fielding plus positional runs are their own heads: three-season rates shrunk toward zero by playing time, with an age term. A head is printed only after it passes its own component test on the 2022 to 2025 holdout against a naive three-season rate and the value the served engine assumes; one that does not pass reads not projected, and its runs sit in the rest of the served projection. The labels are FanGraphs' run parts from the frozen fWAR vintage; the season history on the same card stays eWAR. Each part's 80% range is built from that part's own past errors by horizon and playing-time tier. Ranges are never added up: no WAR range is built from component ranges, and the served WAR keeps its own 80% range. The parts add specificity to the projection; the served WAR itself is unchanged, and each part is judged only by its own component test (docs/PROJ_COMPONENTS_GATE.md).

entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MLB Projections component lines, proj_export.py).
entries.definition: The WAR the projected parts add up to on FanGraphs' WAR frame: for a hitter, the run parts over runs per win; for a pitcher, FIP-based WAR. A sum of means, so itself a mean.
entries.methodology: Only parts that passed their own component test enter the sum; a part that reads not projected stays out, and its runs sit in the rest of the served projection. A two-way player's line adds both sides. It carries no range of its own, because a sum of 80% ranges is not an 80% range. Ranges are never added up: no WAR range is built from component ranges, and the served WAR keeps its own 80% range. It is never fed back into the WAR projection and never trained on. The parts add specificity to the projection; the served WAR itself is unchanged, and each part is judged only by its own component test (docs/PROJ_COMPONENTS_GATE.md).

entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MLB Projections component lines, proj_export.py).
entries.definition: The served WAR minus WAR from components, per season, on FanGraphs' WAR frame: what the served projection holds that the printed parts do not. The parts plus this line equal the served WAR before rounding.
entries.methodology: The served WAR is the projection engine's own mean head; the parts are priced separately, so the two need not agree. This line carries the difference, including the runs of any part that reads not projected (for example the reliever gmLI (Leverage Index) term while it is held back, when the pitcher is priced at a gmLI of 1.0). A registered tripwire blocks the component lines if the mean of this line on the holdout rows at year 1 passes 0.30 WAR either way; the receipt reads it from the eval artifact. It is a difference of two means and carries no range. Ranges are never added up: no WAR range is built from component ranges, and the served WAR keeps its own 80% range.

entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MLB Projections component lines, proj_export.py).
entries.definition: Projected plate appearances for a hitter or innings for a pitcher, per season: the projection engine's playing-time walk, the exposure every run part on FanGraphs' WAR frame is priced at. A mean.
entries.methodology: Printed only once it passes its registered exposure test on the 2022 to 2025 holdout against the prior season's total and a 5/4/3 weighted average of the last three; until then the PA and IP lines read not projected and the board offers no PA/IP cell, while the run parts are still priced at it. Its 80% range is built from its own past errors by horizon and playing-time tier, with a floor of zero. Ranges are never added up: no WAR range is built from component ranges, and the served WAR keeps its own 80% range.

entries.definition: The ceiling on a veteran's projected playing time in any season: the 99.5th percentile of one season's plate appearances (hitters) or batters faced (pitchers) for his role. Without it, the aging curve added the league's average playing-time gain to a young regular every year, so a 22-year-old with 650 PA was walked past 800 PA by 26.
entries.methodology: The projection engine fits the cap from the same corpus as its aging curves, by side and base role (catcher and other hitters; starters and relievers), over the seasons before the projected one; it is never tuned. The year-1 projection and every later season of the aging path are clamped at it. It touches only the WAR path behind team totals, contract tails and surplus; the displayed WAR and wOBA lines, the fantasy and hitter boards and the FA Fit's team baseline do not move with it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (fa_projection.fit_pt_cap, task AG_4_CHAMPION_PT_CAP).
Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MLB Projections component lines, proj_export.py).
entries.definition: FanGraphs' pitcher WAR on its own frame, built on FIP, from a pitcher's projected FIP and innings, per season. A mean, and the pitcher's WAR from components.
entries.methodology: Projected FIP becomes runs allowed per nine against the league, park-neutral, with FanGraphs' dynamic runs per win, a replacement level set by the starter and reliever mix, and the league's WAR per inning held at the last completed season. Reliever gmLI (game-entering Leverage Index) enters only once its own head passes its component test; until then the relief share is priced at a gmLI of 1.0 and the runs gmLI adds sit in the rest of the served projection. It carries no range of its own. Ranges are never added up: no WAR range is built from component ranges, and the served WAR keeps its own 80% range. The parts add specificity to the projection; the served WAR itself is unchanged, and each part is judged only by its own component test (docs/PROJ_COMPONENTS_GATE.md).

entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MLB Projections component lines, proj_export.py).
entries.definition: A labelled second view of a pitcher on FanGraphs' WAR frame: FIP-based WAR plus a heavily shrunk share of his history of runs allowed beyond his FIP. A mean.
entries.methodology: The adjustment is the pitcher's three-season RA9 gap per 100 innings, shrunk toward zero by innings, priced at his projected innings. It is printed only once its head passes its own component test on the 2022 to 2025 holdout; until then the line reads not projected. Its 80% range, where printed, is the adjustment's own range from its own past errors. Ranges are never added up: no WAR range is built from component ranges, and the served WAR keeps its own 80% range.

entries.definition: A minor-league fielding reading in runs: how many runs a player's fielding saved or cost per 1,000 innings at a position against the average fielder at the same level and season, from MiLB play-by-play 2021 to 2026, shrunk by reliability and put on an AAA-equivalent scale. Shown on PROSPX prospect pages by position; never in a grade, rank or sort.
entries.methodology: Every ball in play gets an expected out rate from balls of the same trajectory, hardness, spray angle (5-degree bins) and distance (30-foot bins, air balls) at that level, and each position's share of the outs made in that zone. A fielder who turns a ball into an out earns the part of it his position was not expected to make; a ball that falls costs each responsible position its expected share, in runs (the gap between the zone's hits and an out). Infielders add double plays turned against the level rate, outfielders add runner kills and extra bases allowed on hits they field, and catchers add called strikes on tracked pitches (AAA 2023 on, the Florida State League) and caught stealing. Every part is zeroed within level, season and position. The total is shrunk toward zero by innings over innings plus a split-half constant per position, and lower levels are scaled to AAA by players seen at two levels in the same season. Its pre-registered gate found that pre-debut MFR ranks later MLB fielding runs (B-Ref rfield and Statcast OAA) for players who debuted 2022 to 2024; the numbers and their intervals print in the card's tooltip from the gate's eval artifact. The gate could not show that MFR adds to the scouting field grade.
entries.formula:
runs on a ball in play, position k = (1[k made the out] - p_zone x share_k) x run gap of the zone
MFR = 1,000 x sum over levels (F_level x runs) / (innings + k_pos)
reliability = innings / (innings + k_pos); bands: low under 0.35, medium under 0.60, high
entries.example: A shortstop at +4.0 over 800 innings, high reliability, saved about four runs per 1,000 innings more than an average AAA shortstop would on the same balls.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MILB_FIELDING_RUNS gate, tools/milb_fielding_runs.py), built on MLB StatsAPI play-by-play.

entries.definition: Runs a player added or cost on the bases this season against an average runner with the same chances: stealing, taking the extra base, and staying out of double plays. Counted from MLB's play-by-play on this season's run expectancy. Descriptive: what happened, not a forecast.
entries.methodology: Each chance is valued on this season's run-expectancy table (RE24), shrunk toward the pooled 2018 to 2026 table so a thin cell never swings it: what the inning was worth after what the runner did, minus what it was worth had he held. An average runner scores zero, so each part sums to zero across the league every season. SB runs cover steals, caught stealing and pickoffs, keyed on MLB's movement reason, against what an average runner made of the same times on base with the next base open. XB runs cover taking or not taking the extra base, and outs on the bases, on singles, doubles, caught air balls and ground balls, each against the league's outcomes in the same spot, out count and batted-ball context. DP runs compare double plays grounded into with the league rate for the same base-out state, priced by state. Blocked chances, advances credited to an error, wild pitches, passed balls and balks are left out. No park or fielder-arm term, which is where Baseball Savant's run value differs. Same-season agreement with FanGraphs' BsR, Baseball-Reference's baserunning runs and Savant's run value is measured and published in the eval, never a gate.
entries.formula: eBR = SB runs + XB runs + DP runs
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The stolen-base part of eBR: steals, caught stealing and pickoffs, valued on this season's run expectancy, minus what an average runner made of the same times on base with the next base open.
entries.methodology: Every attempt is priced at its own base-out state (the state after this runner's move only, so a double steal gives each runner his own value), keyed on MLB's movement reason and never on the event type. Pickoffs of a runner who was not attempting are priced the same way against the league's pickoff rate from that base. A two-out caught stealing is priced: run expectancy ends the inning at zero exactly. The league sums to zero every season.
entries.formula: SB runs = sum of attempt values minus the league value per chance times the runner's chances, by origin base
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The advancement part of eBR: taking or not taking the extra base, and outs made on the bases, on singles, doubles, caught air balls and ground balls, against an average runner in the same spot and out count.
entries.methodology: Each chance is a runner at contact in one of four classes (a runner on a single or double, the batter-runner on a hit, a runner on a caught air ball with fewer than two out, an unforced runner on a ground-ball out). His outcome is valued on a fixed reference, so a teammate's extra base is never credited to him, against the league's outcome mix for the same class, base, outs, what the runners ahead did and the batted ball (field, trajectory and depth), with thin cells backed off to broader ones. Outs on the bases are split out and published beside it. Chances blocked by the runner ahead are no chance; an advance credited to an error stops before the error.
entries.formula: XB runs = sum over chances of (value of his outcome minus the league's expected value of the chance), centred to zero by class and season
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The double-play part of eBR, the batter's: double plays grounded into against the league rate for the same chances (a runner on first, fewer than two out), priced by base-out state.
entries.methodology: A chance is a plate appearance whose state at its final pitch has a runner on first and fewer than two out. The cost of a double play in each of the eight states is the run-expectancy gap between the ground-ball outs that were not double plays and those that were, so a loaded-base, one-out double play costs more than a runner-on-first one. FanGraphs' served BsR has carried no double-play part since 2016; Baseball-Reference's double-play runs are the nearest published counterpart.
entries.formula: DP runs = minus the sum over chances of (double play minus the league rate for the state) times the state's cost
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The sum of a club's runners' eBR this season, club today as on every team tab here. Realized runs, not a grade of how a club chose to run.
entries.methodology: The roster basis (the club MLB lists today) is shown, so a traded player's whole season counts for his new club; the earned basis (every chance credited to the club he ran for) rides in the payload and sums to zero across the league every season. Club running style, the decision rather than the runner, is on In-Game Management.
entries.formula: Team eBR = sum of eBR over the club's runners
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How often a runner takes more than the minimum on a hit: first to third or home on a single, second to home on a single, first to home on a double.
entries.methodology: A chance counts only when the base ahead was open; an advance credited to a fielding error counts on neither side; an out made trying is a chance not taken. Counted here from MLB's play-by-play, so no parity with any published XBT% is claimed.
entries.formula: XBT% = extra bases taken / chances
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic; counted here from MLB's play-by-play.

entries.definition: Steal attempts per chance: plate appearances that began with him on first and second open, or on second and third open.
entries.methodology: A chance is counted at the start of a plate appearance from the pre-play state, so a runner on first with second open during a four-pitch plate appearance is one chance. Attempts of second and third from MLB's play-by-play, keyed on the movement reason.
entries.formula: Att% = (SB + CS of second and third) / chances
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic; counted here from MLB's play-by-play.

entries.definition: Outs made while advancing, stretching a hit, returning to a base or in a rundown. Caught stealing, pickoffs and force outs are not included.
entries.methodology: Counted from MLB's play-by-play movement reasons (thrown out, out stretching, out returning, doubled off, rundown, runner out); the batter-runner counts once he is a runner.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic; counted here from MLB's play-by-play.

entries.definition: Advances on a caught fly ball with fewer than two out, third to home and second to third, over the chances.
entries.methodology: Second to third is blocked, and no chance, when the runner on third held. Counted from MLB's play-by-play.
entries.formula: Tag% = advances / chances over both classes
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic; counted here from MLB's play-by-play.

entries.definition: Double plays grounded into per chance: plate appearances with a runner on first and fewer than two out.
entries.methodology: Chances from the play-by-play state at the plate appearance; double plays from the play's event type. The count on the row is the official GIDP; the rate's numerator is the play-by-play count, so no rate mixes sources.
entries.formula: GIDP% = GIDP / chances
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic; counted here from MLB's play-by-play.

entries.definition: FanGraphs' baserunning runs above average as MLB's feed publishes them. Since 2016 they are stolen-base runs (wSB) plus Statcast's extra-base runner runs; before 2016 they also included FanGraphs' UBR and double-play runs (wGDP). Displayed here, never computed.
entries.methodology: Read verbatim from MLB's bulk sabermetrics feed, joined by player id; a traded player reads one season line. The feed's separate UBR and wGDP fields are not shown: they read zero for 2025 and 2026, and from 2016 BsR is not their sum with wSB, so the board shows BsR and wSB and labels the difference as BsR minus wSB.
entries.origin: Industry metric, FanGraphs' baserunning runs as published by MLB. We display it and compute no version of it.

entries.definition: FanGraphs' stolen-base runs above average, from steals and caught stealing on linear weights, as MLB's feed publishes them. Displayed here, never computed.
entries.methodology: Read verbatim from MLB's bulk sabermetrics feed, joined by player id; a traded player reads one season line.
entries.origin: Industry metric, FanGraphs' stolen-base runs as published by MLB. We display it and compute no version of it.

entries.definition: Baseball Savant's runs above average on the bases from extra bases taken and steal attempts, from Statcast tracking. Displayed here, never computed.
entries.methodology: The runner total, its extra-base part and its steal part are read from Savant's baserunning and basestealing run-value leaderboards for the season shown. Savant's model carries fielder-arm and batted-ball context that eBR leaves out, so the two differ by design.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant) baserunning run value.

entries.definition: Runs at 30 feet per second or faster this season, as Baseball Savant counts them.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): competitive runs at 30 ft/s or faster.

entries.definition: Home to first in seconds on competitive runs, as Baseball Savant measures it. Lower is faster.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): home-to-first time.

entries.definition: Runs a prospect added or cost on the bases in one minor-league season against an average runner at the same level in the same season: stealing, taking the extra base, and staying out of double plays, counted from minor-league play-by-play. Shown on PROSPX prospect pages for each level and season at 150 or more plate appearances. Descriptive: what happened, not a forecast, and never part of a grade, rank or projection.
entries.methodology: The same five parts as eBR (steals, pickoffs, advancement and outs on the bases, double plays), priced on a run-expectancy table fitted to that level and season and shrunk toward the level's pooled table (or toward all of the minors that season where a level has one season of play-by-play on file), with every part centred to zero within the level and season. A runner is compared with the average runner of his own league-season, so the minors' rule changes (pickoff limits, bigger bases, the pitch clock) are absorbed, and the number is not comparable across levels or with MLB's eBR in runs. Advances on wild pitches and passed balls are counted beside it and are not in it. Each level-season is checked against the official season lines: league stolen bases and caught stealing within 0.033 percent and exact for 99.48 percent or more of the players who have any. One season is a noisy reading: the split-half reliability of runs at 150 plate appearances is 0.32 to 0.50 at AAA through Single-A and 0.14 to 0.37 at Rookie, and prints in each row's tooltip. On file: Single-A and Rookie 2023 to 2026, AAA, AA and High-A 2026.
entries.formula: level-relative eBR = SB runs + XB runs + DP runs, each centred to zero over every runner of the level and season

entries.definition: The Trends tab of MLB Stats. Players lists changes in a player's own measured mechanics over his recent games that clear a calibrated bar against his earlier games this season, with the number expected from game-to-game noise printed beside the list. Teams shows each club's run differential over its last 10 and 30 games with a chance band, and bullpen workload counts. League shows season-over-season cards. Descriptive: what changed, not what comes next.
entries.methodology: The families measured are fastball velocity, movement, spin and extension, pitch-family mix, reliever entry Leverage Index, and hitter bat speed, swing length and attack angle. A family is listed only when its bar meets the stated policy on a placebo of the same players' games shuffled in time, as of each date, and the fold names the families on the day's list. Results measures (wOBA, strikeout and walk rates, whiff, chase, exit velocity) did not separate real changes from chance in 2023 to 2025, so a card shows OBP or K-BB% as context only. The Teams chance band is the pooled game-to-game spread of a club's run margin over 2021 to 2025; nothing in Teams flags a club. The rotation, new-pitch and lineup events are rule-based. Whether a listed change lasts is measured apart, by one registered persistence read.

entries.definition: The bar a change must clear to be listed on League Trends: the gap between a player's recent window and his earlier games, net of the league-wide change over the same dates, in units of its game-to-game noise. The list prints how many entries noise alone would put there that day.
entries.methodology: Per family, the bar is the smallest on a grid from 2.5 to 6.0 that meets four rules, pooled over 2023 to 2025 (2024 and 2025 for swings) against a placebo of the same players' games shuffled in time. The placebo gives 0.05 or fewer false entries a day; 90 percent or more of the flags sit above the placebo; there are 20 or more flags; and every season with 5 or more flags is at least 75 percent real. The live season is a held-out check against a quasi-Poisson 99th percentile; a family above it is left off. Bars change only after a season completes. Expected false entries a day are the published per-test placebo tail times the tests run that day.
entries.formula: z = (window mean - earlier mean - league drift) / (sigma x sqrt(1/n_window + 1/n_earlier)); listed when |z / phi| >= bar and the shrunk change clears the family's size floor

entries.definition: A listed change pulled toward no change for game-to-game noise. A League Trends card prints it beside the raw change; a large real change is pulled less than a noisy one.
entries.methodology: A two-group prior per family: a share pi0 of players with no real change and a normal spread tau for the rest, fitted on completed seasons before the live one. The shrunk change is the posterior mean. For pitch mix the prior is fitted against the placebo's own largest-of-three change; when that fit is not identified, no shrunk value is printed and the card shows the raw shares only.
entries.formula: shrunk = (1 - lfdr) x change x tau^2 / (tau^2 + se^2), lfdr the chance the change is noise

entries.definition: A tracked swing that is not a check swing or a defensive poke, so bat speed and swing shape compare like with like. League Trends counts a swing as competitive at 50 mph or more and at or above the hitter's own 10th percentile of bat speed.
entries.methodology: The cut is taken as of each date from the hitter's swings on or before it, once he has 100 swings that season; before that his previous season's cut is used. Bunts are left out. The bat speed, swing length and attack angle families average a game's competitive swings.
entries.formula: competitive when bat speed >= max(50 mph, the hitter's 10th percentile of bat speed to date)
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast bat tracking (Baseball Savant), from 2024 on; read here from Savant's per-swing files.

entries.definition: The vertical movement a pitch's spin creates, in inches, with gravity taken out. A fastball with more of it drops less than gravity alone would make it.
entries.methodology: Read for every pitch from the MLB Stats API game feed. League Trends measures a pitcher's primary fastball (his most-thrown four-seamer, sinker or cutter in his earlier games) against his own earlier games; the starter and reliever induced-break families were measured and are listed only when their bar meets the policy (the 2026 calibration left both off).
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast pitch tracking, read here from the MLB Stats API game feed for every pitch.

entries.definition: The sideways movement of a pitch, in inches: how far it moves toward a pitcher's arm side or glove side on its way to the plate.
entries.methodology: Read for every pitch from the MLB Stats API game feed. League Trends compares a reliever's primary fastball over his last 6 outings with his earlier outings, so the feed's sign convention cancels and only the size of the change is read.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast pitch tracking, read here from the MLB Stats API game feed for every pitch.

entries.definition: How fast the sweet spot of the bat is moving at contact or at the point of closest approach, in mph.
entries.methodology: League Trends averages a game's competitive swings and compares a hitter's last 30 days with his earlier games this season, net of the league-wide change.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast bat tracking (Baseball Savant), from 2024 on; read here from Savant's per-swing files.

entries.definition: The total distance the head of the bat travels from the start of the swing to contact or the point of closest approach, in feet.
entries.methodology: League Trends averages a game's competitive swings and compares a hitter's last 30 days with his earlier games this season; the swing-length family is listed only when its bar meets the policy (the 2026 held-out check left it off).

entries.definition: The vertical angle of the bat's path at contact or the point of closest approach, in degrees: above zero the bat is moving upward.
entries.methodology: League Trends averages a game's competitive swings and compares a hitter's last 30 days with his earlier games this season, net of the league-wide change.

Arkmetric, original to eephus.io (MLB Projections Team Outlook, proj_export.py).
entries.definition: A club's first projected season roster, player by player, on the Team Outlook view of MLB Projections: each veteran's component runs, component WAR, served WAR and the gap line between them, footed to the club's Roster WAR. It is a breakdown of the number already printed, not a second projection.
entries.methodology: The listed players are exactly the veterans and arrived prospects the Team Outlook roll-up counts. The foot adds the served WAR of the listed veterans, the champion mean minus the served head (the roll-up sums the champion mean; quantile points are never summed) and the prospects who arrive in that season at their ETA, and shows what is left against Roster WAR; the leftover is rounding. Bat, BsR, Fld and Pos are runs above average and Pitching is FIP-based WAR in runs, on FanGraphs' WAR frame; a part that reads not projected is left blank and its runs sit in the gap line. PA and IP print only where the playing-time heads have passed their own test. It adds no new projection and carries no accuracy claim, so there is no gate to read.
